John was walking down a deserted road. It was hot outside, so he stopped to take a break and have a drink from his cooler. As he took a sip, he noticed something strange.

"What was that?" he asked.

Suddenly, an ugly monster appeared from behind a bush, scaring John. He screamed loudly and ran away.

John ran as fast as he could but he could hear the monster following him. Then, a cooler suddenly hit the monster right in the face. The monster stopped abruptly and ran away.

John was so relieved that he quickly turned around to see who had saved him. It was his friend, Jake. Jake had been walking behind him and saw the monster chasing him. He threw the cooler to scare the monster away.

John and Jake hugged each other tightly and were so thankful they were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a fish called Tuna. Tuna loved exploring and swimming around the big sea. One day, Tuna was feeling very sleepy but he wanted to go for a swim anyway. Lila did not listen to Nemo. She said, "You are just scared, Nemo. I am not afraid of anything. I want to see what is inside the trap. Maybe there is something fun or tasty. You can follow me or stay here."

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to go to the beach. They liked to play in the sand, splash in the water, and look for shells. One day, they saw a big whale on the shore. It was not moving and looked very sad.

"Look, a whale!" Tom said. "Can we touch it?"

"No, we can't," Lily said. "It is hurt and needs help. We have to find someone who can help it."

They ran to find their mom and dad, who were sitting on a blanket. They told them about the whale and asked them to come. Their mom and dad followed them to the shore, where they saw the whale.

"Oh, poor thing," their mom said. "It must have got lost and stranded by the tide. We have to call the animal rescue team. They will know what to do."

She took out her phone and called the number. Soon, a big truck and a boat arrived. The animal rescue team had a big net and a crane. They put the net around the whale and lifted it with the crane. They put the whale on the boat and took it to the water.

"Bye, whale," Tom and Lily said. "We hope you feel better and find your family."

The whale made a loud noise and waved its tail. It looked happy and grateful. It swam away into the deep water.

Tom and Lily learned that day that some animals need help when they are in trouble. They also learned that they should not touch or bother them, but remain calm and find someone who can help them. They felt proud and happy that they helped the whale. They also felt amazed and curious about the big and beautiful animal. They decided to learn more about whales and how to protect them. They also thanked their mom and dad and the animal rescue team for their help. They had a very special day at the beach.

Lily was a girl who liked to demand things. She always wanted more toys, more candy, more attention. She did not like to share or say thank you. She thought she was better than everyone else.

One day, she went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She saw many animals, but she was not happy. She wanted to touch them and play with them. She did not listen to the signs that said "Do not feed" or "Do not climb". She demanded to go inside the cages.

Her mom and dad said no, that was dangerous and rude. But Lily did not care. She waited until they were not looking and sneaked into the cage of a big lion. She thought the lion was cute and fluffy. She wanted to hug him and take him home.

But the lion did not like Lily. He did not like her loud voice and her grabbing hands. He roared and showed his teeth. He was angry and scared. He wanted to escape from the cage and from Lily.

Lily was afraid too. She realized she made a big mistake. She screamed and cried for help. Her mom and dad heard her and ran to the cage. They saw the lion and Lily. They were terrified and called the zookeepers.

The zookeepers came and used a big net to catch the lion. They took him away to a safe place. They were angry at Lily and her parents. They said Lily could have been hurt or killed by the lion. They said Lily was lucky to be alive. They said Lily and her parents had to leave the zoo and never come back.

Lily was sad and ashamed. She wished she had listened to her mom and dad. She wished she had been nice and respectful to the animals. She learned a hard lesson. She was not proud of herself.

The moral of the story is: Do not demand things that are not yours. Do not ignore the rules and the warnings. Do not bother the animals that are not your friends. Be grateful and polite to everyone.

One day, Lily and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big tree with many birds on it. Lily and Ben liked the birds. They wanted to feed them some bread.

"Mom, can we give the birds some bread?" Lily asked.

"Okay, but be careful. Don't go too close to the tree. Some birds are naughty and they might bite you," Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They took some bread from Mom and broke it into small pieces. They threw the bread on the ground near the tree. The birds flew down and ate the bread. Lily and Ben were happy.

But one bird was very naughty. It did not want to share the bread with the other birds. It wanted all the bread for itself. It flew to Lily and Ben and tried to take the bread from their hands. It pecked at their fingers and made loud noises.

"Ow! Go away, naughty bird!" Lily cried.

"Stop it, naughty bird!" Ben shouted.

Mom heard them and ran to them. She scared the naughty bird away. She hugged Lily and Ben and checked their fingers.

"Are you okay, my darlings?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom. But the naughty bird hurt us," Lily said.

"I'm sorry, my darlings. That was a very naughty bird. It should not have done that. Let me tell you a story about a nice bird who shared his bread with his friends," Mom said.

Lily and Ben smiled. They forgot about the naughty bird. They listened to Mom's story and learned to be nice and share. They enjoyed the rest of the day at the park.

Lily and Ben were playing cowboys and robbers in the backyard. Lily had a hat and a pistol, and Ben had a scarf and a bag of coins. They ran around the trees and the swing, pretending to shoot and chase each other.

"Bang, bang, you're dead, robber!" Lily shouted, pointing her pistol at Ben.

"No, I'm not, cowboy! You missed me!" Ben said, dodging behind a bush.

"Yes, I did, I saw you fall!" Lily argued, running after him.

They kept playing until they heard their mom calling them for lunch. They dropped their toys and ran inside, where they saw a big plate of sandwiches and a bowl of fruit.

"Wow, this looks delicious!" Ben exclaimed, grabbing a sandwich.

"Me too, I'm hungry!" Lily agreed, taking a piece of fruit.

They sat down at the table and ate happily, talking about their game.

"Mom, can we play more after lunch?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey, but be careful with your pistol, okay? It's not a real one, but it can still hurt someone if you're not careful." Mom said.

"Okay, mom, I will be careful. And if I hurt Ben, I will heal him with a kiss." Lily said.

"That's very sweet of you, Lily. And Ben, if you hurt Lily, you will heal her too, right?" Mom said.

"Of course, mom. Lily is my best friend, I don't want to hurt her." Ben said.

They finished their lunch and thanked their mom. Then they ran outside again, ready to play more cowboys and robbers. They had a lot of fun, and they always healed each other with kisses when they pretended to get shot.

One day, Lily wants to record how tall she is. She asks her mom to help her. Her mom gets a measure. It is a long tape with numbers on it. Her mom puts one end on the floor and the other end on Lily's head. She tells Lily how many numbers she is.

Lily is happy. She wants to record the number. She runs to her toy and presses the button. She says, "I am 36 numbers tall!" Then she presses the other button and listens. She smiles.

But then she hears a loud noise. It is raining outside. Lily likes rain. She wants to go out and play. She puts on her boots and her coat. She grabs her toy and runs to the door.

Her mom stops her. She says, "Lily, you can't take your toy outside. It will get wet. Wet is bad for your toy. It will stop working. You can leave it here and play with it later."

Lily is sad. She likes her toy. She doesn't want it to get wet. She puts it on the table. She says, "Bye, toy. I will come back soon." Then she goes out with her mom. She splashes in the puddles. She thinks rain is fun, too.

Lily and Ben were playing with chalk on the sidewalk. They drew big flowers and stars and cars. They had fun making colors and shapes.

"Look, Lily, I made a fish!" Ben said, pointing to his blue chalk drawing.

"That's a nice fish, Ben. Can I make one too?" Lily asked.

"Sure, Lily. Here, take some blue chalk. You can make a fish next to mine." Ben said, handing her a piece of chalk.

Lily took the chalk and started to draw a fish. She made a round body, a tail, and a fin. She gave her fish an eye and a mouth. She was happy with her fish.

"Wow, Lily, your fish is beautiful. It looks like it can swim in the water." Ben said.

"Thank you, Ben. Your fish is beautiful too. It looks like it can dive in the water." Lily said.

"Dive? What does dive mean?" Ben asked.

"Dive means to go down in the water, like this." Lily said, and she bent her knees and jumped forward, pretending to dive.

"Ooh, that looks fun. Can I try?" Ben asked.

"Sure, Ben. But be careful, don't hit your head on the sidewalk." Lily said.

Ben nodded and bent his knees and jumped forward, pretending to dive. But he jumped too far and his head hit the edge of the sidewalk. He felt a sharp pain and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! That hurts!" Ben cried.

Lily heard Ben cry and ran to him. She saw blood on his forehead and felt worried.

"Oh no, Ben, are you okay? You have a boo-boo on your head. We need to get help." Lily said.

She helped Ben stand up and held his hand. She looked around and saw a lady walking her dog. She waved to the lady and shouted.

"Help, help! My friend has a boo-boo. He needs a band-aid. Can you help us?" Lily shouted.

The lady heard Lily and saw Ben. She came over and looked at his wound.

"Hello, children. What happened? Did you fall?" The lady asked.

"Yes, we were playing with chalk and he tried to dive and he hit his head." Lily explained.

"I see. That's not good. You need to clean your wound and put a band-aid on it. Come with me, I have a first-aid kit in my house. It's not far from here." The lady said.

She took Ben and Lily by the hand and led them to her house. She cleaned Ben's wound with water and soap and put a band-aid on it. She gave him a hug and a cookie.

"There, there. You'll be fine. It's just a small cut. It will heal soon. You're a brave boy." The lady said.

"Thank you, lady. You're very nice. I'm sorry I made a mess." Ben said.

"You're welcome, Ben. It's okay. Accidents happen. Just be more careful next time. And don't forget your chalk. You can take it with you." The lady said.

She gave Ben and Lily their chalk and walked them back to the sidewalk. She waved goodbye and went back to her dog.

Ben and Lily thanked the lady again and picked up their chalk. They looked at their fish drawings and smiled.

"Ben, I'm glad you're okay. I was worried about you." Lily said.

"Lily, I'm glad you're my friend. You helped me a lot." Ben said.

They hugged each other and decided to draw something else. They drew a big heart and wrote their names inside. They were happy and proud of their chalk art. They played until their moms came to pick them up. They said goodbye and promised to play again soon. They had a good day.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play baseball in the park. They have a bat, a ball and a glove. They take turns hitting and catching.

Tim swings the bat and hits the ball. The ball flies high in the air. Tim runs to the first base.

"Wow, good hit!" Sam says. He runs after the ball.

But the ball is too far. It lands in a big tree. Sam cannot reach it.

"Oh no, our ball is stuck!" Tim says. He stops at the first base.

Sam looks at the tree. He sees a hole in the trunk. He has an idea.

"Maybe we can use this stick to get the ball out," he says. He picks up a long stick from the ground. He thinks it is useful.

He walks to the tree. He puts the stick in the hole. He pushes and pulls.

But nothing happens. The ball does not move.

"This stick is not useful," Sam says. He drops the stick.

Tim and Sam are sad. They do not have their ball. They do not want to play anymore.

They sit under the tree. They look at the sky. They see some clouds. They see some birds. They see the sun.

They start to feel sleepy. They yawn.

"Let's go home, Sam," Tim says. He yawns again.

"OK, Tim," Sam says. He yawns too.

They get up. They leave their bat and glove under the tree. They hope to find their ball tomorrow.

One day, a big boy comes. He has a stick and a ball too. He says he wants to play hockey with them. Tim and Sam say yes. They think he is nice.

But the big boy is not nice. He hits the ball very hard. He does not share. He does not let Tim and Sam touch the ball. He says he is the best. He says they are bad.

Tim and Sam are sad and angry. They want to play too. They want to have fun. They tell the big boy to stop. They tell him to go away.

The big boy does not listen. He laughs at them. He says they are too thin and weak. He says they cannot race him. He says he is faster and stronger.

Tim and Sam are tired of the big boy. They decide to race him. They think they can beat him. They say they are ready. They say they will show him.

The big boy agrees. He says he will race them to the tree. He says he will win. He says they will lose.

They start to race. They run as fast as they can. They try to catch the big boy. But the big boy is too fast. He runs ahead of them. He reaches the tree first. He turns around and smiles.

Tim and Sam are close behind. They do not see the big boy. They do not see the stick. They do not see the ball. They only see the tree.

The big boy swings his stick. He hits the ball. He aims at Tim and Sam. He wants to hurt them. He wants to make them cry.

The ball flies in the air. It hits Tim in the head. It hits Sam in the chest. They fall to the ground. They scream in pain. They bleed and cry.

The big boy laughs. He says he won. He says they lost. He says they are stupid and slow. He says they are not good at hockey. He says they are not good at anything.

He picks up his stick and his ball. He walks away. He does not help them. He does not say sorry. He does not care.

Tim and Sam are alone. They are hurt and scared. They hug each other. They wish the big boy never came. They wish they never raced him. They wish they could play hockey again. They wish they could have fun again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big oak tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see the birds.

"Can you help me, Ben?" Lily asked. She tried to reach a branch, but it was too high.

"Sure, Lily. I will pull you up," Ben said. He grabbed Lily's hand and pulled hard. Lily felt a tug and moved up.

"Thank you, Ben. You are strong," Lily said. She smiled and sat on the branch. She looked around and saw a nest with three eggs.

"Wow, look at the eggs. They are blue and speckled," Ben said. He joined Lily on the branch. He was curious and wanted to touch the eggs.

"Be careful, Ben. Don't touch the eggs. They belong to the birds," Lily said. She knew that the eggs were fragile and the birds would be angry.

"But I just want to see them closer," Ben said. He reached out his hand and touched one of the eggs. Suddenly, he heard a loud squawk and felt a peck on his head.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He looked up and saw a big bird with a yellow beak and black feathers. It was the mother bird and she was not happy.

"Ben, what did you do? You made the bird mad. We have to go," Lily said. She was scared and uncomfortable. She did not like the bird's noise and bite.

"Sorry, Lily. I was just curious. Let's go," Ben said. He was sorry and uncomfortable too. He did not like the bird's noise and bite either.

They slid down the branch and ran away from the tree. They learned a lesson. They should not touch the eggs that belong to the birds. They should respect the nature and the animals. They should be careful and listen to each other.

Lily was surprised and excited. She had never seen a car like this before. She decided to try it. She pressed the button and said, "Hi, I am Lily. I like cars. What is your name?"

She pressed the button again and heard her own voice. She giggled. She liked the record car. She wanted to show it to her mom.

She ran to the kitchen where her mom was making lunch. She held the car in her hand and said, "Mom, look what I found. It is a record car. It can talk to me and I can talk to it. Listen!"

She pressed the button and played her voice. Her mom smiled and said, "Wow, that is a very unusual and fun car, Lily. Where did you get it?"

Her mom nodded and said, "Of course you can keep it, sweetie. It is yours. But remember to share it with your friends when they come over. They might like to play with it too."

Lily agreed and hugged her mom. She was happy. She had a new and unusual car that could record her voice. She wondered what else she could say to it. She ran back to her room and played with the record car for a long time.

"Look, a butterfly!" Sam said.

"Come back, butterfly!" Sam said.

They followed the butterfly. They did not see the rocks and the holes on the hill. They tripped and fell. They rolled down the hill. They bumped and scraped and got dirty. They landed on the grass at the bottom. They were hurt and sad.

"You are nice, butterfly!" Lily said.

They saw their mom and dad. They waved to them. They were proud.

"Hello, Frosty!" Tom said. "You are our friend!"

"Yes, you are!" Lily said. "We like you very much!"

They hugged Frosty and smiled.

But then the sun came out. It was very bright and warm. The snow started to melt. Frosty started to shrink.

"Oh no!" Tom said. "Frosty is melting!"

"We have to save him!" Lily said. "Let's move him to a shady place!"

They tried to push Frosty, but he was too heavy. They only made him smaller and smaller. Soon, he was just a pile of snow with a hat, a scarf and a carrot.

Tom and Lily felt very sad. They saw a stream of water running from Frosty to the road.

"Frosty is gone!" Tom said. "He is dead!"

"No, he is not!" Lily said. "He is still with us, in the water!"

She pointed to the stream. "Look, he is waving to us!"

Tom looked. He saw the hat, the scarf and the carrot floating on the water. They looked like they were moving.

"Hello, Frosty!" Tom said. "You are still our friend!"

"Yes, you are!" Lily said. "We still like you very much!"

They waved back to Frosty and smiled.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see what was up there.

They climbed the tree carefully. They saw many birds and bugs. They heard a chirp-chirp sound. They looked around and saw a nest. The nest was open and had four eggs inside.

"Wow, look at the eggs!" Sara said. "They are so pretty and colorful. Can we touch them?"

"No, Sara, we can't touch them," Ben said. "They belong to the birds. The birds made the nest to keep the eggs warm and safe. If we touch them, we might hurt them or make the birds angry."

"But I want to see them closer," Sara said. "Maybe we can take one and show it to mom and dad."

"That's not a good idea, Sara," Ben said. "The eggs are not toys. They are baby birds. They need their mom and dad to feed them and teach them how to fly. If we take one, we will make the birds sad and the baby bird lonely. How would you feel if someone took you away from mom and dad?"

Sara thought for a moment. She realized that Ben was right. She did not want to make the birds sad or the baby bird lonely. She did not want to be taken away from mom and dad. She said sorry to Ben and to the birds.

"Sorry, Ben, you are right. We should not touch the eggs. Sorry, birds, we did not mean to bother you. We will leave you alone now."

They climbed down the tree and went back to their mom and dad. They told them what they saw and what they learned. Mom and dad were proud of them for being kind and respectful to the birds and their nest.

The moral of the story is: We should not take or touch things that do not belong to us. We should respect the lives and feelings of other animals. We should be grateful for our own family and friends.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They also liked to look for things on the ground. Sometimes they found leaves, or stones, or feathers.

One day, they found a big acorn. It was brown and shiny and had a little hat. Sara picked it up and showed it to Ben.

"Look, Ben, I found an acorn!" she said.

"Wow, Sara, that's a brilliant acorn!" Ben said. "Can I see it?"

Sara nodded and gave the acorn to Ben. He held it in his hand and looked at it closely.

"It's so smooth and round," he said. "I wonder what's inside."

He tried to open the acorn, but it was too hard. He pulled and twisted, but it didn't budge.

"Maybe we need something to help us," Sara said. "Like a tool."

She looked around and saw a big stick. She ran to get it and brought it back to Ben.

"Here, Ben, use this stick," she said. "Maybe you can zip the acorn open with it."

Ben took the stick and tapped the acorn with it. Nothing happened. He tapped harder and harder, until he hit the acorn with all his strength.

CRACK!

The acorn split open and something flew out of it. It was a small, furry creature with a long tail and a black mask. It was a squirrel!

The squirrel was very scared and angry. It had been sleeping inside the acorn, and now it was awake and out in the open. It saw Ben and Sara and made a loud noise.

"SQUEAK!" it said.

Ben and Sara were very surprised and scared too. They dropped the stick and the acorn and ran away.

The squirrel chased them for a while, then stopped and went back to the acorn. It picked up the two halves and tried to put them back together. But it was too late. The acorn was broken and the squirrel had no home.

The squirrel sighed and looked for another acorn. It hoped it would find one that was big and shiny and had a little hat. And it hoped that no one would try to zip it open again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. They saw a cricket on the grass. It was brown and shiny and made a loud noise.

"Look, a cricket!" Tom said. "Let's catch it and keep it as a pet."

Lily nodded. She liked animals. She ran after the cricket and tried to grab it with her hand. But the cricket was fast and jumped away.

"Wait for me!" Tom said. He followed Lily and the cricket. They ran across the garden, past the flowers and the trees and the pond.

They came to a big pile of dirt. It was dirty and smelly and had worms and bugs in it. The cricket jumped into the dirt and hid.

"Ha, I see it!" Tom said. He reached into the dirt and felt the cricket. He pulled it out and held it in his hand. It was dirty and wet and squirmed.

"Yuck, it's dirty!" Lily said. She wrinkled her nose. "I don't want it as a pet anymore. Let's throw it away."

Tom shook his head. He liked the cricket. He wanted to keep it. He put it in his pocket.

"No, it's mine!" he said. "I caught it. It's my pet. I will name it Chirpy."

Lily was angry. She wanted to share the cricket. She did not like Tom being selfish. She pushed Tom and tried to take the cricket from his pocket.

"Give it to me!" she said. "It's not fair. You have to share."

Tom pushed Lily back. He did not want to share the cricket. He wanted to keep it for himself. He ran away from Lily.

"Go away!" he said. "It's my cricket. You can't have it."

Lily ran after Tom. She was crying. She wanted to play with the cricket. She wanted to be friends with Tom. She did not understand why he was so mean.

They ran and ran and ran. They did not see where they were going. They did not see the road. They did not see the car. They did not hear the horn.

The car hit them. They fell to the ground. They did not get up. They did not move. They did not breathe.

The cricket crawled out of Tom's pocket. It was still alive. It jumped away and disappeared.

The end.

"That's not fair, Tom! You are taking too much sand!" Lily said, frowning. She only had a little sand on her truck. She wanted to load more, but Tom was being selfish.

"No, I'm not! It's my sand, I found it first!" Tom said, grabbing another shovel of sand. He did not care about Lily's feelings. He only wanted to have the biggest load.

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like playing with Tom anymore. She had an idea. She waited until Tom was not looking, and then she took a big rock from the pile. She walked over to Tom's truck and put the rock on it.

"Hey, what are you doing?" Tom shouted, seeing Lily. He tried to move his truck, but it was too heavy. The rock was too big for his truck. It made his truck tip over and spill all the sand.

"Ha, ha! Now you have no sand!" Lily said, laughing. She felt happy. She had taught Tom a lesson.

Tom felt mad and sad. He had lost all his sand. He realized he had been selfish and mean to Lily. He wished he had shared the sand with her.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. Can we be friends again?" Tom said, looking at Lily.

Lily looked at Tom. She saw he was sorry. She decided to forgive him.

"Okay, Tom. I'm sorry, too. I should not have put the rock on your truck. Can we share the sand and the rocks?" Lily said, smiling.

"Sure, Lily. Let's share. We can have more fun that way." Tom said, smiling back.

They hugged and made up. They loaded their trucks with sand and rocks, but not too much. They measured their loads with a ruler. They made sure they had the same amount of inches. They played happily together. They learned to be kind and not selfish.

Tommy stood up and continued his wander. He was curious to see what else he might find. He spotted a ladybug on a flower. He carefully picked up the ladybug, admiring its pretty spots. "Come and play with me," he said. The ladybug flew away and Tommy smiled. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud buzzing sound. He looked up to see an ugly fly hovering just above his head. Tommy laughed and waved his hands. The fly flew away and Tommy's wander was over. He happily skipped back home, eager to tell his parents what he had found.

Lily thought that was a great idea. She got out her needle and thread and started to stitch the button onto her teddy bear's shirt. While she was stitching, her teddy bear said, "Thank you, Lily. Now I look even more interesting with my new button!" 

Lily was so happy that her teddy bear liked his new button. From that day on, Lily always looked for interesting things to attach to her toys. And her teddy bear was always by her side, looking his best with his new button.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to bake cakes. One day, she decided to make a special cake for her friend's birthday. She mixed flour, sugar, and eggs in a bowl and stirred it with a spoon. She poured the mixture into a pan and put it in the oven.

While the cake was baking, Lily went to visit her friend's horse at the stable. She fed the horse some carrots and petted its soft fur. Suddenly, the horse kicked its leg and hurt Lily's hand. She cried and ran back to her house.

When she got home, the cake was ready. Lily carefully took it out of the oven and decorated it with frosting and sprinkles. She brought the cake to her friend's birthday party and everyone loved it. Her friend was so happy that she gave Lily a big hug. Lily forgot all about her hurt hand and felt happy too.

The gray sky made Lucy sad. She wanted to see the sunshine. Suddenly, she had an idea. 

"Mommy, let's spray the sky! That will make the clouds go away and then the sunshine will come out," Lucy suggested. 

Mommy smiled. "That's a wonderful idea, Lucy. But, unfortunately, it doesn't work that way. We can't spray the sky and make the clouds go away. But I have an idea. Let's go outside and enjoy what sunshine we can find."

They went outside and a beam of sunshine shined on them. Lucy was happy to see the sunshine and play in it. 

"Look, Mommy! The sunshine came out!" Lucy said with excitement. 

"Yes, it did," Mommy smiled, relieved that the sky was no longer gray.

The path he was walking on started to get smaller and smaller. He soon found himself at the entrance of a dark cave. He stopped and thought for a second. The inside of the cave seemed a bit noisy! He decided to keep going. 

John walked further into the cave until he reached a big room. He could feel the walls vibrating and vibrating. He soon realised why - There were thousands of bats flying around! John was very scared and he wanted to go back. 

But then he saw something sparkle in the corner. He walked closer and saw that it was an old inkwell. He was excited - he'd never seen one before! He leaned closer and used the inkwell to lead him out of the cave. 

John made it out safe and sound. He said to himself, "I'm really glad I had the ink to lead me out of the cave. That was a noisy adventure!".

Her mom replied, "No, sweetheart, nature made the hurricane but also made it go away."

But as Lily dug, something strange happened. The glittery thing started to move. It wriggled and squirmed and made a hissing sound. Then it popped out of the hole and appeared in front of them. It was not gold. It was a snake!

Tom and Lily screamed and ran away from the hole. They dropped their jar and their shovel and ran to the house. They were very scared and very sad. They had not found gold. They had found a snake.

"Mom, dad, help!" they cried. "There's a snake in the garden!"

Mom and dad came out and saw the snake. They were not scared. They knew it was not a dangerous snake. It was a garter snake. It was harmless and shy. It had probably been hiding in the hole and got scared by the digging.

Mom and dad picked up the snake gently and put it in a box. They explained to Tom and Lily that the snake was not gold, but it was still a beautiful and interesting creature. They asked them if they wanted to keep it as a pet or let it go.

Tom and Lily looked at the snake. It was not what they had hoped for, but it was still pretty and curious. They decided to keep it as a pet. They named it Goldie and gave it a nice home in a terrarium. They learned more about snakes and how to take care of them. They still liked to dig in the garden, but they were more careful and respectful of the animals that lived there. They realized that sometimes, what appears to be gold is not gold, but something else that is also valuable and wonderful.

He whispered to Sam, "Don't say anything about the poison. Maybe she won't see it."

Sam nodded and looked away. He felt uncomfortable too.

Their mom started to sort out the things in the shed. She picked up a box and lifted it up. She didn't see the bottle on the shelf. The bottle fell down and broke on the floor. The poison spilled out and made a bad smell.

Their mom screamed and dropped the box. She saw the skull and bones on the bottle. She said, "What is this? Who put this here? This is very dangerous. Tim, Sam, did you know about this?"

They have fun pretending to be different people. They laugh and make stories.

Then, Anna sees a pair of shiny shoes. They are silver and have stars on them. Anna wants the shoes. She says, "Wow! These are the best shoes ever! I want them!"

But Ben sees the shoes too. He wants the shoes. He says, "No, these are the best shoes ever! I want them!"

Anna and Ben both reach for the shoes. They pull and tug. They yell and cry. They are angry and sad.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the garage. She sees Anna and Ben fighting over the shoes. She says, "Stop! What are you doing? Why are you fighting?"

Anna and Ben tell Mom that they both want the shoes. They say that the shoes are the best shoes ever. They say that they are not fair.

Mom looks at the shoes. She says, "These shoes are very old. They are not the best shoes ever. They are Grandma's shoes. She wore them when she was young. She loved them very much. She was very compassionate. She helped many people. She gave them food, clothes, and hugs. She was happy and kind."

Anna and Ben listen to Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not know. We love Grandma. She is compassionate too. She helps us. She gives us cookies, stories, and kisses. She is happy and kind."

Mom smiles. She says, "I am glad you love Grandma. She loves you too. She would be happy if you played with her shoes. But you have to share them. You have to be compassionate too. You have to help each other. You have to be happy and kind."

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Okay, Mom. We will share the shoes. We will be compassionate. We will help each other. We will be happy and kind."

They hug Mom. They hug each other. They put on the shoes. They take turns pretending to be Grandma. They laugh and make stories. They are happy and kind.

Lily and Ben were playing in the backyard. They saw a big grill that their dad used to make food. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Lily said.

"No, we can't. Dad said it is hot and we can get hurt." Ben said.

But Lily did not listen. She pulled the lid and saw some coals that were still glowing. They looked like red stars. She reached out to touch them.

"Ow!" She cried. She burned her hand and it hurt a lot. She ran to Ben and showed him her hand.

"See, I told you. You should listen to dad. He knows what is good for us." Ben said. He hugged Lily and helped her go inside.

Mom saw Lily's hand and put some ice on it. She was not angry, but she was sad.

"Why did you touch the grill, Lily?" She asked.

"I wanted to see the glow. It was pretty." Lily said.

"I know, but it was also dangerous. The glow means it is hot and can hurt you. You should be careful and obey dad. He loves you and wants you to be safe." Mom said.

Lily felt sorry. She learned her lesson. She said sorry to mom and dad and gave them a kiss. She was tired and wanted to sleep. She cuddled with Ben and they fell asleep.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents and be careful with things that can hurt you.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to play outside. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. As she climbed, she found a small, sour fruit on a branch. She picked it and took a bite. "Yuck!" she said, "This is so sour!"

Amy's friend, Tim, heard her and came over. "What's wrong, Amy?" he asked. "I found this sour fruit in the tree," she said, showing it to him. Tim looked at the fruit and said, "That's a lemon! My mom uses it to make lemonade."

Amy thought about it and said, "Let's make lemonade!" They went to Tim's house and squeezed the lemon into a cup. But then, Amy got a little bit of lemon juice on her hand. It was sticky and she didn't like it.

Amy saw a nail on the wall and had an idea. She took a cloth and wiped her hand on it. The sticky feeling was gone. "Thanks, nail!" said Amy. Then, they added water and sugar to the lemon juice, and they had a yummy lemonade to share.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to zoom them around the carpet and make loud noises. Sometimes they pretended they were racing or chasing each other.

"Look, I have a new car!" Lily said, holding up a shiny red car. "It can zoom faster than yours!"

"No, it can't!" Ben said, holding up his blue car. "Mine can zoom faster and louder!"

They decided to have a race to see who had the faster car. They lined up their cars at one end of the carpet and counted to three.

"Ready, set, zoom!" they shouted, and pushed their cars forward.

The cars zoomed across the carpet, leaving behind trails of dust. They were very close, but Lily's car was slightly ahead. Ben tried to catch up, but he pushed his car too hard. His car veered off the carpet and crashed into the door of the chamber.

The chamber was a small room where Mom and Dad kept some old things. They told Ben and Lily not to go inside, because it was dark and gloomy and full of spiders. Ben and Lily were afraid of the chamber, and never opened the door.

But now, Ben's car had opened the door by accident. The door creaked and swung open, revealing the chamber. It was dark and gloomy, just like Mom and Dad said. Ben and Lily could see some shadows and cobwebs inside.

"Uh-oh," Ben said, looking at his car. It had fallen inside the chamber, and he could not see it. "My car!"

He wanted to get his car back, but he was scared to go inside the chamber. He looked at Lily, hoping she would help him.

Lily looked at the chamber, too. She was scared, too, but she also felt sorry for Ben. She knew he loved his car, and she did not want him to lose it.

She took a deep breath and said, "Don't worry, Ben. I'll get your car for you."

She grabbed a flashlight from the shelf and turned it on. She walked slowly towards the chamber, shining the light inside. She saw Ben's car lying on the floor, next to a box of books. She reached inside and picked it up.

"Here you go, Ben," she said, handing him his car. "I found it!"

Ben smiled and hugged his car. He was happy to have it back, and he was grateful to Lily.

"Thank you, Lily," he said. "You're very brave!"

Lily smiled, too. She felt proud and happy.

They closed the door of the chamber and went back to the carpet. They decided to play something else, something that did not involve zooming into dark and gloomy rooms. Tom and Sue packed their toys and books in big boxes. They put their names on the boxes. They said goodbye to their old house and their friends. They got in the car with their mom and dad. They drove for a long time to the new house.

The new house was big and strange. It had no yard and no trees. It had many stairs and many doors. Tom and Sue did not like it. They wanted their old house and their friends. They opened their boxes to find their toys and books. But they could not find them. They only found clothes and shoes and blankets.

Their mom and dad said they were sorry. They said they made a mistake. They said they mixed up the boxes. They said their toys and books were in another car. They said they would get them soon. But they did not. They lied. They sold their toys and books to buy the new house. Tom and Sue were very sad and angry. They hated the new house and the large world. They wished they never packed.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a small table and some cups and plates. They pretended to have a tea party with their toys.

"Would you like some tea, Mr. Bear?" Lily asked, holding a cup.

"Yes, please, Lily. You are very kind," Mr. Bear said in a low voice.

Tom poured some water from a jug into the cup. He added a spoon of sugar and stirred it. He gave the cup to Lily, who served it to Mr. Bear.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good helper," Lily said.

Tom smiled. He liked to help his sister. He looked at the other toys. He saw a card on the table. It had a picture of a lemon and some words.

"What is this, Lily?" Tom asked, pointing at the card.

"That is a recipe, Tom. It tells you how to make lemonade. Mom gave it to me. She said it is a refreshing drink for hot days," Lily explained.

"Can we make lemonade, Lily? I want to try it," Tom said.

"Sure, Tom. We need some lemons, some water, some sugar, and a big bowl. Let's go to the kitchen and ask Mom," Lily said.

They took the card and ran to the kitchen. Mom was there, making a cake.

"Mom, can we make lemonade, please?" Lily asked, showing her the card.

"Of course, my dears. That sounds like a fun idea. Here are some lemons, some water, some sugar, and a big bowl. You can use the juicer to squeeze the lemons. Be careful not to get the juice in your eyes. It is very bitter," Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. We will be careful," Lily said.

Tom and Lily took the things to the garden. They followed the recipe on the card. They squeezed the lemons, added the water and the sugar, and mixed everything in the bowl. They poured the lemonade into the cups and tasted it.

"Mmm, this is delicious," Lily said.

"Yes, it is. But it is also a little bitter," Tom said.

"That's okay, Tom. The sugar makes it sweet. Do you want to serve some to our toys?" Lily asked.

"Yes, Lily. I think they will like it too," Tom said.

They served the lemonade to their toys and enjoyed their tea party. They were happy and thirsty. They drank all the lemonade and thanked Mom for the card.

Lily and Tom were going to the airport with Mom and Dad. They were very excited to fly in a big plane. They had a suitcase each with their clothes and toys.

"Be careful with your suitcase, Lily," Mom said. "It has a fragile sticker on it. That means it can break easily."

"What is fragile, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Fragile means something that is not strong or hard. It can crack or tear if you drop it or hit it. Like your doll or your glass cup," Mom explained.

"Oh, I see. I will be gentle with my suitcase, Mom. I don't want to break my doll," Lily said.

They got to the airport and waited in a long line. Tom was bored and started to kick his suitcase.

"Stop that, Tom," Dad said. "You might damage your suitcase or someone else's. And you might hurt your foot."

"But I'm bored, Dad. This line is too slow," Tom said.

"I know, Tom. But we have to be patient. The airport is very busy today. They are trying to improve their service, but it takes time," Dad said.

"What is improve, Dad?" Tom asked.

"Improve means to make something better or nicer. Like when you clean your room or draw a picture. You improve your room or your picture," Dad explained.

"Oh, I see. I will try to improve my behavior, Dad. I don't want to be naughty," Tom said.

They finally reached the check-in counter and gave their suitcases to the lady. She put them on a belt that moved them to the plane.

"Have a nice flight, Lily and Tom," the lady said.

"Thank you, lady. We will have fun on the plane," Lily and Tom said.

They followed Mom and Dad to the gate and boarded the plane. They found their seats and buckled their seat belts. They looked out the window and saw the airport and the other planes.

"Wow, this is amazing," Lily and Tom said.

They smiled and hugged each other. They were ready for their adventure.

Lily was a shy girl who did not like to talk to other kids. She liked to play with her dolls and draw pictures in her room. One day, her mom told her that they were going to visit her aunt and uncle, who had a big house and a big dog.

Lily was scared of the big dog. She had never seen a dog so big and loud. She hid behind her mom when they entered the house. The dog ran to them and barked. Lily's mom said, "Don't be afraid, Lily. This is Max. He is very friendly and gentle. He just wants to say hello."

Lily did not want to say hello. She ran to the couch and covered herself with a sheet. She hoped the dog would not see her. But Max was curious. He sniffed the sheet and nudged it with his nose. Lily screamed and held the sheet tighter.

"Lily, what are you doing?" her aunt asked. She came to the couch and lifted the sheet. She saw Lily's scared face. "Oh, honey, you don't have to be shy. Max is a good dog. He won't hurt you. He just wants to play with you. Why don't you give him a chance?"

Lily looked at her aunt and then at Max. Max wagged his tail and licked her hand. He looked friendly and gentle. Lily felt a little less scared. She smiled and petted his head. Max barked happily and licked her face. Lily giggled and hugged him.

Lily's mom and aunt smiled and praised her. "You see, Lily, you don't have to be shy. Sometimes, you just have to be brave and try new things. You might find a new friend or have a new fun. You are a good girl, Lily."

Lily felt proud and happy. She had a new friend and a new fun. She played with Max and the other kids. She had a great time at her aunt and uncle's house. She learned that being shy is not always good. Sometimes, being brave is better.

Tom and Lily were very happy. They took turns to sit in the pumpkin car and drive it around the garden. They pretended they were going to a party or a farm or a castle. They had so much fun.

But then, Tom drove the pumpkin car too fast and hit a rock. The pumpkin car broke into pieces. The wheels and the steering wheel fell off. The pumpkin was smashed and messy. Tom and Lily were sad.

Mom came to see what happened. She hugged Tom and Lily and said it was okay. She said they could make another pumpkin car or something else. She said they could use the broken pumpkin to make a pie or a soup. She said they could reverse the sad into happy.

Tom and Lily smiled. They liked the idea of reversing the sad into happy. They helped Mom to collect the pumpkin pieces and the toy parts. They said they were sorry for breaking the pumpkin car. They said they loved Mom and each other. They said they still liked to play with their toy cars. They said they would try to be more careful next time.

But then they saw some dark clouds in the sky. They heard a loud noise like a big drum. They felt some drops of water on their faces. They knew it was a storm. They did not like storms. They were scared.

"Let's go inside, Lily!" Tom said. "The storm is coming!"

"OK, Tom!" Lily said. "But where is our ball?"

They looked around and saw their ball on the other side of the yard. It was near a big tree. They wanted to get their ball, but they did not want to go near the tree. They heard that trees could be hit by lightning in storms. That was rare, but it could happen.

"Who will get the ball?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Lily said.

They looked at each other. They did not want to leave their ball outside. They did not want to lose it. They liked their ball.

They decided to be brave. They held hands and ran towards the ball. They reached the ball and grabbed it. They turned around and ran back to the house. They were fast.

They made it to the door just as the storm got worse. The wind was blowing and the rain was pouring. They heard more loud noises and saw flashes of light. They were glad they were inside.

They closed the door and hugged their ball. They felt safe and happy. They had their ball and each other. They had risen to the challenge. They were proud.

"OK, Tom, but be careful. There is a storm coming. See the dark clouds?" Lily said.

They ran to the stick and put the ruler next to it. It was longer than the ruler. They were happy.

"Wow, this stick is so long! How many rulers do you think it is?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe four or five. But we should go inside now. The storm is getting closer. Hear the thunder?" Lily said.

But Tom did not listen. He wanted to measure the stick more. He moved the ruler along the stick.

"Wait, Lily, I want to see how long it is. Just one more minute!" Tom said.

Lily was scared. She saw a flash of lightning in the sky. She grabbed Tom's hand.

"Tom, please, let's go inside. The storm is here. It is dangerous. The lightning can hurt us!" Lily said.

But Tom did not listen. He pulled his hand away from Lily. He wanted to measure the stick more. He moved the ruler to the end of the stick.

"Look, Lily, I did it! The stick is six rulers long! Isn't that amazing?" Tom said.

But Lily did not answer. She saw another flash of lightning. It hit the stick. It hit Tom. Tom fell to the ground. He did not move. He did not speak.

Lily screamed. She ran to Tom. She tried to wake him up. But he did not wake up. He was gone.

Lily cried. She wished she had made Tom listen. She wished they had gone inside. She wished they had been careful.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your friends when they warn you of danger. Do not play with things that can attract lightning. Be careful when there is a storm.

"Yes, it is a block," Mom said. "And it can be many things. It can be part of a tower, or a castle, or a rocket, or anything you can imagine. But it can only be one thing at a time. And it can only be one thing if you work together. If you fight over it, it is nothing but a block."

She put the block down and gave them a gentle smile.

"Why don't you try to move your feet and share your space?" Mom said. "Maybe you can build something amazing with the blocks, if you use your words and your hands and your hearts."

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for being mean and selfish. They nodded and said sorry.

"Sorry, Lily," Ben said.

"Sorry, Ben," Lily said.

They moved their feet and shared their space. They used their words and their hands and their hearts. They built a wide and high tower, with a castle and a rocket on top. They were happy and proud.

Mom came back and saw the tower. She was happy and proud too.

"Wow, what a wonderful tower!" Mom said. "You did a great job, Lily and Ben!"

"Thank you, Mom!" Lily and Ben said.

They hugged Mom and each other. They learned that sharing is caring, and that working together is better. They played with their blocks and had fun.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They also saw some bees flying around a big hive.

"Look, mom, bees!" Lily said, pointing at the hive.

"Yes, they are bees. They make honey and help the flowers grow," mom said.

"Can we go closer and see them?" Ben asked.

"Only a little bit, and be very quiet and careful. Bees don't like to be disturbed," mom said.

Ben and Lily walked slowly to the hive. They saw the bees buzzing in and out of the small holes. Some bees had yellow and black stripes, and some had orange and black stripes.

"Wow, they are so busy!" Ben said.

"They are. They have to organize their hive and collect nectar and pollen from the flowers," mom said.

"What is organize?" Lily asked.

"Organize means to make things neat and tidy and in order. The bees have to organize their hive so they can store their honey and take care of their babies," mom said.

"That sounds hard. How do they do that?" Ben asked.

"They use their antennas and their dances to talk to each other and tell each other what to do and where to go. They are very smart and work together as a team," mom said.

"Can we talk to them too?" Lily asked.

"Maybe, but we have to be very polite and gentle. Let's try to say hello to them," mom said.

Mom, Ben and Lily waved their hands and said softly, "Hello, bees! We are your friends. We like your honey and your flowers. Thank you for being so nice and helpful."

Some of the bees flew closer and buzzed back, as if to say hello too. Ben and Lily smiled and giggled.

"See, they are friendly. But we should not stay too long. They have a lot of work to do, and we don't want to bother them," mom said.

"Okay, mom. Bye, bees! Have a good day!" Ben and Lily said.

They waved goodbye to the bees and walked back to the bench. They had a snack and a drink and talked about the bees and their hive.

"They are amazing, mom. I want to be a bee when I grow up," Ben said.

"Me too, mom. I want to organize things like the bees," Lily said.

Mom hugged them and said, "You can be anything you want, my sweeties. But you are already wonderful just the way you are."

One day, Tom and Anna wanted to bake a cake for their mom. They found a recipe in a book and got some eggs, flour, sugar, and butter. They mixed everything in a big bowl and poured it into a pan. Then they put the pan in the oven and turned it on.

"Mom will love this cake!" Tom said.

But they forgot to set the timer and went to play with their toys. The cake stayed in the oven for too long and started to burn. Smoke came out of the oven and filled the kitchen. The smoke alarm beeped loudly and scared Tom and Anna.

"Uh-oh, what's that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, but it smells bad!" Anna said.

They ran out of the kitchen and saw a fire truck outside. A fireman knocked on the door and opened it. He saw the smoke and the cake in the oven. He turned off the oven and took out the cake. It was black and hard and smelled awful.

"Who baked this cake?" the fireman asked.

Tom and Anna looked at each other and felt uncomfortable. They knew they had done something wrong.

"We did, sir," Tom said.

"We wanted to surprise our mom," Anna said.

The fireman smiled and said, "That's very sweet of you, but you should never bake without an adult. Baking can be dangerous if you don't watch the oven. Next time, ask your mom or dad to help you, okay?"

Tom and Anna nodded and said, "Okay, sir. We're sorry."

The fireman said, "It's okay, no one got hurt. But this cake is not edible. How about I help you make a new one? I know a good recipe."

Tom and Anna smiled and said, "Yes, please!"

The fireman took them to his fire truck and showed them his kitchen. He had some ingredients and tools in a box. He taught them how to measure, mix, and bake a cake. He also let them decorate it with frosting and sprinkles. The cake looked and smelled delicious.

"Wow, you're a great baker, sir!" Tom said.

"Thank you, you're great helpers!" the fireman said.

They wrapped the cake in a paper and wrote a note for their mom. They thanked the fireman and gave him a hug. He drove them back to their house and said goodbye.

Tom and Anna ran inside and put the cake on the table. They waited for their mom to come home. When she saw the cake and the note, she was very happy and proud. She hugged them and said, "This is the best cake ever! Thank you, my loves!"

They cut the cake and shared it with their mom and the fireman. They all enjoyed it and had a fun time. Tom and Anna learned a lesson and made a new friend. They never baked without an adult again.

The trap snapped on Tom's leg and hurt him a lot. He cried and cried, but no one came to help him. He was stuck in the trap. He could not move. He could not eat. He could not go back to his celery.

He looked at his celery and felt very sad. He wished he had not left his celery. He wished he had shared his celery with his friends. He missed his celery and his friends. He learned that celery was better than carrot, and sharing was better than being greedy.

There was a hairy creature in her wardrobe. It had four legs, a long tail, and a big mane. It looked like a lion, but it was glowing. It had yellow eyes that stared at Lily. Lily wanted to run away, but the creature spoke to her.

"Hello, little girl. Don't be afraid. I am Leo, the glowing lion. I come from a world where everything glows. I was looking for a friend to play with. Do you want to come with me?"

Lily was surprised. She had never seen a glowing lion before, or heard one talk. She wondered what his world was like. She felt brave and curious. She nodded and smiled.

"OK, Leo. I will come with you. But we have to be back before morning. My mom and dad will be worried if they don't see me in my bed."

Leo nodded and smiled back. He moved aside and let Lily enter the wardrobe. Behind the clothes and shoes, there was a hole that led to a tunnel of light. Leo and Lily walked through the tunnel, holding paws. They were ready for an adventure.

Lila and Ben were twins who loved to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big teddy bear that was soft and brown. They named him Teddy and gave him hugs and kisses every day.

One day, they decided to play hide and seek with Teddy. Lila hid Teddy under a blanket on the couch and told Ben to find him. Ben looked around the room, but he could not see Teddy anywhere. He checked behind the curtains, under the table, and in the closet, but Teddy was not there.

"Where is Teddy?" Ben asked, feeling sad. "I can't find him!"

Lila giggled and said, "He is very good at hiding! Do you want a hint?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, please!"

Lila smiled and said, "He is somewhere cozy and warm!"

Ben thought for a moment and then ran to the couch. He lifted the blanket and saw Teddy's adorable face peeking out. He grabbed Teddy and hugged him tightly.

"I found you, Teddy!" Ben exclaimed, happy. "You are the best hider ever!"

Lila joined him on the couch and cuddled with Teddy too. She said, "You are the best finder ever, Ben!"

They both kissed Teddy on his nose and settled on the couch with him. They wrapped the blanket around their waists and snuggled together. They felt cozy and warm and loved.

He runs after the bird and jumps on it. But the bird is not scared. It is fierce. It turns around and pecks Tom on the nose. It flaps its wings and makes a loud noise. Tom is surprised and hurt. He lets go of the bird and runs away.

The bird flies to a tree and laughs. It is a peacock. It is proud of its feathers and its strength. It does not like cats. It thinks they are rude and silly. It spreads its tail and shows its colors. It serves Tom a lesson.

Lily and Tom stop fighting. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, friend."

Mom smiles. She says, "It is OK. I am glad you are sorry. Now, let us play with the trains together. You can have the red train for five minutes, and then you can give it to Tom. And then he can give it back to you. And so on. Is that OK?"

Lily and Tom nod. They say, "OK, Mom. OK, friend."

They play with the trains. They share the track. They make the trains go fast or slow. They are happy. Mom is happy.

Lily was a poor girl who lived with her mom in a small house. They did not have much money or things, but they loved each other very much. Lily wanted to help her mom, so she tried to do some chores every day.

One day, Lily decided to clean the bathroom. She took a sponge and some soap and started to scrub the sink and the toilet. She was very careful not to make a mess. She wanted to make the bathroom shiny and nice.

Then she saw the shower. It was dirty and had some mold on the tiles. Lily thought that the shower needed some cleaning too. She turned on the water and sprayed the soap on the walls. She used the sponge to wipe the soap off. She was having fun and did not notice that the water was splashing everywhere.

"Wow, Lily, what are you doing?" her mom asked, as she walked into the bathroom. She saw the water on the floor and the soap on the mirror. She was not angry, but she was surprised.

"I'm cleaning the shower, mom!" Lily said proudly. "Do you like it?"

Her mom smiled and hugged her. "You are very sweet, Lily, and I appreciate your help. But you don't need to clean the shower like that. You can just use a cloth and some vinegar. And you have to be careful not to waste water. Water is precious, and we don't have much of it."

Lily nodded and said sorry. She did not know that water was precious. She wanted to do a good job and make her mom happy. She did not want to waste water or make a mess.

Her mom dried the floor and the mirror with a towel. She helped Lily finish cleaning the shower with a cloth and some vinegar. She praised Lily for her hard work and her good intentions. She told her that she was proud of her and that she loved her.

Lily felt happy and hugged her mom back. She learned something new and she succeeded in cleaning the shower. She loved her mom too and she wanted to help her more. She thought that they were not so poor after all. They had each other and they had a clean bathroom.

Sam and Tom were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill with a cliff at the end. They wanted to go up the hill and see what was on the other side of the cliff.

"Let's go, Sam!" Tom said. "Maybe we can find something fun!"

"OK, Tom!" Sam said. "But be careful. The hill is steep and the cliff is high."

They started to climb the hill, holding hands and helping each other. They saw some birds, some flowers, and some rocks on the way. They were happy and curious.

When they reached the top of the hill, they saw a big lake with blue water and green trees. They also saw a thin bridge that crossed the lake to the other side.

"Wow, look at that, Sam!" Tom said. "Do you want to cross the bridge?"

Sam looked at the bridge and felt scared. The bridge was thin and old. It looked like it could break any time.

"I don't know, Tom," Sam said. "The bridge is thin and old. It looks like it could break any time."

"Don't be scared, Sam," Tom said. "It will be fun. Come on, follow me!"

Tom ran to the bridge and started to cross it. He did not listen to Sam. He did not see the cracks and holes in the bridge.

"Tom, wait!" Sam shouted. "The bridge is not safe!"

But Tom did not answer. He was too excited to hear Sam. He kept running and jumping on the bridge.

Suddenly, the bridge snapped and broke. Tom fell into the lake with a splash.

"Tom!" Sam screamed. "Tom, are you OK?"

Sam ran to the edge of the cliff and looked down. He saw Tom in the water, waving his arms and calling for help.

"Help me, Sam!" Tom said. "Help me, please!"

Sam was scared and sad. He did not know what to do. He wished he had a rope or a stick or something to help Tom.

He looked around and saw a big bird flying in the sky. The bird had a long and strong beak. Sam had an idea.

"Hey, bird!" Sam shouted. "Hey, bird, can you help me?"

The bird heard Sam and flew down to him. It looked at Sam and Tom and understood their problem.

"What do you need, little boy?" the bird asked.

"Can you please help my brother?" Sam said. "He fell into the lake and he can't swim. Can you please pick him up with your beak and bring him to me?"

The bird nodded and flew to the lake. It grabbed Tom with its beak and lifted him out of the water. It carried him to the cliff and dropped him next to Sam.

"Thank you, bird!" Sam said. "Thank you so much!"

"You're welcome, little boy," the bird said. "But next time, be more careful. Don't cross thin and old bridges. They are dangerous."

Sam hugged Tom and said sorry. Tom hugged Sam and said thank you. They both said thank you to the bird again.

The bird smiled and flew away. Sam and Tom went back down the hill, holding hands and helping each other. They learned their lesson and never crossed thin and old bridges again.

"Icy ice helps the ouch," she said. "But you have to be careful. Don't touch the cactus again. It is not nice."

Tom nodded. He hugged Lily and said sorry. He learned his lesson. He would stay away from the cactus. He would play with Lily and the other plants. They were nice. They did not bite.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their dog, Rex. Rex was a big and reliable dog. He always followed them and protected them from danger. Lily and Tom loved Rex very much.

One day, they saw some smoke coming from a big house near the park. They heard people shouting and crying. They were scared and curious. They wanted to see what was happening. They ran towards the house, but Rex barked and stopped them.

"Rex, what's wrong?" Lily asked. "Why can't we go and see?"

Rex barked louder and pulled them back. He knew the house was on fire and it was not safe to go near it. He wanted Lily and Tom to stay away from the smoke and the flames.

"Rex, let us go!" Tom said. "We just want to look!"

Rex shook his head and growled. He did not let them go. He was a reliable dog and he cared for Lily and Tom.

Soon, they saw some big red trucks coming. They had sirens and lights. They were fire trucks. The fire trucks stopped near the house and some men in yellow suits got out. They had hoses and ladders. They were firefighters. They sprayed water on the house and climbed on the roof. They tried to put out the fire and save the people inside.

Lily and Tom watched from a distance. They saw how brave and strong the firefighters were. They also saw how dangerous and scary the fire was. They felt the heat and smelled the smoke. They started to tremble and cry.

"Rex, you were right," Lily said. "We should not have gone near the house. It was too risky. We could have been hurt or lost."

"Rex, you are a good dog," Tom said. "You saved us from trouble. You are our hero."

Rex licked their faces and wagged his tail. He was happy and proud. He had done his job. He was a reliable dog and he loved Lily and Tom.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your reliable friends. They know what is best for you and they want to keep you safe.

Mia nodded and smiled. She said, "Of course, I will hold your hand. We are friends. We can swim together."

Sam put on his swimsuit and took Mia's hand. They walked slowly to the pool and dipped their toes in the water. It was warm and soft. Sam felt better and less cold. He said, "Hey, this is not so bad. It is actually nice and cozy."

Mia said, "I told you so. It is fun. Let's go deeper and splash and laugh."

Sam and Mia went deeper into the pool and splashed and laughed. They forgot about the cold and the wind. They had fun. Their moms watched them and smiled. They were proud of them. They encouraged them. They were happy.
