"Thank you for saving me," Tweetie said to Lily.

"Don't worry, little one. I promise to always protect you," Lily replied.

From that day on, Tweetie and Lily became the best of friends. Whenever Whiskers came around, Lily would scare him away with her graceful wings. Tweetie was happy to have such a good friend who kept her promise to always keep him safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to climb mountains with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went on a big adventure to climb a very tall mountain. It was so high that Lily felt a little scared, but her mommy and daddy were there to hold her hand.

As they climbed higher and higher, Lily's mommy noticed that her shoe was untied. She stopped to tie it, but accidentally dropped her water bottle. It fell down the mountain and hit a rock, making a terrible noise. Suddenly, a big boulder came loose and started rolling down the mountain.

Lily's mommy and daddy tried to run, but the boulder was too fast. It hit them and they couldn't attach themselves to the mountain. Lily was very sad and missed her mommy and daddy very much. She knew she would never climb a mountain again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet dog named Max. One day, Lily and Max were playing in the park when suddenly, Max saw a squirrel and ran after it. Lily tried to call him back, but Max didn't come back. Lily was sad and started to cry.

Just then, a kind lady saw Lily crying and came over to ask what was wrong. Lily told her that Max had run away and she didn't know where he went. The lady said she would help Lily find Max and they started to look for him.

They looked everywhere, but Max was nowhere to be found. Lily was getting more and more sad. Just when they were about to give up, Max came running back to Lily, wagging his tail. Lily was so happy to see Max again and hugged him tight. "Max, you came back so quick!" she said.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty garden. In the garden, there was a spider who loved to spin webs. One day, a little girl named Lily came to the garden.

"Hello, Mr. Spider," said Lily. "Can you please spin me a web?"

"Of course, little girl," replied the spider. "I will spin you the prettiest web you've ever seen."

The spider spun and spun until he made a beautiful web. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Spider! Your web is so pretty."

"You're welcome, little girl," said the spider. "I'm happy to help." And from that day on, Lily visited the garden often to see the pretty spider and his webs.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat candy all day long. He would eat candy for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. His mom told him that too much candy would make him sick, but Timmy didn't listen.

One day, Timmy got really sick. His tummy hurt and he had a fever. The doctor told Timmy's mom that Timmy had eaten too much candy and that he needed to stop. Timmy felt guilty for not listening to his mom.

From that day on, Timmy decided to turn his bad habit around. He started to eat more fruits and vegetables and less candy. His tummy felt better, and he had more energy to play with his friends. Timmy learned that too much candy can increase the chances of getting sick, and that it's important to listen to his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved pie, especially apple pie. His mommy always made sure to bake him a healthy pie with fresh apples from their garden. 

One day, Timmy went outside to play with his friends. They were having so much fun that they didn't hear the sound of thunder. Suddenly, it started to rain really hard. Timmy and his friends ran back to his house to get out of the rain. 

When they got inside, Timmy's mommy was just taking a fresh apple pie out of the oven. The smell was so good that Timmy's friends could hardly wait to try a piece. They all sat down at the table and enjoyed a nice warm slice of healthy apple pie. They were so happy to be safe and warm inside, listening to the raindrops falling on the roof.

Once upon a time, there was a little flower. The flower was very small and couldn't bloom like the other flowers. It felt sad and lonely. One day, it heard about a meeting for all the flowers in the garden. The little flower was excited to go and meet other flowers.

At the meeting, the little flower saw all the other flowers blooming beautifully. It felt even sadder and lonelier because it couldn't bloom like them. Suddenly, a powerful wind came and blew all the flowers away. The little flower was scared and didn't know what to do.

But then, the little flower remembered something it had heard. It had heard that even though it was small, it had a powerful ability to hold on tight to the ground. So, the little flower used its powerful ability and held on tight. It didn't get blown away like the other flowers. The other flowers were amazed and realized that even though the little flower couldn't bloom, it had its own powerful ability. From that day on, they all became friends and the little flower never felt sad and lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect pretty rocks and shells at the beach. One day, she saw a poor little mole digging in the sand. "What are you doing?" Lily asked. "I'm trying to find my home," replied the mole. "Can I help you?" asked Lily. "Yes, please!" said the mole.

So, Lily and the mole searched together and found the mole's home. "Thank you so much!" said the mole. "You're welcome," said Lily. "Do you want to come collect rocks and shells with me?" "Yes, please!" said the mole. And from that day on, Lily and the mole collected rocks and shells together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny lived in a big forest with his family and friends. One day, Benny was playing with his friends when he saw a big, scary cat! Benny was so scared that he ran away as fast as he could.

The cat chased Benny, but Benny was very fast. Benny ran and ran until he found a small hole in the ground. Benny squeezed through the hole and escaped from the cat. Benny was safe!

But then, Benny saw a gloomy cop walking by. The cop saw Benny and asked him what was wrong. Benny told the cop about the scary cat and how he had to escape. The cop listened and then helped Benny find his way back home. Benny was very happy that the cop was kind and helped him.

Lily loves her pony, Max. She likes to brush his hair and feed him carrots. Sometimes, she rides on his back and he goes fast.

One day, it rains a lot. Lily and Max stay inside the barn. They are sad because they cannot play outside. Lily gives Max a hug and tells him it will be sunny soon.

The next day, the sun comes out. Lily and Max are happy. They go outside and see a big puddle. Lily wants to jump in it, but Max does not. He does not like to get wet. Lily says, "Please, Max, it will be fun!"

Max shakes his head. He does not want to make Lily sad, but he does not want to jump in the puddle. He sees a lemon tree nearby. He has an idea. He picks a lemon and gives it to Lily. He says, "Try this, Lily, it is yummy!"

Lily takes the lemon and bites it. She makes a funny face. The lemon is sour! It makes her mouth pucker. She says, "Ew, Max, this is not yummy! This is sour!"

Max laughs. He says, "I know, Lily, I was joking. I do not like lemons either. But I like you. And I like to make you laugh."

Lily laughs too. She says, "You are silly, Max. But I like you too. And I like to make you laugh. Come on, let's go jump in the puddle. It will be fun!"

Max nods. He says, "Okay, Lily, let's go. But only if you dry me off later."

Lily says, "Deal, Max, deal. You are the best pony ever."

They run to the puddle and splash each other. They have fun. They are happy. They are friends.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to go on the swing. The swing is fun. It goes up and down, and makes them feel happy.

One day, they go to the park with Anna's mom. Anna's mom says, "You can play on the swing, but be careful. Don't go too high, or you might fall. I will watch you from the bench."

Anna and Ben nod. They are honest. They want to be good. They run to the swing. They take turns. Anna pushes Ben. Ben pushes Anna. They laugh and giggle.

But then, Ben pushes Anna too hard. Anna goes very high. She feels scared. She wants to stop. She says, "Ben, stop! Stop! I don't like it!"

Ben tries to stop. He grabs the swing. But the swing is too fast. It slips from his hand. Anna flies off the swing. She lands on the grass. She cries. She hurts her knee.

Anna's mom hears her cry. She runs to her. She picks her up. She hugs her. She says, "Anna, are you okay? What happened?"

Anna tells her mom what happened. She says, "Ben pushed me too hard. I fell off the swing. It was an accident. He didn't mean it."

Ben runs to Anna and her mom. He is sorry. He panics. He says, "Anna, I'm sorry! I'm sorry! I didn't mean to push you too hard. Are you okay?"

Anna's mom looks at Ben. She sees that he is honest. She sees that he is scared. She says, "Ben, it's okay. I know you didn't mean it. Anna is okay. She just has a little scratch. But you have to be more careful next time. The swing can be dangerous if you go too high."

Ben nods. He says, "I'm sorry, Anna. I'm sorry, Anna's mom. I will be more careful next time. Can we still be friends?"

Anna looks at Ben. She sees that he is honest. She sees that he is sorry. She says, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. We can still be friends. But don't push me too hard again."

Anna and Ben hug. They say sorry again. Anna's mom smiles. She says, "That's good. I'm glad you are friends. Now, let's go get some ice cream. That will make you feel better."

Anna and Ben smile. They say, "Yes, please! Ice cream! Ice cream!"

They hold hands. They walk with Anna's mom. They go get some ice cream. They are happy. They are friends.

Sam and Lily like to play in the hut. The hut is in the garden. It is made of wood and has a door and a window. Sam and Lily have toys and books in the hut.

One day, it is raining. Sam and Lily are in the hut. They hear a loud noise. They look out of the window. They see a big truck. The truck has a heavy load. It is carrying bricks and stones.

"Wow, look at that truck!" Sam says. "It is so big and strong. I want to drive a truck like that when I grow up."

"Me too!" Lily says. "But I also want to build things with the bricks and stones. Maybe we can make a castle or a bridge."

They watch the truck go by. Then they have an idea. They take some of their toys and books and make a pile. They pretend it is a load of bricks and stones. They take turns to be the truck driver and the builder.

"Beep beep!" Sam says. He pushes a toy car with the pile on it. "I am the truck. I have a heavy load. Where do you want me to go?"

"Over here!" Lily says. She points to a corner of the hut. "I am the builder. I need the bricks and stones to make a castle. Thank you, truck."

They have fun playing with their toys and books. They make a castle and a bridge and a tower. They are happy in the hut. They do not mind the rain.

Lily and Ben were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many boats on the sea, but one boat was very big and shiny. It was a yacht.

"Look, mom, look, dad, a yacht!" Lily said, pointing at the boat.

"Yes, dear, that is a yacht. It is a very big and fancy boat. Some people live on yachts and travel around the world," mom said.

"Wow, can we go on the yacht?" Ben asked.

"No, sweetie, we can't. The yacht belongs to someone else. We can only look at it from here," dad said.

Lily and Ben were a little sad. They wanted to see the yacht up close. They wondered what it was like inside. They imagined it had many rooms and toys and snacks.

Then they saw a man waving at them from the yacht. He had a big smile and a colorful hat. He shouted, "Hello, kids! Do you want to see my yacht?"

Lily and Ben looked at their mom and dad. They nodded and smiled. The man said, "Come on, I'll show you. I have a small boat that can take you to the yacht. It's very safe and fun."

Lily and Ben were very excited. They ran to the small boat with their mom and dad. The man helped them get on board. He said, "My name is Jack. I'm the owner of the yacht. I like to show it to nice people like you."

The small boat took them to the yacht. Jack showed them around. He showed them the big living room, the cozy bedrooms, the shiny kitchen, and the fun playroom. He showed them his toys, his books, his paintings, and his pets. He showed them the colorful flags, the shiny lights, and the loud horn. He showed them how to steer the yacht and how to read the maps. He showed them everything.

Lily and Ben had a wonderful time. They thanked Jack for showing them his yacht. They said, "Your yacht is amazing. You are very lucky and very kind."

Jack said, "You're welcome, kids. I'm glad you liked it. You are very sweet and very smart. Come back anytime you want."

Lily and Ben hugged Jack and said goodbye. They went back to the small boat with their mom and dad. They waved at Jack and his yacht. They said, "Bye, Jack. Bye, yacht. We'll see you again."

The end.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a big box in the garage. They use the box to make a boat. They put pillows and blankets in the box. They pretend they are sailing to an island.

They use a stick to steer the boat. They use a sheet to make a sail. They use a map to find the island. They see birds and fish and waves. They have fun on the boat. They are very intelligent.

They reach the island. They use the box to get out of the water. They use the sheet to make a tent. They use the pillows and blankets to make a bed. They use the stick to make a fire. They use the map to explore the island. They see trees and flowers and animals. They have fun on the island. They are very happy.

Anna liked to follow pigeons in the park. She wanted to touch their soft feathers and hear their cooing sounds. She ran after them with her hands out, but they always flew away. She did not give up. She wanted to make friends with a pigeon.

One day, she saw a big pigeon with a shiny ring on its leg. It looked different from the other pigeons. Anna thought it was special. She followed it to a corner of the park, where there was a big trash can. The pigeon landed on the trash can and started to peck at something.

Anna climbed on the trash can and reached for the pigeon. She grabbed its ring and pulled. The pigeon squawked and bit her finger. Anna cried out and let go of the ring. She looked at her finger and saw blood. It hurt a lot.

She wanted to run back to her mom, but she did not know where she was. She was lost. She looked around and saw no one. She was scared. She started to cry louder.

The pigeon flew away and left Anna alone. It did not care about her. It only wanted the sour food in the trash can. Anna wished she had never followed the pigeon. She wished she had stayed with her mom. She wished she had a friend.

Sam and Mia were playing with their dad's tools. They wanted to repair their old dollhouse that was broken. They found a hammer and some nails in the garage.

"Look, I can fix the roof with this nail!" Sam said, holding the hammer.

"Be careful, Sam, you might hurt yourself!" Mia warned.

But Sam did not listen. He hit the nail hard with the hammer. But he missed the nail and hit his finger instead. He cried out in pain and dropped the hammer.

"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts so much!" Sam sobbed.

Mia ran to get their mom. She saw what happened and was very angry.

"What were you doing with dad's tools? You know you are not allowed to touch them!" she scolded.

She took Sam to the bathroom and put some ice on his finger. She also checked the dollhouse and saw that it was more broken than before.

"Now you have made it worse! You can't repair it with nails, you need glue and paint. And you have ruined dad's hammer too!" she said.

She took away the tools and the dollhouse and put them in a closet. She told Sam and Mia that they were not allowed to play with them anymore.

Sam and Mia felt very sorry and sad. They wished they had listened to Mia and left the tools alone. They learned that they should not play with things that are not theirs and that they should be careful with sharp and heavy things. They hoped that one day they could repair their dollhouse and make it look original again. But they knew it would take a long time and a lot of work.

Ben and Mia liked to play at the beach. They made sand castles and looked for shells. One day, they saw a big boat with a shiny anchor. They wanted to see it closer.

"Let's go to the boat," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful," Mia said.

They walked to the boat and saw a man on it. He was wearing a hat and a vest. He smiled at them.

"Hello, kids. Do you like my boat?" he asked.

"Yes, it's very nice. Can we see your anchor?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but you have to be very careful. The anchor is heavy and sharp. It can hurt you if you touch it," the man said.

He showed them the anchor. It was big and metal. It had a chain and a hook. Ben and Mia looked at it with wonder.

"Wow, it's so cool. How do you use it?" Mia asked.

"I use it to keep my boat in one place. When I want to stop, I lower the anchor into the water. When I want to go, I pull it up with a machine," the man explained.

"That's amazing. Can we help you pull it up?" Ben asked.

The man laughed. "Maybe another time. Right now, I have to go. I have some work to do. But you can come back later. I'll be available then," he said.

He encouraged them to keep playing and learning. He waved goodbye and started his boat. Ben and Mia waved back and ran to the shore. They decided to make their own anchor with sand and sticks. They had fun pretending to be sailors. They looked forward to seeing the man and his boat again.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Sara wants to go first. She runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder.

"Wait for me!" Ben says. He follows Sara to the top of the slide. He sees a sign with a question on it. It is a quiz. Ben likes quizzes. He reads the question.

"What is two plus two?" the sign says.

"Easy!" Ben says. "Two plus two is four!"

He pushes a button with the number four on it. He hears a loud noise. The slide starts to twist and turn. Ben is scared. He screams.

"Sara, help me!" he cries.

Sara looks at Ben. She sees him go down the slide. The slide is not straight. It is like a snake. It twists and bends. Sara is scared too. She does not want to go down the slide. She looks for another way down.

She sees another sign with a question on it. It is another quiz. Sara does not like quizzes. She does not know the answer.

"What is three times three?" the sign says.

Sara does not know. She guesses. She pushes a button with the number six on it. She hears a loud noise. The ladder starts to shake. Sara falls off the ladder. She lands on the ground. She feels a lot of pain. She is hurt.

"Sara, are you okay?" Ben says. He comes out of the slide. He is dizzy and dirty. He runs to Sara. He sees her cry. He sees blood on her leg. He is sad.

"I'm sorry, Sara," he says. "I should have waited for you. I should not have pushed the button. It was a bad quiz. It was a bad slide."

Sara does not answer. She cries louder. She wants her mom. She wants to go home. She does not want to play in the park anymore. She does not want to be friends with Ben anymore.

Jill and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big cave. They want to enter the cave and look for jewels. They are impatient and curious.

"Come on, Ben, let's go inside!" Jill says.

"OK, Jill, but be careful. It is dark and scary," Ben says.

They enter the cave and use a flashlight. They see many rocks and bats. They walk deeper and deeper. They hope to find jewels.

"Look, Ben, look!" Jill shouts. She points to a shiny thing on the wall. It is a jewel. It is red and sparkly.

"Wow, Jill, you found a jewel! It is so pretty!" Ben says.

They run to the jewel and try to take it. But the jewel is stuck. They pull and pull. They are impatient and greedy.

Suddenly, they hear a loud roar. It is a bear. The bear lives in the cave. The bear is angry and hungry. The bear sees Jill and Ben. The bear wants to eat them.

"Run, Jill, run!" Ben screams.

They drop the flashlight and the jewel. They run to the exit. They are scared and sorry.

They enter the park again. They are safe and relieved.

"Jill, Ben, where have you been?" their mom asks. She is worried and angry.

"We were in the cave, mom. We wanted to find jewels. But there was a bear. We are sorry, mom," Jill and Ben say.

Their mom hugs them and scolds them. She is glad and sad.

"Jill, Ben, you should never enter a cave without me. It is dangerous and foolish. You could have been hurt or lost. You don't need jewels. You have each other. You are my jewels," their mom says.

Jill and Ben nod and cry. They are sorry and happy.

They hug their mom and say, "We love you, mom. You are our jewel."

Lily and Ben love to collect things. They collect rocks, shells, leaves, and stickers. They have a big box where they keep their collections. Sometimes they trade with each other or show their friends.

One day, Lily and Ben go on a trip with their mom and dad. They drive in the car for a long time and then they stop at a hotel. A hotel is a big house where many people sleep in different rooms. Lily and Ben get to share a room with their mom and dad. They are very excited.

The hotel has a garden with many flowers and trees. Lily and Ben want to explore the garden and see what they can collect. They ask their mom and dad if they can go outside. Their mom and dad say yes, but they have to be careful and stay together. They also have to be back before dark.

Lily and Ben run outside and look around. They see many beautiful things. They see butterflies, birds, bees, and squirrels. They see roses, daisies, sunflowers, and tulips. They see pine cones, acorns, nuts, and seeds. They start to collect some of them and put them in their pockets.

Lily and Ben are very happy with their new collections. They run back to their room and show their mom and dad what they have. "These are our memories. They are more precious than any treasure or magic wand. They show us where we came from and who we love. We have to take good care of them and share them with each other," Mom said.

Tom and Lily hugged Mom and looked at the photos. They learned something new and felt happy.

The moral of the story is: Memories are more valuable than material things, and we should respect and cherish them.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw an old man walking with a cane. He looked sad and tired.

"Let's play a trick on him," Tom said. "We can spring out from behind that bush and scare him."

Lily did not think that was a good idea. She said, "No, Tom, that is not nice. He might fall or hurt himself. We should be kind to him."

But Tom did not listen. He hid behind the bush and waited for the old man to come closer. Lily stayed behind and watched.

When the old man was near the bush, Tom jumped out and shouted, "Boo!" The old man was startled and dropped his cane. He stumbled and fell to the ground.

Tom laughed and ran away. Lily ran to the old man and helped him up. She said, "I'm sorry, sir. My brother was being mean. Are you okay?"

The old man smiled and said, "Thank you, dear. You are very sweet. I'm fine, just a bit shaken. Here, take this as a reward." He gave Lily a candy from his pocket.

Lily thanked him and took the candy. She looked for Tom and saw him sitting on a bench. He looked unhappy. He had also found a candy on the ground, but it was sour and made his mouth hurt.

Lily went to him and said, "Tom, you were wrong to scare the old man. He was nice and gave me a candy. Yours is sour because you were bad. You should say sorry to him."

Tom felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "You're right, Lily. I was bad. I will say sorry to him. Maybe he will forgive me and give me a better candy."

Lily nodded and said, "That's good, Tom. Come on, let's go." They both went back to the old man and Tom apologized. The old man forgave him and gave him another candy. It was sweet and made him happy.

The twins learned a lesson that day. They learned that being kind and respectful is better than being mean and rude. They also learned that good deeds are rewarded and bad deeds are punished. They decided to be good from then on.

"Hello, Mr. Ranger," Lily said. "What is a pine seed?"

"A pine seed is what makes a pine tree grow, Lily," the man said. "If you plant it in the soil and give it water and sun, it will grow into a big and strong tree. Pine trees are very important for the forest. They give us air and shade and homes for many animals."

"Wow, that is amazing," Lily said. "Can I plant this pine seed, Mr. Ranger?"

"Sure, Lily, but you have to be careful. The pine seed is very fragile. It can break easily if you squeeze it too hard or drop it. You have to find a good spot for it, where it is not too dry or too wet, not too sunny or too shady, and not too crowded by other plants. And you have to come back and check on it often, to see how it is growing."

"OK, Mr. Ranger, I will do that," Lily said. "Thank you for telling me about the pine seed. I want to help the forest too."

She hugged the man and ran off with Max, looking for a good spot to plant her pine seed. She hoped that one day, it would grow into a beautiful pine tree.

So, Timmy's mom had an idea. She went to get some snacks and drinks and asked Timmy and his friend to come with her to the kitchen. While they were there, Timmy's mom told them that they could have the snacks and drinks, but only if they were quiet and didn't make any noise during the movie. Timmy's friend agreed and they all went back to the living room to watch the movie. It was much better without all the noise!

Lily felt sad and said, "Timmy, can I play with your toy truck too? We can take turns." 

Timmy thought about it and realized it was better to share. "Okay Lily, you can play with it first and then I'll play with it," he said with a smile. 

They both had fun playing with the toy truck together. After a while, they got tired of playing and decided to sit by the stream. The water was flowing gently and made a relaxing sound. They talked about their day and how much fun they had playing together. 

Timmy said, "Lily, I'm sorry I didn't want to share my toy truck at first. It wasn't very nice of me." 

Lily smiled and said, "That's okay Timmy. It's always better to share so we can both have fun." 

They both agreed and realized that sharing was important. They continued to sit by the stream and enjoy each other's company, even if the conversation was a bit dull.

Once upon a time, there was a crane who lived near a river. The crane was very smart and always thought of new ways to catch fish.

One day, the crane saw a big fish in the river. The fish was too big for the crane to catch with its beak. So the crane had to imagine a way to catch the fish.

The crane had an idea. It went to a nearby village and found a big jar. The crane picked up the jar with its beak and flew back to the river. The crane put the jar in the river and waited for the fish to swim into it.

The fish saw the jar and swam inside. The crane quickly grabbed the jar with its beak and flew away with the fish inside. The crane was very happy and proud of itself.

The moral of the story is that if you use your brain and imagine, you can find new ways to solve problems.

Lily was surprised that the penguin could talk. She asked, "Can you come home with me?"

The penguin replied, "I cannot come with you, but you can receive a toy penguin as a gift from me."

Lily was very happy to receive the toy penguin from the regular penguin. She hugged the toy penguin and said, "Thank you! I will take good care of him."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun and sing with the birds. One day, it started to rain and rain and rain. The rain didn't stop and soon there was a big flood. The water was everywhere and Lily's house was all wet. 

Lily's mom told her they needed to leave their house and go to a safe place. But Lily disagreed. She wanted to stay in her house and play with her toys. Her mom explained that it was not safe, but Lily was too stubborn to listen. 

The flood got worse and Lily's house started to fill up with water. She realized she was wrong and that her mom was right. She felt ignorant for not listening to her mom. From that day on, Lily learned to always listen to her mom and trust her decisions.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her pink dress and play with her red ball. One day, she went to the park to play with her ball. She met a boy named Timmy who also had a red ball.

"Can I play with your ball?" asked Lily.

"No, it's mine," replied Timmy.

Lily felt sad and wanted to play with the ball. She thought of an idea and said, "Let's play shoot the ball. If I win, I get to play with your ball."

Timmy agreed, and they started playing. Lily aimed and shot the ball, but it went too far and hit a window. The window broke, and the owner got angry.

Lily and Timmy ran away, feeling scared and guilty. Lily learned that it's not okay to shoot things that don't belong to her. The moral of the story is to always be careful and respectful of other people's things.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. Lily has a doll. Her name is Anna. Ben has a car. His name is Max.

One day, Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big dog. The dog is brown and furry. He runs to them and barks. Lily and Ben are scared. They hug their toys.

"Go away, dog!" Lily says. "You are loud and mean!"

"Leave us alone, dog!" Ben says. "You are big and scary!"

But the dog does not go away. He comes closer and closer. He sniffs Anna and Max. He licks them with his tongue. He wags his tail.

"Hey, dog!" Lily says. "Stop that! You are making Anna wet and dirty!"

"Hey, dog!" Ben says. "Stop that! You are making Max sticky and messy!"

But the dog does not stop. He picks up Anna and Max with his mouth. He runs away with them. Lily and Ben are sad. They cry.

"Anna! Max!" Lily says. "Come back! We love you!"

"Anna! Max!" Ben says. "Come back! We need you!"

They run after the dog. They want their toys back. They see a man. He is the dog's owner. He calls the dog.

"Rex! Rex!" the man says. "Drop that! Those are not your toys!"

The dog hears the man. He drops Anna and Max. He runs to the man. The man pets the dog.

"Good boy, Rex!" the man says. "You are a smart dog!"

Lily and Ben get their toys. They hug them. They are happy.

"Thank you, man!" Lily says. "You are nice!"

"Thank you, man!" Ben says. "You are kind!"

The man smiles. He says, "You're welcome, kids! I'm sorry Rex took your toys. He likes to play. He does not mean to be bad. He does not know how to care for dolls and cars. He only knows how to care for bones and balls."

Lily and Ben look at the dog. The dog looks at them. He wags his tail. He barks.

"Maybe Rex is not so loud and mean," Lily says.

"Maybe Rex is not so big and scary," Ben says.

"Maybe Rex is just a dog," they say together.

They laugh. They pet the dog. The dog licks them. They are friends.

They swing and swing until they are tired. They get off the swings and sit on the bench. They drink some water and eat some cookies.

"It is Friday, Sara," Ben says. "The calendar says so. See? It has a picture of a fish. That means Friday."

Sara nods. She knows the calendar too. She has one at home. It has different pictures for each day. She likes the pictures. They are colorful and fun.

"Ben, do you know what we are going to do tomorrow?" Sara asks.

Ben smiles. He knows what they are going to do tomorrow. He is very excited.

Sara claps her hands. She is very excited too.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a small house made of wood and a big tree with a swing. They also had a mint plant that smelled good and made their tea sweet.

One day, Lila and Ben decided to make a tea party for their toys. They set the table with cups and plates and spoons. They picked some mint leaves and put them in a pot of water. They boiled the water on the stove and poured it into the cups.

"Here you go, Mr. Bear, some mint tea for you," Lila said, giving a cup to her teddy bear. "And here you go, Mrs. Doll, some mint tea for you," Ben said, giving a cup to his rag doll.

They sat down and pretended to sip their tea. They talked to their toys and each other. They had a lot of fun.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. It was their mom, who had come home from work. She saw the stove on and the pot empty. She was very angry and scared.

"Lila and Ben, what are you doing?" she shouted. "You could have burned the house down! You could have hurt yourselves! You know you are not allowed to use the stove without me!"

Lila and Ben dropped their cups and ran to their mom. They were very sorry and scared. They hugged their mom and said, "We are sorry, mom. We wanted to make mint tea for our toys. We didn't know it was bad to use the stove."

Their mom hugged them back and said, "I know you wanted to have fun, but you have to be careful. The stove is very hot and dangerous. You could have started a fire or burned yourselves. You have to ask me before you use it, okay?"

Lila and Ben nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We will ask you next time. We love you, mom."

Their mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lila and Ben. Now, let's clean up this mess and have some real mint tea together."

The moral of the story is: You should always ask your parents before you use something that could be dangerous.

Tom and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck and Mia has a doll. Tom likes to make loud noises with his truck and Mia likes to dress up her doll.

"Vroom, vroom, beep, beep!" Tom says, moving his truck around the carpet. "My truck is fast and strong!"

"Shh, Tom, you are too loud!" Mia says, holding her doll. "My doll is calm and pretty!"

Tom does not listen to Mia. He drives his truck closer to her doll and pretends to crash into it. "Boom, boom, smash, smash!" Tom says, laughing.

"Tom, stop it!" Mia says, getting angry. "You are hurting my doll!"

Mia grabs her doll and slaps Tom's truck away. Tom does not like that. He slaps Mia's doll out of her hands. Mia does not like that. She slaps Tom's face.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom says, crying. "Mia, why did you slap me?"

"Because you slapped my doll!" Mia says, crying too.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees Tom and Mia slapping each other and their toys on the floor. She is not happy.

"Tom, Mia, what are you doing?" Mom says, picking them up. "You should not slap each other or your toys. That is not nice!"

"Sorry, Mom," Tom and Mia say, sniffling.

Mom hugs them and gives them a kiss. She tells them to say sorry to each other and to their toys. She also tells them to share and play nicely.

"Sorry, Tom," Mia says, giving him his truck.

"Sorry, Mia," Tom says, giving her his doll.

They hug and smile. They decide to play together with their toys. They make calm and happy noises. Mom smiles and watches them. She is proud of them.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the park. They saw many animals there, like birds, dogs and squirrels. One day, they saw a very old squirrel sitting on a bench. He had gray fur and a long tail.

"Hello, Mr. Squirrel," Ben said. "What are you doing?"

The squirrel looked at them and smiled. "I am pretending to be a human," he said. "I like to watch the people and listen to their stories. They are very interesting."

"Can we pretend with you?" Mia asked. "We like to pretend too."

"Of course, you can," the squirrel said. "Come and sit with me. I will tell you some of the stories I heard."

Ben and Mia sat next to the squirrel and listened. He told them about a man who traveled to many places, a woman who painted beautiful pictures, and a boy who played the guitar. They were amazed by his stories and asked him many questions.

They had so much fun that they did not notice the time. The sun was setting and their mom was calling them.

"Ben, Mia, it's time to go home," their mom said. "Say goodbye to your friend."

"Goodbye, Mr. Squirrel," Ben and Mia said. "Thank you for the stories. Can we see you again?"

"Maybe, if you come back to the park," the squirrel said. "But remember, I am only pretending to be a human. I am really a squirrel, and I have to go back to my tree."

He waved his tail and ran away. Ben and Mia waved back and followed their mom. They were happy and curious. They wondered what other stories the squirrel had to tell.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. Lily found a jar of olives and opened it. She liked olives. She took one and ate it.

"Yum, yum, olives are good," she said.

Ben saw the jar and made a face. He did not like olives. He thought they were yucky and bitter.

"Yuck, yuck, olives are bad," he said.

Lily and Ben started to argue. Lily wanted to share the olives with Ben. Ben wanted to throw the olives away.

"Olives are good, you should try one," Lily said.

"Olives are bad, I don't want one," Ben said.

They raised their voices and pushed the jar back and forth. The jar slipped from their hands and fell on the floor. The glass broke and the olives rolled everywhere.

Lily and Ben were frightened. They heard their mom coming. They knew they had made a mess and a noise. They did not want to get in trouble.

They ran to the living room and hid behind the couch. They hoped their mom would not find them.

Their mom entered the kitchen and saw the broken jar and the olives. She was angry and confused.

"Who did this?" she asked. "Lily? Ben? Where are you?"

She looked around and saw their feet sticking out from behind the couch. She walked over and pulled them out.

"Lily and Ben, what did you do?" she asked. "Why did you break the jar and waste the olives?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They were sorry and scared.

They decided to tell the truth. They said they were playing and arguing and the jar fell. They said they liked and did not like olives. They said they were sorry and they would clean up.

Their mom listened and sighed. She was not happy, but she was not too mad. She said they should not play with food and break things. She said they should not fight and yell. She said they should respect each other's tastes and choices.

She said she loved them and hugged them. She said they could help her clean up and then have a snack. She said they could have something they both liked, like cookies or apples.

Lily and Ben nodded and smiled. They said they loved her and hugged her. They said they were sorry and they would help. They said they would not fight and yell again.

They went to the kitchen and cleaned up the mess. They threw away the broken glass and the olives. They washed the pots and pans. They had a snack and shared it. They were happy and quiet.

They learned a lesson. They learned that olives are good and bad, depending on who you ask. They learned that telling the truth is better than hiding. They learned that playing nice is better than fighting. They learned that mom knows best.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Ben says. "How does it work?"

"I don't know, but it looks fun. Let's pretend we are millers and make bread," Anna says.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is Mom. She is calling them.

"Anna! Ben! Where are you? It's time to go home!"

Anna and Ben drop the tray and run to the door. They see Mom looking worried.

"Mom, we are here! We were playing in the mill. It is incredible!" Anna says.

"Thank goodness you are safe. I was looking for you everywhere. The mill is not a place to play. It is dangerous and dirty. Come on, let's go home and wash up," Mom says.

Anna and Ben follow Mom. They are sad to leave the mill, but they are happy to have seen it. They think it is the most incredible thing in the park.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toys. One day, they saw a man outside their house who had a big cart full of candy. The man said he would sell them some candy if they gave him some money.

Tim and Sam wanted some candy very much, but they did not have any money. They looked around their room and saw their toys on the floor. They thought they could sell some of their toys to the man and get some candy.

They took some of their toys and ran outside. They showed them to the man and asked him how much candy they could get. The man smiled and said he would give them a lot of candy for their toys. He took their toys and put them in his cart. He gave them a big bag of candy and told them to enjoy.

Tim and Sam were very happy. They ran back to their room and opened the bag. They took out some candy and put it in their mouths. But as soon as they tasted it, they made a face. The candy was sour and bitter. It made their tongues hurt and their stomachs ache.

They spit out the candy and looked at the bag. They saw that the candy was old and rotten. They felt sick and sad. They had sold their toys for bad candy. They wanted their toys back, but the man was gone. He had tricked them and taken their toys away.

They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had not sold their toys. They wished they had not listened to the man. They wished they had no candy. They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that some people are not nice and some things are not worth selling.

Jenny liked to play with fire. She found a box of matches in the kitchen and took them to her room. She lit one match and watched the flame. It was bright and warm and made a hissing sound. She thought it was attractive.

She lit another match and held it close to her teddy bear. The teddy bear had fur and eyes and a nose. Jenny liked her teddy bear very much. She wanted to see what would happen if she touched the match to the fur. She did not know that fire could burn things.

The teddy bear caught fire. It made a loud whistle and a bad smell. Jenny was scared and dropped the match. The fire spread to the bed and the curtains. Jenny ran out of the room and screamed for help.

Mom and Dad heard Jenny and saw the smoke. They ran to the room and saw the fire. They were angry and sad. They grabbed Jenny and took her outside. They called the firemen to put out the fire.

The firemen came with a big truck and a hose. They sprayed water on the fire and made it go away. They also made a lot of noise and mess. They asked Mom and Dad what happened. Mom and Dad told them that Jenny played with matches and started the fire. They said that Jenny was very naughty and careless.

Tom likes to polish his cactus. He has a small cactus in a pot on his window. He thinks it is very pretty and green. He uses a cloth to make it shine.

One day, his friend Anna comes to play. She sees the cactus and wants to touch it. She thinks it looks soft and fuzzy.

"Can I touch your cactus, Tom?" she asks.

"No, Anna, don't touch it!" Tom says. "It is not soft. It has sharp things that can hurt you. They are called spines."

But Anna does not listen. She reaches out her hand and touches the cactus. Ouch! She feels a pain in her finger. She pulls it back and sees a red drop of blood.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she cries. "Your cactus is mean, Tom! It bit me!"

Tom feels sorry for Anna. He gets a band-aid and puts it on her finger. He hugs her and says, "I'm sorry, Anna. My cactus did not mean to bite you. It is just how it protects itself. You have to be careful with it. Here, let me show you how to polish it. It likes that."

Anna stops crying and smiles. She takes the cloth from Tom and gently polishes the cactus. She sees it shine and feels happy. She says, "Your cactus is pretty, Tom. But I like you more."

Tim and Sam were playing cops and robbers in the park. Tim had a toy gun that made a loud noise when he pulled the trigger. Sam had a toy gun that was very quiet and did not make any noise at all.

"Bang, bang, bang!" Tim shouted, pretending to shoot Sam. "You're under arrest, robber!"

Sam did not like that Tim's gun was louder and more fun than his. He wanted to have Tim's gun instead of his own. He had an idea. He waited until Tim was not looking and quickly took Tim's gun from his hand. He replaced it with his own gun and ran away.

"Hey, give that back!" Tim yelled, noticing that his gun was gone. He chased after Sam, but Sam was faster. He ran to the other side of the park, where there was a big slide. He climbed up the slide and pointed Tim's gun at him.

"Ha, ha, ha!" Sam laughed. "Now I have the loud gun and you have the quiet gun!"

But Sam did not know how to use Tim's gun. He pulled the trigger too hard and the gun flew out of his hand. It landed on the ground and broke into pieces. Sam was shocked and scared. He looked at Tim, who was angry and sad.

"Look what you did!" Tim cried. "You broke my gun! That was my favorite toy!"

Sam felt very bad. He realized that he had been very mean and selfish. He wished he had not taken Tim's gun. He wished he had played nicely with him. He was very embarrassed and sorry.

"I'm sorry, Tim," Sam said. "I didn't mean to break your gun. I just wanted to try it. Can you forgive me?"

Tim looked at Sam. He saw that Sam was sincere and regretful. He remembered that Sam was his friend and that friends sometimes make mistakes. He decided to forgive him.

"It's okay, Sam," Tim said. "I forgive you. But don't ever do that again, okay? And don't touch my toys without asking me first."

"Okay, Tim," Sam said. "I promise. And I'm sorry again."

Tim and Sam hugged and made up. They decided to play something else that did not need guns. They went to the swings and had fun together. They learned a lesson about sharing and respecting each other's things. They were happy again.

One day, his mom said, "Tommy, we are going to visit grandma. She is sick and needs some quiet. Please do not bring your drum."

When they got to grandma's house, Tommy saw a big cake on the table. It had candles and frosting and sprinkles. He wanted to eat some. He asked his mom, "Mom, can I have some cake?"

His mom said, "Not now, Tommy. The cake is for grandma. She is resting in her room. We will sing happy birthday to her later. Why don't you play with your toys in the living room?"

Tommy nodded. He went to the living room. He saw a big pillow on the couch. He had an idea. He took his drum out of his backpack. He put it under the pillow. He thought he was clever. He said, "No one will see my drum. I can play it when no one is looking."

He waited for a few minutes. He looked around. He did not see his mom or dad or sister. He lifted the pillow. He grabbed his drum. He started to bang it loud and fast.

But he did not know that grandma's room was next to the living room. He did not know that grandma heard his drum. He did not know that grandma was very angry.

Grandma came out of her room. She saw Tommy with his drum. She said, "Tommy, what are you doing? How dare you make so much noise? Don't you know I am sick and need some quiet? You are very rude and selfish. Give me that drum right now!"

Tommy was scared. He dropped his drum. He said, "I'm sorry, grandma. I just wanted to play. I did not mean to hurt you."

Grandma picked up his drum. She said, "You should have listened to your mom. She told you not to bring your drum. You should have respected her and me. You are not independent. You are dependent on us. We love you and want you to be happy. But you also need to follow the rules and be polite. Do you understand?"

Tommy nodded. He said, "Yes, grandma. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you too."

Grandma hugged him. She said, "It's okay, Tommy. I forgive you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will not play your drum in the house again. You can play it outside or in the garage. But not in the house. Do you promise?"

Tommy promised. He said, "I promise, grandma. I will not play my drum in the house again. I will play it outside or in the garage. But not in the house."

Grandma smiled. She said, "Good. Now, let's go and have some cake. It's my birthday, after all. And I want to share it with you. You are my special grandson. And I am proud of you."

Ben and Lily smiled and ran to the tree. They climbed up and up, until they reached a big branch. They saw something round and brown on the branch. It was a nest!

"Look, Lily, a nest!" Ben said. "Maybe there are birds inside."

Lily nodded. "Let's see. Maybe we can say hello to them."

They moved closer to the nest. They heard some chirping sounds. They peeked inside the nest. They saw four small birds with yellow feathers. The birds looked at them with big eyes.

"Hello, birds!" Lily said. "We are Ben and Lily. We are your friends."

The birds nodded. They seemed friendly. They chirped some more.

"Hello, Ben and Lily!" Mom said from below. "It's time to go home. Come down now."

Ben and Lily nodded. They waved goodbye to the birds.

"Bye, birds!" Ben said. "We will come back and visit you again."

"Bye, birds!" Lily said. "You have a nice nest."

They climbed down the tree and ran to Mom. They told her about the birds and the nest. Mom smiled and hugged them.

"You had a fun adventure today," Mom said. "But now it's time for a regular nap. You must be tired."

Ben and Lily nodded. They were tired, but happy. They had made some new friends in the park.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with clay. They made animals, houses, and cars with the clay. One day, Lily saw a new color of clay in the art room. It was shiny and sparkly, like a star. Lily wanted to use it, but it was not hers. It belonged to Miss Rose, the art teacher.

Lily asked Ben, "Can I borrow the star clay? I want to make a necklace for my mom."

Ben said, "No, Lily. You can't borrow it. It is not ours. Miss Rose will be angry if we take it."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She thought Miss Rose would not notice. She took the star clay and hid it in her pocket. She went to the playground with Ben and made a necklace with the star clay. It was very pretty.

But when they came back to the art room, Miss Rose was looking for the star clay. She asked the children, "Who took my star clay? I need it for a special project."

Lily felt afraid. She knew she did something bad. She did not want to tell the truth. She hoped Miss Rose would not find out.

But Miss Rose saw the necklace around Lily's neck. She said, "Lily, did you take my star clay?"

Lily felt ashamed. She nodded and said, "Yes, Miss Rose. I'm sorry. I wanted to make a necklace for my mom. I thought you would not mind."

Miss Rose said, "Lily, I do mind. You should not take things that are not yours. That is called stealing. You should ask before you borrow something. And you should return it when you are done. How would you feel if someone took your clay without asking?"

Lily said, "I would feel sad and angry. I'm sorry, Miss Rose. I won't do it again. Can I give you back the star clay?"

Miss Rose said, "Yes, Lily. You can give me back the star clay. And you can also give me the necklace. You can make another one with your own clay. And you can also say sorry to Ben. He tried to stop you, but you did not listen to him."

Lily said, "Okay, Miss Rose. I'm sorry, Ben. You were right. I should not have taken the star clay."

Ben said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. But next time, please listen to me. And please ask before you borrow something."

Lily and Ben hugged and made up. They learned a lesson about borrowing and stealing. They decided to be more careful and respectful with other people's things.

He hopped and hopped until he came to a dark cave. He wondered what was inside. He wanted to see. He hopped into the cave, but it was very dark and cold. He could not see anything. He felt scared.

"Hello? Is anyone here?" he croaked.

"Yes, I am here," a voice said. It was a big snake. He lived in the cave. He was hungry and mean. He saw the little frog and licked his lips.

"Who are you?" the frog asked.

"I am your friend," the snake lied. "Come closer, I want to talk to you."

The frog was not very smart. He believed the snake. He hopped closer to the voice. He did not see the snake's teeth and eyes.

The snake opened his mouth and bit the frog. He swallowed him in one gulp. He was very happy. He had a good meal.

The frog was gone. He did not hop anymore. He did not see anything anymore. He was inside the snake's belly. He was very sad. He had a bad end.

One day, Lily's mom had a surprise for her. She showed her a new mixer that she bought. It was shiny and modern. It had many buttons and lights. Lily's mom said, "This is our new mixer. It can do many things. It can mix, whip, knead, and blend. Do you want to try it?"

Lily looked at the new mixer. She felt scared. She liked the old mixer. It was simple and familiar. She said, "No, thank you. I don't want to use the new mixer. I want to use the old mixer."

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "I understand. You are used to the old mixer. But sometimes, it is good to try new things. You might like them. Why don't you give the new mixer a chance? I will help you. We can make a cake together. Will you accept that?"

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they decided to be soldiers and march around the house. They wore their dad's hats and used empty bottles as guns. They made loud noises and saluted each other.

"Ready, soldier?" Ben asked Lily.

"Yes, sir!" Lily said.

They marched into the kitchen, where their mom was making lunch. She smiled and said, "Hello, soldiers. What are you doing?"

"We are on a mission, mom," Ben said. "We have to find the enemy and capture them."

"Who is the enemy?" mom asked.

Ben pointed at the cat, who was sleeping on the couch. "That's the enemy. He is a spy. We have to sneak up on him and shoot him with our bottles."

Lily nodded and followed Ben. They tiptoed to the living room, where the cat was still napping. They raised their bottles and aimed at the cat.

"Ready, aim, fire!" Ben shouted.

They threw their bottles at the cat, but they were clumsy and missed. The bottles hit the lamp and the vase, and they both fell and broke. The cat woke up and hissed. He jumped off the couch and ran away.

Mom heard the crash and came to the living room. She saw the mess and the scared cat. She was angry and said, "What have you done, soldiers? You broke the lamp and the vase. You scared the cat. You are in big trouble."

Lily and Ben felt sorry and said, "We are sorry, mom. We were just playing. We didn't mean to break anything."

Mom sighed and said, "I know you were playing, but you have to be careful. You can't throw things in the house. You can't hurt the cat. You have to clean up this mess and apologize to the cat. And no more playing soldiers today."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom."

They picked up the pieces and threw them in the trash. They found the cat and said, "We are sorry, cat. We didn't mean to scare you. You are not the enemy. You are our friend."

The cat meowed and licked their faces. They hugged the cat and said, "We love you, cat."

Mom smiled and said, "That's better, soldiers. Now, come and have some lunch."

They marched to the kitchen and ate their sandwiches. They learned their lesson and decided to play something else next time.

The girl ran the anchor back to her boat and threw it into the sea. It made a big splash! She watched as the anchor dug deep into the ocean floor and held her boat in place. The anchor was strong enough to handle the harsh winds and the brave girl was safe.

The girl smiled and said, "Thank you, anchor, for saving me today".

Milly had an idea and she looked around the area until she found a big, round log. She smiled and said, "That's it! I'll roll the log over to the break and use it as a bridge. Thank you, bird!"

Milly rolled the log right onto the break and made a bridge that she could walk across. And sure enough, she was safe on the other side. 

Milly squealed with joy, "I did it!"

The bird smiled and said, "Good job Milly. Any problems can be solved if you just think hard enough!"

Suddenly, there was a loud, cheeping noise. It was a bird! The smelly feather and the bird got together and played. They both had lots of fun jumping around in the grass.

Soon after, four more birds joined in. They all looked the same, but were different sizes. All the birds united, and the lonely smelly feather was very happy.

The birds all laughed, chirped and flew around the farmyard. The smelly feather was very proud to be a part of the bird group. Even though it was smelly, the birds all accepted it.

And they all stayed friends forever.

The cashier smiled. "That's very sweet of you. I'm sure she will love it!" She took the spell book, told him the price, and Ted went to the counter to pay. When he went home, he gave his mom the spell book and said, "This spell is for you." His mom thanked him, gave him a hug and said, "Thank you, my young boy." Ted smiled and was very happy.

Once upon a time there was a bunny. He liked carrots a lot and decided to go for an adventure. He hopped along until he reached a big hill. On top of the hill, he saw a cave. It was dark and dangerous, so he decided to go back and find his friends.

He asked the two turtles if they wanted to explore the cave with him. The turtles were scared and said no. The bunny was sad and not sure what to do. Then he saw a bird up in a tree.

The bunny asked the bird, "Will you come with me to the cave?"
The bird replied, "Of course!"

He recommended that they bring a flashlight so they could safely explore the cave. With the light, they could see everything and make sure it was safe. The bunny and the bird ventured into the cave together.

At the top of the cave, they found the most wonderful sight. A huge field of carrots! The bunny was delighted and offered the bird some of the carrots. The bird was thankful and they both ate.

They were so happy that the bunny recommended exploring the dangerous cave to the bird. From then on, the bunny and the bird were the best of friends.

One day, Slithery noticed something strange. Someone had come to the lake and they had designed something. It was a harmless bridge stretching across the middle of the lake. Slithery was very curious, so he decided to try it out.

The bridge was made of smooth stones, and Slithery glided across them until he reached the other side. He looked around, amazed at what he saw. The bridge allowed him to explore the parts of the lake he had never seen before.

But what was it for? Slithery thought and thought, wondering why someone had designed the bridge.

Just then, he heard a voice coming from the other side. "Hey, you! What are you doing?"

It was a little boy, waving from the other side of the lake. He smiled at Slithery, and then explained.

"I designed this bridge so that my friends and I could get over the lake. Now we can explore more of the lake, and even swim around together! Isn't it fun?"

Slithery smiled. He suddenly understood why the bridge was so harmless. It was meant for friendly exploration.

"Maybe the key goes in here," said Tom. He put the key in the hole and turned it. It clicked.

"We were sorry, Mom," said Tom and Anna. "We were just playing. We wanted to cook a potato, but we locked it."

You can enjoy music with others. That is what makes music beautiful. That is what makes you humble. Being humble means you are not proud or selfish. You are thankful and generous. You are happy and friendly. Do you understand?"

Sara thought for a moment. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I am sorry. I was not humble. I was proud and selfish. I will wash my hands. And I will share my piano with Lily. I will be kind and humble. I will enjoy music with others."

Sara's mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Sara. I am proud of you. Now, go and wash your hands. And then, invite Lily to play the piano with you. I am sure she will be happy. And you will be happy too."

Sara did as her mom said. She washed her hands. She went to Lily. She said, "Lily, I am sorry. I was not nice to you. Do you want to play the piano with me? I will teach you some songs. And you can teach me some songs. We can have fun together."

Lily smiled. She said, "Yes, Sara. I would love to play the piano with you. Thank you for sharing. You are a good friend."

Sara and Lily played the piano together. They learned from each other. They taught each other. They had fun together. They enjoyed music together. They were humble and happy.

"Let's test the refrigerator," Lily said. "Maybe we can find some yummy food."

"Okay," Ben said. "But we have to be careful. Mommy said we should not open the refrigerator too much."

"Wow," Lily said. "Look at all the food. Can we have some?"

"Sure," Ben said. "But we have to be quick. We don't want the refrigerator to get warm."

Mommy heard the noise. She came to the kitchen and saw the open refrigerator. She saw Lily and Ben eating the food. She was not happy.

"Lily and Ben, what are you doing?" Mommy asked. "You are wasting the food and the energy. You are making the refrigerator work too hard. You are not supposed to test the refrigerator like that."

"Mmm, this is delicious!" Jen said.

Tim and Tom were two goats who lived on a farm. They liked to eat hay every day, but they were not happy. They wanted to see the world and have fun. One day, they saw a hole in the fence and ran away.

They ran and ran until they came to a big forest. They saw many wild animals there, like bears and wolves and foxes. They were scared, but they also wanted to play. They saw some hay on the ground and started to eat it. But it was not good hay. It was old and dry and had thorns in it. It hurt their mouths and made them thirsty.

They looked for water, but they could not find any. They were lost and hungry and tired. They wished they were back on the farm, where the farmer provided them with fresh hay and water and a warm barn. They realized they had been foolish and ungrateful. They decided to go back and say sorry to the farmer.

They walked and walked until they found the fence. They saw the hole and tried to squeeze through it. But they had grown bigger and fatter from eating the hay. They could not fit. They were stuck. They cried and cried for help.

The farmer heard them and came to see. He saw the two goats and shook his head. He said, "You silly goats, you ran away from your home and your food and your safety. You wanted to be wild, but you did not know the dangers. You learned a hard lesson today. But I am glad you are alive and sorry. I will help you get out and take you back to the barn. But you must promise me to never run away again."

The two goats nodded and said, "We promise, we promise. Thank you, farmer, for providing us with everything we need. We are sorry for being wild and greedy. We will be good and happy goats from now on."

The farmer smiled and cut the fence. He freed the two goats and led them back to the barn. He gave them fresh hay and water and a hug. The two goats felt warm and cozy and loved. They learned to appreciate what they had and to be content. They never ran away again.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big pumpkin growing on a vine. They wanted to pick it and make a pie.

"Let's get the pumpkin, Tom!" Lily said.

"OK, Lily!" Tom said.

They ran to the pumpkin and tried to pull it off the vine. But it was too heavy and stuck. They pulled and pulled, but it did not move.

"Hey, what are you doing?" a voice said.

They looked up and saw a scarecrow standing next to the pumpkin. He had a straw hat, a plaid shirt, and a mean face.

"This is my pumpkin!" the scarecrow said. "You can't have it! Go away!"

The twins were scared and angry. The scarecrow was very rude. He did not share his pumpkin.

"No, it's not your pumpkin!" Lily said. "It's ours! We want to make a pie!"

"Yeah, we want to make a pie!" Tom said.

They pulled harder on the pumpkin, but the scarecrow pushed them away.

"Stop it, stop it!" the scarecrow said. "You are hurting the pumpkin! Leave it alone!"

He grabbed a bucket of water and threw it at the twins. The water soaked them from head to toe. They were wet and cold.

"Hey, that's not nice!" Lily said.

"That's not fair!" Tom said.

They ran away from the scarecrow and the pumpkin. They went back to the house and told their mom what happened.

Their mom was not happy. She went to the garden and talked to the scarecrow. She told him that he was very rude and that he should share his pumpkin with the twins. She also told him that he should not soak them with water.

The scarecrow felt sorry. He did not mean to be rude. He just loved his pumpkin very much. He did not want to lose it.

He said he was sorry to the mom and the twins. He said he would share his pumpkin with them. He said he would help them make a pie.

The mom and the twins were glad. They thanked the scarecrow and hugged him. They picked the pumpkin together and carried it to the house. They made a delicious pie and ate it with the scarecrow. They became friends and played in the garden. They were happy.

The zookeeper said, "I'm glad you learned your lesson. But you are lucky. The tiger was wise and did not hurt you too much. He could have killed you. He only wanted to warn you and teach you a lesson. He is a wise tiger. You should be a wise boy."

Tom nodded and thanked the zookeeper. He hugged his mom and dad and said, "I love you. Thank you for taking me to the zoo. But I will never touch a tiger again. I will only look at him and admire him from far away."

The end.

Timmy got upset and started to cry. His mom came into the room and saw what was happening. She picked up the cat and put it outside. Then she gave Timmy a hug and told him that he could keep his toys all to himself. Timmy was happy again and went back to playing on his rug. The end.

Mia and Ben felt sad and angry. They did not like how Max was so selfish and mean. They decided to teach him a lesson. They waited until Max was not looking and grabbed the toy car. They ran outside and hid it behind a bush.

Max noticed that his toy car was gone. He looked everywhere for it. He could not find it. He started to cry and scream. He wanted his toy car back. He did not know what to do.

Mia and Ben watched him from the window. They felt sorry for him. They realized that they were not being nice either. They decided to give him back his toy car. They came out and said they were sorry. They asked him if he wanted to play with them.

Max saw his toy car and felt happy. He said he was sorry too. He said he wanted to share his toy car and play with them. He learned that it was more fun to be kind and generous than to be spoiled and lonely. They all became friends and played together.

Lily and Ben love to play pirates. They have a big box that they pretend is a ship. They wear hats and scarves and say "Arrr!" They also have a hook that Ben's dad made for them. It is not a real hook, but a plastic one that fits over Ben's hand.

One day, they decide to go on a treasure hunt. They make a map with crayons and paper. They draw an X where the treasure is. They say the treasure is rich and shiny and has many coins and jewels. They hide the map under the box and start to sail.

They sail across the living room, the kitchen, and the hallway. They have to watch out for sharks and crocodiles and other pirates. They use their hook and their swords to fight them off. They have a lot of fun.

They finally reach the X on the map. It is in Ben's sister's room. They sneak in and look for the treasure. They see a big chest with a lock on it. They think that is where the treasure is. They try to open it, but it is too hard.

"Maybe we need a key," Lily says.

"Or maybe we can use the hook," Ben says. He puts the hook in the lock and tries to turn it. He pushes and pulls and twists and turns. He hears a click.

"Yay, we did it!" he says. He opens the chest and looks inside.

But there is no treasure. There is only a lot of pink and purple stuff. There are dolls and dresses and ribbons and bows. There are no coins and jewels.

"Aw, this is not treasure," Ben says. "This is boring."

Lily looks at the stuff and smiles. She picks up a doll and a dress. She likes them. She thinks they are pretty.

"I think this is treasure," she says. "This is fun."

Ben looks at Lily and frowns. He does not like the stuff. He does not think they are pretty. He thinks they are silly.

He takes the hook out of the lock and puts it back on his hand. He says "Arrr!" and walks out of the room. He does not want to play pirates with Lily anymore.

Lily shrugs and stays in the room. She does not care. She has a new treasure. She plays with the doll and the dress. She says "Yay!" and smiles. She still loves to play pirates, but she also loves to play princesses.

Lily likes to run fast. She likes to speed on the grass, on the road, and on the track. She is very fit and strong. She can run faster than most of her friends.

One day, Lily has a race at school. She is very excited. She wants to win the race and get a medal. She puts on her shoes and her shirt with a number. She goes to the start line with the other kids.

The teacher blows a whistle. Lily runs as fast as she can. She speeds past the other kids. She is in the lead. She sees the finish line. She is almost there.

But then, she sees something on the ground. It is a note. It is pink and has a heart on it. Lily is curious. She slows down and picks up the note. She opens it and reads it.

It says: "Lily, you are the best. I like you a lot. Will you be my friend? From, Ben."

Lily smiles. She likes Ben. He is in her class. He is nice and funny. She looks up and sees Ben waving at her. He is at the finish line. He has a medal around his neck.

Lily runs to Ben. She gives him the note and a hug. She says: "Yes, I will be your friend. You are the best, too."

They both laugh and hold hands. They don't care who won the race. They are happy. They have each other.

One day, they want to play with the lion suit. But there is only one lion suit. They both want to be the lion. They pull the suit from each other. They split the suit in two. The suit is broken. They are sad and mad.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lila had a shiny diamond necklace that she got from her grandma. Ben had a big truck that he got from his dad. They were having fun, but they wanted to play together.

"Can I play with your diamond necklace?" Ben asked Lila.

"OK, but you have to be careful. It is very special and pretty," Lila said.

"Can I play with your truck?" Lila asked Ben.

"OK, but you have to be strong. It is very heavy and fast," Ben said.

They swapped their toys and tried to play with them. But they soon found out that they did not like them very much. The diamond necklace was too tight and scratchy for Ben. The truck was too loud and hard for Lila.

They looked at each other and felt sad. They wanted to play with their own toys again.

"Can we switch back?" they both asked at the same time.

They nodded and gave each other their toys. They felt happy again.

"Let's play together with both our toys," Lila suggested.

"OK, how?" Ben asked.

"We can pretend that the truck is a treasure hunter and the diamond necklace is the treasure. We can hide it and find it and share it," Lila said.

"That sounds fun. Let's do it," Ben agreed.

They started to play their new game. They hid the diamond necklace under a pillow, behind a curtain, or in a shoe. They used the truck to drive around and look for it. They made noises and talked to each other.

"Vroom, vroom, I am the treasure hunter. I will find the shiny treasure," Ben said.

"Shh, shh, I am the treasure. I am hiding from the treasure hunter. He will never find me," Lila said.

They had a lot of fun playing together. They did not notice that their mom was watching them from the kitchen. She smiled and thought that they were very clever and creative. She was glad that they learned to include each other and share their toys. She did not mind that they made a mess. She was proud of them.

She also thought that their dad was very lazy. He was lying on the couch, snoring and holding the remote. He did not help her with the dishes or the laundry. He did not play with the kids or talk to her. He only watched TV and slept.

She decided to wake him up and ask him to do some chores. She took the remote from his hand and turned off the TV. She said in a loud voice:

"Hey, lazy bones, it's time to get up and help me. The kids are playing with a diamond and a truck. What are you doing?"

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys in their room, but sometimes they wanted to explore other places in their house. One day, they decided to crawl to the kitchen, where their mom was making lunch.

"Look, Ben, there are many things in the kitchen!" Lily said, pointing to the pots, pans, spoons and knives. "Can we touch them?"

"No, Lily, mom said they are not for us. They are hot or sharp and can hurt us. We can only look at them." Ben said, shaking his head.

"But what is that?" Lily asked, seeing a big jar on the counter. It was filled with colorful candies that sparkled in the light. "Can we have some?"

Ben's eyes widened as he saw the jar. He loved candies and wanted to taste them. He forgot what mom said and crawled to the counter. He tried to reach the jar, but it was too high for him.

"Ben, come back! Mom will be angry if she sees us!" Lily cried, feeling scared.

But Ben did not listen. He climbed on a chair and stretched his arm. He touched the jar, but it was too heavy for him. He pulled it, but it slipped from his hand and fell to the floor. It broke into many pieces and the candies scattered everywhere.

"Ben, what have you done?" Mom said, hearing the noise and coming to the kitchen. She saw the mess and the twins. She was not happy.

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted some candies." Ben said, looking down.

"You know you are not allowed to go to the kitchen without me. You could have hurt yourself or your sister. And you wasted the candies I bought for your birthday. You are very naughty, Ben." Mom said, picking up the broken jar and the candies.

"I'm sorry, mom. I won't do it again." Ben said, feeling sorry.

Mom sighed and hugged him. She was not too angry, because she loved him. She loved Lily too, who was crying in the corner. She hugged her too and kissed them both.

"It's okay, my loves. I forgive you. But you have to be more careful and listen to me. The kitchen is not a place for you to play. And you have to share the candies with your friends, not eat them all by yourself. Do you understand?" Mom said, smiling.

"Yes, mom. We understand." Ben and Lily said, nodding.

Mom took them to their room and gave them each a candy. They thanked her and said they loved her. They ate their candies and played with their toys. They did not crawl to the kitchen again. They learned their lesson. They were modest and happy twins.

Sam felt scared. He did not want to help the man. He wanted his car back. He tried to run away, but the man grabbed him and said, "No, you can't go. You have to stay and stir the pot until it is done. Then you can have your toy. But if you stop stirring, the soup will explode and hurt you."

Sam cried and shouted for help. He wished he had not traded his car. He wished he had listened to Ben. He wished he had not followed the mysterious man.

Ben heard Sam's cries and ran to the alley. He saw the man and the pot and the toys. He was brave and threw a rock at the man. The man let go of Sam and chased Ben. Sam ran to Ben and they escaped. The man was angry and threw the pot at them, but it missed and hit the wall. The pot broke and the soup spilled. It was not magic, it was just mud and garbage.

The knight took the sword in his hands and was filled with courage. He was ready to fight. He stepped outside the castle and faced the enemy. He held up the sword, ready to battle.

The enemy saw the sword and was scared. He ran away as fast as he could. The knight was victorious!

The sword was proud of the knight and said, "I reminded you that you could be brave. That made you strong enough to defeat the enemy."

The knight smiled and thanked the sword for reminding him of his courage.  He kept the sword with him so that it could always remind him of how brave he really was.

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Ted and Tim. 
Ted and Tim loved to play soccer together. They would score points and laugh each time one of them made a goal. 
But one day, Ted felt jealous because he wasn't scoring as much as Tim. He started to get selfish and take the ball away from his brother. 
Tim noticed the change in Ted's behaviour and asked him, "What is wrong? Why are you being selfish?"
Ted frowned and replied, "I just want to be the one to score all the points. I want to be the best."
Tim shook his head. "Scoring more doesn't mean you are better. We can play soccer together and serve each other. That's what being a good brother is all about."

Ted heard his brother's wise words and felt ashamed of being so selfish. From that day on, whenever they would play soccer, Ted would pass the ball to Tim when it was his turn. They would both score points and have great fun. 

Ted had learned an important lesson that day: sometimes you have to let go of your selfishness and serve others.

He was angry and mean and always tried to make the other prince feel bad. He said things like, "You are not a real prince, you are just a shooter. You have no friends, no fun, no crown. You are boring and silly."

One day, the envious prince had a plan. He waited until the shooter prince was out in the woods, practicing his shooting. He followed him quietly and hid behind a tree. He saw the shooter prince take out an arrow from his bag and put it on his bow. He aimed at a bird on a branch. He was about to shoot when the envious prince jumped out and shouted, "Boo!"

The shooter prince was startled and missed his shot. The arrow flew past the bird and hit a bee hive. The bees came out and buzzed angrily. They saw the shooter prince and the envious prince and thought they were enemies. They stung them all over their faces and arms and legs. The princes screamed and ran away, but the bees followed them.

They ran back to the castle, but the guards did not recognize them. They saw two boys covered in red bumps and swollen eyes and thought they were thieves or spies. They grabbed them and locked them in a dark dungeon. They said, "You will stay here until the king comes and decides what to do with you. You are in big trouble."

The shooter prince and the envious prince were very sad and sorry. They wished they had been nicer to each other and not played with arrows and bees.
