When he got to the car, he saw a little boy sitting in the driver's seat and he asked, "What are you doing?" The little boy answered, "I'm sending a horn." The owl could not believe what he heard.

The wise owl gave the little boy some advice. He said, "Sending horns is not very nice. You should use your time and energy in better ways, like helping your family or playing with your friends."

The little boy thanked the wise owl and promised never to send another horn again. He learnt his lesson and has been a much better person ever since. The wise owl was proud of the little boy and the moral he had learnt.

The coin made Jill very excited. She thought that one day, she could perhaps use it to buy something special.

Lila looked at Ben's bone. It was different from her bone. It was not big or long or hard. It was not a real bone. She thought it was silly and laughed. She said, "That is not a bone. That is a toy. My bone is better. It is a real bone. It is big and tasty and strong."

Ben was hurt. He did not like Lila's laugh. He did not think his bone was silly. He liked his bone. It was a gift from his human. He said, "My bone is not a toy. It is a special bone. It is a whistle. It makes a sound when I blow it. Like this." He put his bone in his mouth and blew. It made a loud and funny noise.

Lila was surprised. She had never heard a bone make a sound before. She wondered how Ben did that. She was curious and wanted to try it. She said, "Can I see your bone? Can I blow it too?"

Ben smiled. He was glad that Lila was interested in his bone. He said, "Sure, you can see my bone. You can blow it too. But you have to share your bone with me. Can I see your bone? Can I chew it too?"

Lila thought for a moment. She liked her bone, but she also wanted to play with Ben's bone. She decided to share. She said, "Okay, you can see my bone. You can chew it too. But you have to be careful. It is hard and sharp. Do not hurt your teeth."

Ben nodded. He was careful with Lila's bone. He chewed it gently and tasted it. He said, "Your bone is good. It is crunchy and meaty. Thank you for sharing."

Lila smiled. She was happy with Ben's bone. She blew it loudly and made it sound. She said, "Your bone is fun. It is noisy and funny. Thank you for sharing."

They both laughed and played with each other's bones. They found out that they had more in common than they thought. They both liked to run and chase and dig and fetch. They became friends and did not care that they were different. They belonged together.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to fish. They went to the pond with their rods and buckets. They wanted to catch the biggest fish they could.

"Look, I got one!" Tim shouted, as he pulled a fish out of the water. He put it in his bucket and smiled. "It is very big and shiny. I will measure it later."

Sam was happy for Tim, but he also wanted to catch a big fish. He tried harder and harder, but he only caught small fish. He put them in his bucket, but he was not satisfied.

"Tim, can I see your fish?" Sam asked, as he walked over to Tim's bucket. "Maybe I can learn from you."

"Sure, here it is," Tim said, as he lifted his fish out of the bucket. He was proud of his catch.

But Sam was clumsy. He tripped over a rock and bumped into Tim. The fish slipped out of Tim's hands and fell back into the pond. It swam away quickly.

"Oh no!" Tim cried, as he watched his fish disappear. "That was my biggest fish ever! Why did you do that, Sam?"

"I'm sorry, Tim, I'm sorry!" Sam said, as he felt bad. "I didn't mean to. I was just curious. Please forgive me."

Tim was angry and sad. He wanted to yell at Sam, but he remembered that Sam was his friend. He knew that Sam was sorry and that it was an accident. He decided to be kind and forgive Sam.

"It's okay, Sam, it's okay," Tim said, as he hugged Sam. "You are still my friend. We can fish again another day. Maybe we will catch an even bigger fish."

Sam was grateful and relieved. He hugged Tim back and thanked him. He learned that he should be more careful and respectful. He also learned that friendship was more important than fish.

The moral of the story is: Be kind and forgive your friends when they make mistakes. Friendship is more valuable than anything.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. But their favorite was the gorilla. The gorilla was big and black and had a funny face.

"Look, mom, look!" Ben said, pointing at the gorilla. "He is eating a banana!"

"Yes, he is, Ben," mom said. "Gorillas love bananas. They are good for them."

Lily wanted to see the gorilla too. She ran to the fence, but she was too slow. The gorilla finished his banana and threw the peel away. Then he walked to the other side of his cage, where there was a tire swing.

"Wait, gorilla, wait!" Lily shouted. "I want to see you play!"

The gorilla heard Lily and turned his head. He saw her waving and smiling. He felt curious and friendly. He walked back to the fence, slowly and gently. He reached out his hand and touched Lily's hand.

"Hello, gorilla, hello!" Lily said, giggling. "You are so soft and warm!"

"Hello, Lily, hello!" the gorilla said, in his own way. He made a grunting sound and nodded his head.

Ben and mom joined Lily and the gorilla. They all looked at each other and smiled. They felt happy and safe. They had made a new friend.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big plane that could fly in the air. They liked to pretend they were pilots and go on adventures.

One day, they wanted to play with the plane outside, but it was raining. They waited and waited for the rain to stop, but it did not. They were sad and bored. They decided to play with the plane inside, but they had to be careful not to break anything.

They took turns flying the plane around the room, making noises and stories. Tom flew the plane first, and then gave it to Lily. Lily flew the plane next, and then gave it back to Tom. They did this for a while, and had fun.

But then, they started to get competitive. They wanted to fly the plane longer and higher and faster than the other. They did not want to share anymore. They began to argue and fight over the plane.

"Give me the plane, it's my turn!" Tom shouted.

"No, it's mine, I want to fly more!" Lily yelled.

They pulled and tugged on the plane, until it slipped from their hands and crashed into the window. The window broke, and the plane broke too. They heard their mom coming, and they knew they were in trouble.

They looked at each other, and felt sorry. They realized they had been selfish and silly. They hugged and said sorry to each other. They also said sorry to their mom, and promised to be more careful and kind.

Their mom was angry, but also glad that they learned their lesson. She told them to help her clean up the mess, and then they could play with their other toys. She also said that when the rain stopped, they could go outside and make a new plane with paper and sticks. They agreed, and thanked their mom.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring, and fighting is not fun.

Lily liked to help her mom bake cakes. She liked to mix the flour, the eggs and the sugar in a big bowl. She liked to lick the spoon and taste the batter. She liked to watch the cakes rise in the oven and smell the sweet air.

One day, her mom said they would make a special cake with cream and strawberries. Lily was very excited. She helped her mom whip the cream until it was fluffy and white. She helped her mom wash and cut the strawberries. She helped her mom spread the cream and the strawberries on top of the cake.

But then, Lily made a mistake. She left the cake on the table and went to play with her toys. She forgot about the cake. She forgot that the cream would spoil if it was not in the fridge. She forgot that the strawberries would make the cake wet and soggy.

When her mom came back, she saw the cake and she was very sad. The cream was yellow and sour. The strawberries were mushy and brown. The cake was dry and hard. She said to Lily, "Oh, Lily, what have you done? You spoiled the cake. We can't eat it now. It's ruined."

Lily felt very sorry. She didn't mean to spoil the cake. She wanted to make her mom happy. She said to her mom, "I'm sorry, mom. I was bad. I didn't listen to you. I forgot about the cake. Can we make another one?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. Everyone makes mistakes. I'm not mad at you. I love you. Yes, we can make another cake. But this time, we have to put it in the fridge. And we have to eat it soon. Okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I love you too. Thank you for making cakes with me. They are yummy."

They smiled and went to the kitchen to make another cake. They had fun and they learned a lesson. They never spoiled a cake again.

Lily liked to make pictures with her crayons. She had many crayons of different colors. She could make flowers, animals, houses, and anything she wanted. She liked to show her pictures to her mom and dad. They always said she was a good artist.

One day, Lily ran out of paper. She looked around for something else to make pictures on. She saw a big white wall in her room. She thought it was boring. She wanted to make it more fun. She took her crayons and started to draw on the wall. She made a big rainbow, a sun, a tree, and a bird. She was very happy with her picture.

But when her mom came in, she was not happy. She saw the crayons on the wall and said, "Lily, what did you do? You can't make pictures on the wall. That's naughty. You have to clean it up." She gave Lily a wet cloth and told her to wipe the wall.

Lily was sad. She didn't mean to be naughty. She just wanted to make something nice. She tried to clean the wall, but the crayons were hard to erase. She cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't do it again."

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you like to make pictures, but you have to use paper, not the wall. Next time, ask me for more paper, okay? I love you, and I love your pictures, but not on the wall."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I love you too. Can I have more paper, please?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. Here you go. You can make as many pictures as you want, as long as you use paper."

Lily thanked her mom and took the paper. She put away her crayons and picked up her markers. She decided to make a new picture for her mom, to say sorry and to make her happy. She hoped her mom would like it. She thought it was better than the boring wall.

Lily liked to grow plants in her window. She had a pot with a long green bean plant. She watered it every day and watched it climb up a stick. She was proud of her plant.

One day, she saw a bird outside her window. It was red and blue and had a yellow beak. It was singing a pretty song. Lily wanted to talk to the bird. She opened her window and said, "Hello, bird. Do you like my plant?"

The bird flew closer and looked at the plant. It said, "Yes, I do. It is very long and green. Can I have a taste?"

Lily was surprised. She did not want the bird to eat her plant. She said, "No, bird. This is my plant. I grew it with water and sun. You can look, but you cannot eat."

The bird was sad. It said, "But I am hungry. And your plant looks yummy. Please, can I have a little bit?"

Lily thought for a moment. She liked the bird, but she loved her plant. She said, "How about this? You can have one bean, but only one. And you have to sing me another song."

The bird agreed. It picked one bean from the plant and ate it. It said, "Thank you, Lily. That was very good. And here is your song." It sang a beautiful song for Lily. Lily smiled and clapped her hands.

They became friends. The bird came back every day to visit Lily and her plant. They talked and sang and had fun. Lily was happy. She had a plant and a bird.

He asked his mom if he could go outside anyway, but she said no. She said he would get wet and cold and sick. She said he had to stay inside and play with his toys. Tommy did not want to play with his toys. He wanted to splash in the puddles.

He waited until his mom was busy in the kitchen. Then he sneaked out the door. He ran to the street and saw a huge puddle. He smiled and stepped in it. He felt the water splash on his legs and feet. He laughed and jumped in the puddle. He felt happy and free.

But then he heard his mom's voice. She was angry. She saw him from the window and came outside. She grabbed his hand and pulled him out of the puddle. Tommy was miserable again. He wished he had listened to his mom. He wished he had his boots and raincoat. He wished he could go back to the puddle. He cried and hugged his teddy bear. He hoped his mom would forgive him. He hoped it would stop raining soon.

"No, Tim, you can't keep it," Mia says. "It is not a pet. It is a wild bug. It needs to go back to its home."

"But I like it. It is my friend. Can I send it a letter?" Tim asks.

They run back to the house and have a snack. They are happy. They wonder if the bug will write back.

"Mommy, will it heal soon?" Lily asked.

"Yes, my sweetie, it will heal soon. You just need to be careful and not touch it too much. It will get better every day," Mommy said.

"Can I have a peach, Mommy? I like peaches. They are sweet and juicy and soft," Lily said.

"Of course, you can have a peach. Peaches are good for you. They have vitamins and water and fiber. They help you grow and stay healthy," Mommy said.

She washed a peach and cut it into small pieces. She put them in a bowl and gave it to Lily.

Lily smiled and ate the peach. She liked the taste and the texture. She felt a little better.

"Mommy, can you tell me a story? A story about peaches?" Lily asked.

"Sure, I can tell you a story. A story about peaches and a princess and a dragon. It is a very interesting story. Do you want to hear it?" Mommy asked.

"Yes, please, Mommy. I want to hear it. I love stories. They make me happy," Lily said.

He was very mean and cruel. The princess was very sad and scared. She ran to her room and cried. She did not know what to do. She loved her peach tree very much. Lily cried, "Ben, it is a storm. We have to go down. Now!"

Ben was scared too. He said, "OK, OK. Let's go down. Fast!"

Timmy looked up at his mom and said, "Mommy, can we cover my cars too?" His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Timmy." They covered the cars with the umbrella and continued to play in the rain. Timmy was so happy that he could still play with his cars even though it was raining.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a huge birdcage in her room with a pretty bird inside. One day, Lily's friend came to visit her and they played together.

Lily's friend asked, "What's in the big cage?"

Lily replied, "It's my birdie! Do you want to see?"

Lily's friend said, "Yes, please!" and Lily opened the cage. The birdie flew out and landed on Lily's friend's hand. 

Lily's friend said, "Wow! He looks so colorful. Can I taste him?"

Lily laughed and said, "No silly, you can't taste him! He's a birdie, not food!" 

Lily's friend giggled and said, "I know, I was just joking!" They played with the birdie for a while before it was time for Lily's friend to go home.

After the storm passed, the little girl went outside to play. She saw a toy that looked like a real dog, but it was fake. She didn't like it because it wasn't real. She wanted a real dog to protect her like her mom did during the storm.

The little girl went to her mom and said, "I want a real dog to protect me." Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, I will always protect you, even from fake dogs." The little girl felt safe and happy knowing her mom would always be there to protect her.

Once upon a time, there was a big ostrich who was very proud of his long feathers. He would strut around showing off his beautiful feathers to everyone he met. One day, a little bird came up to him and said, "Why are you so proud of your feathers? They don't make you a better ostrich."

The big ostrich got angry and pushed the little bird away. But as he did, some of his feathers fell out and he realized that he was now bald in some parts. He felt sad and ashamed of his bald spots.

The big ostrich learned that it's not good to be proud and push others away. He realized that everyone is different and special in their own way, and that it's important to be kind to others. From that day on, he stopped showing off his feathers and started being a kinder ostrich.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bear named Ben who lived on a big hill. One day, he decided to go for a walk and meet his friend, a rabbit named Lily. 

As he was walking down the hill, he stumbled and fell. "Ouch!" he cried. "Are you okay?" asked Lily, who had just arrived. "Yes, I'm okay," said Ben, "just a little clumsy today."

Lily and Ben continued walking together and talking about their day. "I saw a beautiful flower on my way here," said Lily. "Do you want to see it too?" "Yes, please!" said Ben excitedly. 

When they reached the flower, Ben was amazed by its beauty. "Wow, it's so pretty!" he exclaimed. "I'm glad I met you today, Lily. You always show me such wonderful things." "I'm happy to be your friend," said Lily with a smile. And with that, they continued their walk down the hill, enjoying each other's company.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a swamp with his friends. One day, Freddy's friend Bobby told him about a big, beautiful lily pad that he found in the swamp. Freddy didn't believe Bobby because he was being selfish and wanted the lily pad for himself.

The next day, Freddy went to find the lily pad. He searched and searched, but he couldn't find it. Suddenly, he heard a loud croak. It was Bobby, who had found the lily pad again. Bobby told Freddy that he would share it with him if he promised to never be selfish again.

Freddy felt bad for not believing Bobby and promised to be a better friend. From that day on, Freddy and Bobby shared everything they found in the swamp. They even found a new friend, a little turtle named Timmy, who they shared their adventures with. Freddy learned that it's better to be kind and share than to be selfish and miss out on all the fun.

When Timmy woke up, he felt much better. He learned that it's important to be careful about what he eats, and that sometimes things that look good on the outside can make you feel bad on the inside. From that day on, Timmy always made sure to check his food before he took a bite.

But then, Max's other friendly monkey friends came to his rescue. They all played their drums together, making even more noise than Max. Spike did not like this and ran away. Max was happy again and played his drum with his friendly friends all day long.

One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's train too. Timmy didn't want to share his train because he loved it so much. Billy said, "Can I play with your train too, Timmy?" Timmy shook his head and said, "No, I don't want to share."

Billy disagreed and said, "Sharing is good, Timmy. Let's play together." Timmy thought about it and realized Billy was right. He said, "Okay, Billy. Let's play together." Jack shrugged and said, "Sure, I could use some help."

Lily smiled and agreed. From that day on, she learned that it's not about the things you build, but the people you build them with that truly matter.

The duck and the swan played together every day. But one day, the duck became selfish and said to the swan, "I don't want to play with you anymore. I want to play with the other ducks." The swan was sad and didn't know what to do.

Then, the swan remembered something her mother had told her. "If you are not happy with something, you can change it," her mother had said. So the swan decided to change her situation. She went to the other side of the pond and found some new friends to play with.

The duck saw the swan playing with her new friends and felt bad for being selfish. She went to the swan and said, "I'm sorry for being selfish. Can we be friends again?" The swan forgave the duck and they played together happily ever after.

The boy said, "No, this is my scooter. You have your own scooter. Go away."

Tommy was angry. He thought the boy was mean. He waited until the boy was not looking. Then he ran to the fat scooter and jumped on it. He tried to ride it, but it was too heavy and hard to control. He lost his balance and crashed into a tree. He hurt his knee and his head. He cried.

The boy nodded. He said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you should be careful. My scooter is for older kids. Your scooter is better for you. You are very good at riding your scooter. Do you want to be friends?"

Tommy smiled. He said, "Yes, I want to be friends. Thank you for being nice to me. Can I help you fix your scooter?"

The boy said, "Sure, let's do it together. Maybe we can share our scooters sometimes. But only if we ask each other first."

Tommy and the boy became friends. They learned to respect each other's things and to share. They had fun riding their scooters in the park.

"I'm Remy, the magic rabbit. I live in the park and I do tricks for fun. But you are too loud and you scare away my friends. The birds, the squirrels, the bugs. They don't like noise. They like peace and quiet."

"Sorry, we didn't know," Ben said. "We just wanted to play with our cars. They are new and we like them a lot."

"I understand, but you have to be more careful. The park is not only for you, it's for everyone. And everyone has different ways of having fun. Some like to sing, some like to run, some like to hide, some like to watch. You have to respect that."

"OK, we will," Sara said. "But can you show us some of your tricks? We like magic too. It's amazing and cool."

Remy smiled. He liked to share his magic with others, as long as they were nice and polite. He nodded and waved his wand. He made a rainbow appear in the sky, a flower grow from the ground, and a balloon float from his hat. Sara and Ben clapped and cheered. They were amazed and happy.

"Wow, you are awesome, Remy!" Ben said.

"Thank you, you are very kind," Remy said. "But remember, my magic is harmless and gentle. It doesn't hurt anyone or anything. It only makes them more beautiful and joyful. That's the best kind of magic, don't you think?"

"Yes, we do," Sara said. "And we will remember that. Thank you for showing us, Remy. You are a good friend."

"You're welcome, Sara and Ben. You are good friends too. Now, let's play together, but quietly. OK?"

"OK!" Sara and Ben said. They put away their cars and joined Remy in his magic games. They had a lot of fun, but they also made a lot of peace.

Lila and Sam were friends who liked to play in the park. They saw a big tree with many branches. They wanted to climb the tree and have fun.

"Look, there is a branch that is very high. I want to go there," Lila said.

"I want to go there too. But it is too far. How can we reach it?" Sam asked.

Lila had an idea. She saw a rope that was hanging from another branch. She grabbed the rope and swung to the high branch. She was very happy.

"Wow, you did it! You are so brave and strong!" Sam said. He was envious of Lila. He wanted to be like her.

"I did it! I did it! Look at me! I am the best!" Lila said. She was very proud and boastful. She did not care about Sam.

Sam felt sad and angry. He wanted to show Lila that he could do it too. He grabbed the rope and swung to the high branch. But he was not careful. He swung too hard and missed the branch. He fell to the ground and hurt himself.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! Help me! Help me!" Sam cried. He was in pain and scared.

Lila heard Sam's cry. She looked down and saw him lying on the ground. She felt sorry and guilty. She wanted to help him. But she did not know how to get down from the high branch. She was stuck and afraid.

"Help me! Help me!" Lila cried. She was in trouble and alone.

No one heard their cries. No one came to help them. They stayed in the park until it was dark and cold. They were very unhappy.

The moral of the story is: Do not be envious of others. Do not be proud and boastful. Do not be careless and reckless. Be careful and kind. Listen to your friends. Share and help each other.

But before she could touch the fish, something else came out of the water. It was big and green and had many teeth. It was an alligator!

"Ah, an alligator!" Ben shouted, pulling Mia back.

The alligator opened its mouth and snapped at them. Ben and Mia were scared and ran away. They ran to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench.

"Mom, Dad, there's an alligator in the pond!" Ben said, panting.

"An alligator? Are you sure?" Mom asked, surprised.

"Yes, yes, we saw it! It was big and scary and tried to eat us!" Mia said, crying.

Mom and Dad hugged them and calmed them down. They looked at the pond and saw the alligator. It was a fake alligator, made of plastic and metal. It was part of a show for the park visitors. It moved and made noises with a remote control.

"Look, kids, it's not a real alligator. It's a toy. Someone is playing a trick on you," Dad said, smiling.

Ben and Mia looked again and saw a man behind a tree. He had a remote control in his hand. He was laughing.

"Hey, kids, did you like my alligator? It's just for fun. Don't be afraid," he said, waving.

Ben and Mia felt silly and angry. They did not like the trick. They did not like the man. They did not like the alligator.

They turned to their mom and dad and said, "Can we go home now? We don't want to play here anymore."

Lily looked at the muffin. It was still on the table. She said, "Me too. I'm hungry and sad."

Ben and Lily were sad. They wished they had not tried to get the muffin. They wished they had waited for their mom. They learned a lesson. But they did not like it.

The lamp was not happy. It did not like to be pulled and squeezed so hard. It wanted to be gentle and nice. So it decided to teach Jen and Ben a lesson. It made a loud noise and grew huge. It filled the whole room with bright light.

Jen and Ben were scared. They let go of the lamp and ran to the door. But the door was locked. They could not get out. They looked at the lamp and saw that it was angry. It said, "Stop fighting! Share and be kind! Or I will stay huge and bright forever!"

Jen and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, lamp. We were bad. We will share and be kind. Please shrink and be normal again."

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play outside in the snow. They had red mittens that their grandma made for them. They were very warm and soft, and they had a little string to keep them together.

One day, they decided to build a snowman in their backyard. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found a carrot for the nose, two rocks for the eyes, and a scarf for the neck. They were very proud of their snowman.

"Look, he is smiling!" Lila said.

"Yes, he is happy to be our friend!" Ben said.

They hugged their snowman and gave him a name. They called him Bob.

Suddenly, they heard a loud bark. It was their dog, Rex, who had escaped from the house. He ran towards them, wagging his tail. He saw Bob and thought he was a toy. He jumped on him and knocked him down. He bit the carrot and the rocks and the scarf. He also grabbed one of Lila's mittens with his teeth and ran away.

"Hey, stop!" Lila shouted. "That's my mitten!"

She chased after Rex, but he was too fast. He ran around the yard, shaking the mitten and making it fly in the air. He thought it was a game.

Ben followed Lila, trying to help her. He saw the mitten land on a branch of a big tree. He had an idea.

"Wait here, I'll get it!" he said.

He found a stick and threw it at the branch. He hoped the mitten would fall down. But the stick missed the branch and hit a bird's nest instead. The nest had three eggs inside. They were blue and speckled. They were rare eggs, from a rare bird.

The eggs cracked and broke. Three baby birds came out. They were wet and cold and hungry. They opened their mouths and chirped.

"Oh no!" Ben said. "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to do that!"

He felt bad for the baby birds. He wanted to help them. He looked around and saw Bob's hat. It was still on the ground, next to the snowman's head. He picked it up and ran to the tree. He climbed the tree and reached the branch. He put the hat over the nest, to keep the baby birds warm. He also gave them some of the carrot and the scarf, to feed them.

"Here you go, little ones," he said. "Don't be scared, I'm your friend."

The baby birds stopped chirping. They snuggled in the hat and ate the carrot and the scarf. They looked at Ben with their big eyes. They liked him.

Lila saw what Ben did. She smiled. She was proud of her brother. He was kind and brave.

She also saw Rex. He was tired of playing with the mitten. He dropped it on the ground and came to Lila. He licked her face and wagged his tail. He was sorry for taking her mitten.

"It's okay, Rex," Lila said. "I forgive you. You're my friend, too."

She picked up her mitten and put it back on her hand. She joined Ben on the tree. They looked at the baby birds and the snowman and the dog. They felt happy.

They had made new friends today. They had also learned a new word. They had learned what "rare" meant. It meant something that was not common, something that was special.

They thought the baby birds were rare. They thought their snowman was rare. They thought their mittens were rare. They thought their dog was rare. They thought they were rare.

They hugged each other and said, "We are rare, and we love each other."

"How do we cook it?" Tom asks.

"We need to get a pot and some water. And we need to ask Mom for help. She knows how to cook potatoes," Sue says.

They get a pot from the cupboard. They fill it with water from the tap. They ask Mom for help. Mom is in the living room. She is reading a book.

"Mom, can you help us cook a potato?" Sue asks.

"Sure, I can. I have some time available. What do you want to do with the potato?" Mom asks.

"We want to boil it and mash it. And add some butter and salt. That is yummy," Tom says.

"OK, that sounds good. Let me show you how to do it. First, we need to wash the potato and peel it. Then we need to cut it into small pieces. Then we need to put it in the pot with the water and turn on the stove. We need to wait until the water boils and the potato is soft. Then we need to drain the water and mash the potato with a fork. Then we need to add some butter and salt and mix it well. Then we can eat it," Mom says.

She helps them do all the steps. They are careful not to burn themselves. They work together as a team. Soon, they have a big bowl of mashed potato. It smells good. It looks good. It tastes good.

"Thank you, Mom, for helping us cook a potato. It is delicious," Sue says.

"You're welcome, Sue. You and Tom did a great job. I'm proud of you. You learned something new today. And you had fun," Mom says.

They hug Mom and share the mashed potato. They are happy. They are full. They love potato. They love Mom.

She saw a picture of a lion. It was yellow and brown and had a big mane. It looked strong and brave. Lily said, "Lion. Roar roar." She gasped and turned the page.

She saw a picture of a snake. It was green and black and had no legs. It looked scary and mean. Lily said, "Snake. Hiss hiss." She screamed and threw the book away.

She ran out of her room and into the living room. She saw her dad sitting on the couch. He was wearing blue pants and a red shirt. He looked calm and kind. Lily said, "Dad. Help help."

Her dad heard her cry and got up. He saw her face and hugged her. He said, "Lily. What's wrong?"

Lily pointed to her room and said, "Snake. Book. Scary."

Her dad understood and smiled. He said, "Lily. It's just a picture. It can't hurt you. Come on, I'll show you."

He took her hand and walked to her room. He picked up the book and opened it. He said, "Look, Lily. This is a snake. It's an animal that lives in the grass or the jungle. It makes a hiss sound. It's not scary. It's just different."

Lily looked at the book and at her dad. She said, "Really?"

Her dad said, "Really. And look, here are more animals. They are all different and interesting. Do you want to study them with me?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, please."

Her dad said, "Good. Let's sit on the bed and read together. You are a smart and brave girl, Lily. And I love you very much."

Lily said, "I love you too, dad. You are a loyal and kind dad."

They hugged and studied the book. They learned many names and sounds. They had fun and forgot about the snake.

Lily took the twig and poked under the rock. She was curious to see what was there. She felt something soft and furry. She gasped and pulled the twig back.

"What is it?" Tom asked. "What did you find?"

Lily looked at the twig. There was a small, gray mouse on it. It had big ears and a long tail. It looked scared and squeaked.

"A mouse!" Lily said. "It was under the rock. It's so cute!"

"Wow!" Tom said. "Can we keep it?"

They looked at the mouse. It looked at them. They smiled and laughed. They decided to make a home for the mouse with some grass and leaves. They named it Rocky and played with it until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to Rocky and left him some cheese. They hoped to see him again. They had a lot of fun with their new friend.

Lila and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to make shapes with their hands and see the shadows on the wall. They made a bird, a rabbit, a dog and a cat.

"Look, I can make a lion!" Ben said. He put his fingers together and opened his mouth wide. His shadow looked like a big, scary lion.

"Wow, that's good!" Lila said. She tried to make a lion too, but her shadow looked like a mouse. She was sad.

"Don't be sad, Lila. You can make other things. Like a flower, or a star, or a heart." Ben said. He wanted to make Lila happy.

"OK, let's make a show. We can perform for Mom and Dad. They will like it." Lila said. She smiled.

They made a show with their shadows. They told a story about a lion and a mouse who became friends. They made funny noises and movements. They had fun.

Mom and Dad came to see their show. They clapped and cheered. They said they were proud of Lila and Ben. They said their shadows were useful and creative.

Lila and Ben hugged Mom and Dad. They were happy. They liked to play with their shadows.

Ben and Jen are twins who love to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes, but their favorite ones are the red and blue ones that can make sounds and move by themselves. They need fuel to make their cars work, and they use batteries as fuel.

One day, their mom tells them that she has a surprise for them. She gives them a big box and says, "This is for you, my darlings. You can open it together and share what you find inside." Ben and Jen are very excited and curious. They thank their mom and rip off the paper from the box.

Inside the box, they see two shiny new cars that look like real ones. They are bigger and faster than their old cars, and they have lights and horns. They also see a pack of batteries and a note that says, "These are your new cars. They are very special and need a lot of fuel. Use these batteries as fuel and take good care of them. Have fun and be safe. Love, Mom."

Ben and Jen are very happy and eager to try their new cars. They each take one car and a pack of batteries and run to the backyard. They put the batteries in their cars and turn them on. They hear the engines roar and the horns beep. They are ready to race and have fun.

But soon, they start to argue and fight over who has the better car and who can go faster and farther. They do not share or take turns. They push and shove each other and their cars. They do not listen to their mom when she tells them to stop and be nice. They waste their fuel and damage their cars.

After a while, their cars stop working and their batteries run out. They try to find more fuel, but they have none left. They look at their cars and see that they are scratched and broken. They feel sad and sorry. They realize that they have been selfish and foolish. They wish they had been more careful and kind.

They go to their mom and hug her. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We did not share or take care of our new cars. We wasted our fuel and broke our cars. We were not grateful for your gift. Can you forgive us and help us fix our cars?"

Their mom smiles and kisses them. She says, "Of course, I forgive you and I love you. I am glad that you learned your lesson. Sharing and caring are more important than having and winning. You can fix your cars with some glue and tape, and I will buy you some more fuel later. But first, you have to promise me that you will play nicely and respectfully with each other and your cars from now on."

Ben and Jen nod and say, "We promise, Mom. Thank you for your gift and your help. We will share and care and have fun together. We love you, Mom." They hug their mom again and go to fix their cars. They are ready to play and enjoy their new cars in a better way.

Lily was a girl who liked to write in her diary. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her secrets. She kept her diary under her pillow and locked it with a key.

One day, Lily came home from school and found her diary on the floor. It was open and some pages were torn. She was very sad and angry. Who did this to her diary?

She saw her brother Tom in his room. He was playing with his cars. Lily went to him and asked, "Did you steal my diary?"

Tom looked at her and said, "No, I did not. Why do you think I did?"

Lily said, "Because you are always nosy and mean. You always take my things without asking. You are a bad brother."

Tom said, "That is not true. I am an honest brother. I did not touch your diary. Maybe someone else did. Maybe it was the dog or the wind or a ghost."

Lily did not believe him. She said, "You are lying. You are the only one who could do this. You are the thief. Give me back my key and say sorry."

Tom said, "I don't have your key. I don't have to say sorry. You are the liar. You are the mean sister. Go away and leave me alone."

Lily and Tom started to yell and fight. They pushed and pulled and kicked and scratched. They made a lot of noise and mess.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them fighting and their rooms in chaos. She saw Lily's diary on the floor. She was very upset and disappointed.

She said, "Stop it, both of you. What is going on here? Why are you fighting? Why is Lily's diary on the floor?"

Lily and Tom stopped fighting and looked at their mom. They both tried to explain what happened. They both blamed each other. They both said they were right and the other was wrong.

Their mom said, "Enough. I don't want to hear any more. You both need to calm down and listen. Stealing is wrong. Lying is wrong. Fighting is wrong. You both need to learn to respect each other and each other's things. You both need to apologize and make up. You both need to be honest and kind. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They said sorry to their mom and hugged. They picked up the diary and the key and the cars and the books. They cleaned up their rooms and their faces. They promised to be honest and kind. They learned their lesson.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, their mom gave them a big bowl of cream to share. She said, "This is a special treat for you. Be nice and share it with each other."

Lily and Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, mom!" They took two spoons and dipped them in the cream. It was sweet and smooth and yummy. They both enjoyed it very much.

But soon, Lily noticed that Ben was eating more cream than her. He was taking big spoonfuls and licking his lips. Lily felt angry and said, "Hey, Ben, that's not fair! You are eating too much cream. You are selfish!"

Ben looked at Lily and said, "No, I'm not. I'm just hungry. You are selfish too. You want all the cream for yourself."

Lily and Ben started to argue and fight. They pulled the bowl and the spoons and the cream spilled on the floor. They both cried and screamed.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and the tears and said, "Oh, no! What have you done? You wasted the cream and made a big mess. You were not nice and did not share. You were both selfish and rude."

Lily and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were wrong. We should have shared the cream and been nice to each other."

Their mom said, "I'm glad you realize that. Sharing is caring. Next time, I hope you will accept what you have and be grateful and kind. Now, help me clean up this mess and then go to your room."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom." They helped their mom clean up the cream and then went to their room. They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, Ben. I love you."

They learned their lesson and never fought over cream again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They had a bow and some arrows that their dad made for them. They liked to pretend they were hunters and shoot at the trees and the birds.

"Look, I hit that big bird!" Ben said, pointing at a crow that flew away. "It was so ugly and loud."

Lily did not like crows. She thought they were mean and scary. She wanted to shoot at something else. She saw a butterfly on a flower. It was very pretty and colorful.

"I want to shoot the butterfly!" Lily said, aiming her arrow.

"No, don't do that!" Ben said, grabbing her arm. "Butterflies are nice and friendly. You can't hurt them."

Lily did not like Ben telling her what to do. She pulled her arm away and shot the arrow. But she missed the butterfly. The arrow flew past the flower and hit a bee.

"Ow!" the bee said, feeling the arrow in its back. "Who did that? That was very rude and mean!"

The bee was very angry. It flew out of the flower and looked for the one who shot it. It saw Lily and Ben with the bow and arrows. It knew they were the ones.

The bee buzzed loudly and flew towards them. It wanted to sting them for hurting it.

Lily and Ben saw the bee coming. They were very scared. They dropped the bow and arrows and ran away.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "The bee is chasing us!"

They ran to their dad, who was sitting on a bench. He saw them running and the bee following them.

"What's wrong?" he asked, getting up.

"The bee! The bee!" Lily and Ben said, hiding behind him.

"Why is the bee angry at you?" he asked.

Lily and Ben did not want to tell him the truth. They did not want to get in trouble.

"We don't know," they said, lying.

The bee flew to their dad and told him what happened. It showed him the arrow in its back.

"They shot me with this!" the bee said, pointing at the arrow. "They were trying to shoot the butterfly, but they missed and hit me. They are very bad and naughty!"

Their dad looked at the bee and the arrow. He looked at Lily and Ben. He knew they were lying. He was very disappointed and angry.

"Is this true?" he asked them.

Lily and Ben looked down. They felt ashamed and sorry. They nodded.

"Yes, it's true," they said, softly.

Their dad took the arrow out of the bee's back. He gave it to the bee and apologized.

"I'm very sorry for what they did," he said. "They should not have shot you or the butterfly. They should not have lied to me. They will say sorry to you and the butterfly, and they will not play with the bow and arrows anymore."

The bee accepted the apology and the arrow. It flew away, feeling better.

"Thank you," it said. "And please, be kind to the animals."

Lily and Ben said sorry to the bee and the butterfly. They felt very bad for what they did. They learned their lesson. They did not play with the bow and arrows anymore. They did not complain. They played with other toys that did not hurt anyone. They were kind to the animals. They were happy.

"Uh-oh, look out, it's a monster!" Tom shouted, dropping his voice. He grabbed the box and tried to run away.

"Stop, Spot, stop!" Lily yelled, waving her sword. She tried to protect Tom and the box.

Spot did not stop. He jumped on Tom and Lily, licking their faces and wagging his tail. He knocked over the box and scattered the shiny things. He picked up a necklace and ran away.

"Hey, that's our gold!" Tom cried, getting up. He chased after Spot, leaving Lily behind.

Lily sighed. She picked up the hat, the scarf, and the sword. She looked at the mess in the garden. She wished Spot did not disturb their game. She wished they could be famous pirates again.

"Hello, sir, what do you want to eat today?" Lila asked Ben.

"I want some shrimp, please," Ben said.

"Shrimp? What is shrimp?" Lila asked.

Ben pointed to a small pink thing in the toy basket. "This is shrimp. It is a small fish that lives in the water. It is yummy."

Lila looked at the shrimp. She was confused. She had never seen a fish like that before. It had a long tail and a hard shell. It did not look yummy to her.

"Are you sure you want shrimp?" Lila asked.

"Yes, I am sure. Please cook it for me," Ben said.

Lila took the shrimp and put it in a toy pot. She pretended to boil some water and add some salt. She did not know how to cook shrimp, but she wanted to make Ben happy.

"Here you go, sir. Your shrimp is ready. Enjoy!" Lila said.

She gave Ben a plate with the shrimp and a fork. Ben smiled and thanked her. He picked up the shrimp and tried to eat it. But he could not. The shrimp was too hard and he could not bite it.

"Ow! This shrimp is not good. It hurts my teeth. How do you eat this?" Ben said.

Lila laughed. She realized that the shrimp was not a real food, but a toy. She had made a mistake.

"Sorry, Ben. This shrimp is not a food. It is a toy. It is for playing, not for eating. Let me give you something else. How about some cake?" Lila said.

Ben nodded. He was hungry and he liked cake. He gave back the shrimp and took the cake. He ate it happily. It was soft and sweet.

Lila and Ben learned something new that day. They learned what shrimp was and that not all toys were foods. They also learned to act and have fun. They were good friends.

One day, Lily was very happy. She had completed the sweater. She ran to her room to put it on Rosie. She thought Rosie would look very pretty and warm in her new sweater. She hugged her doll and said, "I love you, Rosie. I made this sweater just for you."

But when she got to her room, she saw something terrible. Her little brother, Max, was playing with Rosie. He had taken off the sweater and thrown it on the floor. He had drawn on Rosie's face with a marker. He had pulled off one of her arms. He was laughing.

Lily was very angry and sad. She screamed, "Max, you are so mean! You ruined my sweater and my doll! I worked so hard on them! How could you do this?"

Max looked at her and shrugged. He said, "It's just a doll and a sweater. They are not important. They are boring. I wanted to have fun."

But you know what? You did something very important. You made something with love and care. You showed Rosie how much you value her. That is more important than anything else. No one can take that away from you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, grandma. You are right. I still love Rosie, even if she is broken. And I still love my sweater, even if it is dirty. Maybe we can wash it and mend it together."

Her grandma nodded and said, "Of course we can, Lily. And maybe we can also teach Max a lesson. How about we make him a sweater too? A very itchy one."

Lily giggled and said, "Yes, grandma. That would be funny. And maybe he will learn to be nice and respectful."

"Wow, look at that ship!" Tim said. "I wonder what it does and where it goes."

"Let's go and see!" Sam said. "Maybe we can find some treasure or pirates."

They ran to the ship and climbed up a ladder. They saw many people and boxes on the deck. Some people were carrying boxes to the ship, and some were carrying boxes from the ship.

"Hello, boys," a man said. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He had a beard and a smile. "What are you doing here?"

"We are curious about the ship," Tim said. "Can we look around?"

The man nodded. "Sure, but be careful. This is a cargo ship. We carry many things from one place to another. Some things are heavy, some things are fragile, some things are dangerous."

"What kind of things?" Sam asked.

The man pointed to some boxes. "These are books. We carry them to a library. These are toys. We carry them to a store. These are bananas. We carry them to a market."

Tim and Sam looked at the boxes with interest. They saw pictures and words and colors on them.

"Can we help you carry some boxes?" Tim asked.

The man laughed. "You are very kind, but these boxes are too big and heavy for you. You can help me carry this one, though. It is light and small. It is a gift for my son. He is your age."

He handed them a box wrapped in paper and ribbon. It had a tag that said "To Ben, from Dad".

"Thank you, sir," Sam said. "We will be careful."

They carried the box to the other side of the deck, where the man had a car. They put the box in the trunk and closed it.

"Thank you, boys," the man said. "You are very helpful and curious. I hope you enjoy your adventure on the ship. But don't stay too long. The ship will leave soon."

"Bye, sir," Tim and Sam said. "Have a good trip. Say hi to Ben for us."

They waved to the man and ran back to the ladder. They climbed down and ran to their mom, who was waiting for them.

"Wow, that sounds exciting," their mom said. "But you should not go on a ship without asking me first. It could be dangerous. You could get lost or hurt or left behind."

"We are sorry, mom," Sam said. "We were just curious. We wanted to see the ship."

"OK, mom," Tim and Sam said. "We will. Can we see the ship again?"

They put the potato in the water and waited. After a few days, the potato started to sprout! Timmy was so happy that he ran to tell his mom. She was proud of him for figuring out how to make the potato grow. Timmy and his friend continued to water the potato and watch it grow. They learned that sometimes you just need to soak things to make them better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a small village. One day, Lily was playing outside when she saw an elderly woman walking down the street. The woman looked lost and confused.

Lily went up to the woman and asked, "Do you know where you're going?" The woman replied, "No, I'm looking for my pet rat. He ran away and I can't find him."

Lily felt sad for the woman and decided to help her look for the rat. They searched high and low, but they couldn't find him anywhere. Just when they were about to give up, Lily heard a faint squeaking noise. They followed the sound and found the rat hiding behind a bush.

The woman was overjoyed to be reunited with her pet and thanked Lily for her help. Lily felt happy that she could help someone in need. From that day on, Lily and the elderly woman became good friends and would often go on adventures together.

Lily looked at the comb and said, "I don't want to comb my hair. It's scary."

"Why is it scary?" asked her mom.

"Because I dare not to look at myself in the mirror when my hair is all combed," said Lily.

Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. You're beautiful no matter what your hair looks like. But if you ever change your mind, the comb is here for you."

Sally guessed that Max's oil tank was broken. She had a spare one that she gave to Max. Max was very grateful and poured the oil into his engine. Now, Max was able to continue his journey and deliver the oil to the people who needed it.

They asked their mom if they could borrow her phone. She said yes, but only for a little while. She told them to be careful and not to go too far. She was busy making dinner and did not watch them.

Ben and Sam ran outside with the phone. They crossed the street and went to the billboard. They held the phone up and pressed the record button. They said, "Look, mom, we found a red car! It is on the billboard! Do you like it?"

But they did not see the big truck that was coming. The truck driver did not see them either. He was looking at his phone and not at the road. He hit the brakes, but it was too late. The truck crashed into the billboard and the phone. Ben and Sam were hurt and scared. They cried and screamed.

Their mom heard the noise and ran outside. She saw the truck, the billboard, and the phone. She saw Ben and Sam lying on the ground. She was shocked and sad. She called for help and hugged them. She wished they had been more careful and organized. She wished they had stayed inside and played with their toy cars and trucks.

"Let's look inside the bin," Ben said. He lifted the lid and saw paper, cans and bottles. He took out a can and threw it on the ground.

"No, Ben, that is bad," Lily said. "We should put the things back in the bin. The bin keeps the park clean."

Ben did not listen. He took out more things and made a mess. Lily was sad. She did not like the mess.

She saw a man walking a dog. The dog was gentle and friendly. It wagged its tail and licked Lily's hand.

"Thank you, Spot. Thank you, man," Lily said.

Ben felt sorry. He saw that Lily was right. He said sorry to Lily and the man. He helped Lily pick up the rest of the mess. He put the lid back on the bin.

They hugged Spot and thanked the man. They went back to play. They had fun. They did not make a mess again. They were gentle and kind.

Sara and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and find things. Sometimes they found rocks, or shells, or worms. One day, they found something shiny and heavy. It was a piece of iron.

"Look, Sara, what is this?" Ben asked, holding the iron in his hand.

"I don't know, Ben. It is cold and hard. Maybe it is a treasure," Sara said, touching the iron.

"Let's take it to Mom. Maybe she knows what it is," Ben said. He put the iron in his pocket and they ran to the house.

But when they got to the door, they saw a big dog. The dog was barking and growling. It had sharp teeth and angry eyes. It wanted to bite them.

"Help, Sara, help!" Ben cried, scared of the dog.

"Ben, don't worry. I have an idea," Sara said. She took the iron from Ben's pocket and threw it at the dog. The iron hit the dog on the head. The dog yelped and ran away.

"Wow, Sara, you are brave. You saved us," Ben said, hugging Sara.

"Thank you, Ben. You are kind. You shared your treasure with me," Sara said, smiling.

They went inside and showed the iron to Mom. Mom was surprised and proud. She told them the iron was very old and came from a ship that sank long ago. She said they could keep it as a souvenir.

Sara and Ben were happy. They had found a treasure and a friend. They had also learned that iron was cold and hard, but also useful and strong. They put the iron on their shelf and went to play some more.

"Let's get some grapes!" Lily said. "They are good for us!"

"But they are too high!" Ben said. "We can't reach them!"

Lily had an idea. She saw a big rock near the tree. She said, "We can climb on the rock and then jump to the grapes!"

Ben was scared, but he wanted to try. He followed Lily to the rock. They climbed on it and looked at the grapes. They were still high, but not too high.

"Ready?" Lily said. "One, two, three, jump!"

They jumped as hard as they could. They stretched their arms to grab the grapes. But they missed. They fell to the ground and hurt themselves. They cried and cried.

A lady who was walking her dog heard them and came to help. She saw their cuts and bruises and said, "Oh, you poor things! What happened?"

"We wanted grapes!" Lily said. "But they were too high!"

The lady realized what they had done. She said, "Those are not grapes, those are berries! And they are not good for you, they are poisonous! You could have gotten very sick!"

Lily and Ben felt very silly and very sorry. They wished they had listened to Ben and not jumped. They learned a hard lesson that day. They never tried to get grapes from a high tree again.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play at the beach. They had a big bucket and a small shovel to make sand castles. Anna was bossy and always told Ben what to do. She said, "Ben, you provide the sand and I will make the castle. You are too slow and clumsy."

Ben was sad and did not like to be bossy. He wanted to make his own castle and have fun. He said, "Anna, you are not nice. I can make a castle too. Let me use the shovel and the bucket."

Anna did not listen and snatched the shovel and the bucket from Ben. She said, "No, you can't. You will ruin everything. Go away and find something else to play with."

Ben was angry and ran away. He saw a big crab on the shore and picked it up. He thought, "This crab is better than a castle. It can move and pinch. I will show Anna."

He ran back to Anna and threw the crab on her castle. The crab snapped its claws and broke the castle. Anna screamed and dropped the shovel and the bucket. She said, "Ben, you are mean. You broke my castle and scared me. Go away and leave me alone."

Ben felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I was mad because you were bossy. I wanted to play with you and share the shovel and the bucket. Can we be friends again?"

Anna calmed down and said, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I was bossy because I wanted to make a perfect castle. I should have let you help me and play with me. Can we make a new castle together?"

Ben smiled and said, "Yes, we can. Let's provide the sand and make the best castle ever."

They hugged and picked up the shovel and the bucket. They worked together and made a new castle. They also made a hole for the crab and gave it some seaweed. They said, "Thank you, crab, for teaching us a lesson. You can be our friend, too."

They played happily at the beach and learned to share and be nice.

Tom was a small boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a lot of cars, trains, and planes that he zoomed around the floor. He also had a big box of dress-up clothes that he used to pretend he was different people. One day, he found a funny thing in the box. It was a long, black, hairy thing that looked like a snake. He wondered what it was.

He ran to his mom, who was in the kitchen, and showed her the hairy thing. "Mom, what is this?" he asked.

Mom smiled and took the hairy thing from him. "This is a mustache, Tom. It is something that some men have on their faces, like your dad and grandpa. You can put it on your lip and pretend you are a grown-up."

Tom thought that sounded fun. He took the mustache back and stuck it on his lip. He looked in the mirror and laughed. He looked very silly with the mustache. He decided to show his dad, who was in the living room, reading a book.

He ran to his dad and said, "Dad, look at me! I have a mustache like you!"

Dad looked up and saw Tom with the mustache. He was surprised and amused. He said, "Wow, Tom, you look very handsome with that mustache. Where did you get it?"

Tom said, "I found it in the dress-up box. Mom said it is a mustache. Do you like it?"

Dad said, "I do like it, Tom. But you know what? You have to be careful with it. It is not a real mustache, it is a fake one. It is made of glue and hair. If you pull it too hard, it might come off and hurt your lip. Or it might stick to something else and make a mess. So you have to be gentle with it and take it off when you are done playing."

Tom nodded and said, "OK, Dad, I will be careful. Can I play with it for a little while?"

Dad said, "Sure, Tom, you can play with it for a little while. But don't forget to take it off before you go to bed. And don't close your mouth too much, or you might eat some hair."

Tom said, "OK, Dad, I won't close my mouth too much. Thank you for the mustache. I love you."

Dad said, "I love you too, Tom. Have fun with your mustache."

Tom hugged his dad and ran back to his room. He played with his mustache and his toys for a long time. He pretended he was a pilot, a cowboy, a pirate, and a detective. He had a lot of fun with his mustache. But he forgot what his dad said about being careful. He pulled it too hard, and it came off his lip. It hurt a little bit, and he cried. He also closed his mouth too much, and he ate some hair. It tasted bad, and he spit it out. He was sad and sorry. He threw the mustache in the trash and said, "I don't like this mustache anymore. It is not fun. It is ouchy and yucky."

He went to his mom and dad and told them what happened. They hugged him and kissed him and said, "It's OK, Tom. We are not mad at you. We are sorry you got hurt and ate some hair. But we are glad you had fun with your mustache. You are still our handsome boy, with or without a mustache. We love you."

Tom smiled and said, "I love you too, Mom and Dad. I don't need a mustache to be happy. I just need you and my toys."

The end.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big clock on a tower. The clock has two hands and many numbers.

"What is that?" Sam asks.

"That is a clock. It tells the time," Ben says.

"What is time?" Sam asks.

Ben thinks for a moment. He does not know how to explain time to Sam. He says, "Time is when things happen. Like when we eat, or sleep, or play."

Sam nods. He thinks he understands. He says, "Can we play with the clock?"

Ben shakes his head. He says, "No, we cannot. The clock is too high and too big. We can only look at it."

Sam is sad. He wants to play with the clock. He says, "Maybe we can stand on each other's shoulders and reach the clock."

Ben laughs. He says, "That is silly. We are too small and the clock is too high. We will fall and hurt ourselves."

Sam does not listen. He says, "Let's try. You stand first and I will stand on you."

Ben sighs. He does not want to argue with Sam. He says, "Fine. But be careful."

Ben stands on the ground. Sam stands on Ben's shoulders. They are still too far from the clock. Sam says, "We need to stand higher. Let's find something to stand on."

They look around. They see a bench near the tower. They run to the bench. Ben stands on the bench. Sam stands on Ben's shoulders. They are closer to the clock, but still not enough. Sam says, "We need to stand higher. Let's find something else to stand on."

Sam and Ben are scared. They hear people shouting. They look down. They see many people looking at them. They see a man in a blue suit running to them. He looks angry.

"What are you doing?" the man yells. "You are not supposed to touch the clock! You are messing up the time!"

Sam and Ben do not answer. They are too scared and sorry. They wish they never saw the clock. They wish they listened to Ben. They wish they could go back in time.

"I know you like it, but it is not a good choice for today. Look, here is another dress that is also pretty, but modest. It is blue and has small flowers. It matches your eyes. Why don't you try it on?" Mom said, showing her another dress.

Lily looked at the blue dress. She liked the flowers, but she still wanted the pink dress. She did not want to make mom angry, but she did not want to give up her dress. She did not know what to do.

"Mom, can I wear both dresses?" Lily asked, hoping to find a solution.

"Both dresses? How would you do that?" Mom asked, surprised.

"I can wear the blue dress under the pink dress. Then I can have both colors and both flowers. And I can take off the pink dress when I play. Please, mom, can I do that?" Lily said, smiling.

Mom looked at Lily and laughed. She saw that Lily was very creative and clever. She also saw that Lily loved dresses very much. She decided to let Lily have her way.

"Okay, Lily, you can wear both dresses. But you have to promise me that you will take off the pink dress when you play. And you have to be careful not to get it dirty or torn. Do you understand?" Mom said, smiling back.

"Yes, mom, I understand. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever." Lily said, hugging mom.

Mom hugged Lily back and helped her put on both dresses. Lily looked at herself in the mirror and felt very happy. She had the best dress and the best mom in the world. She could not wait to go to the park and show her friends.

"Let's go, Ben!" Anna said. "It will be fun!"

"OK, Anna!" Ben said. "But we have to be careful. The hill is very high and steep."

They put on their shoes and hats and started to climb. They held hands and helped each other. They saw flowers, rocks, and birds on the way. They felt happy and excited.

But when they reached the top, they felt very tired and dizzy. They could not breathe well. They did not know that the air was thin and had less oxygen on the hill.

"Anna, I don't feel good," Ben said. "I want to go back."

"Me too, Ben," Anna said. "But how do we go down? It is too hard and scary."

They looked around and saw a man with a backpack and a stick. He was also climbing the hill. He saw them and came closer.

"Hello, kids," he said. "What are you doing here? This hill is not safe for you. You need special equipment and training to climb it. You could get hurt or sick."

"We are sorry, sir," Anna said. "We just wanted to see what was on top. We did not know it was dangerous."

"It's OK, kids," he said. "But you have to learn to be more careful and listen to your parents. They know what is best for you. Come, I will help you go down. I have some water and snacks in my backpack. You need to drink and eat to feel better."

"Thank you, sir," Ben said. "You are very kind."

The man helped them go down the hill. He gave them water and snacks. He told them stories and jokes. They felt better and safer. They thanked him again and went back to their house.

They told their parents what happened. Their parents were worried and angry at first, but then they hugged them and said they were glad they were OK. They also thanked the man for helping them.

Anna and Ben learned their lesson. They never climbed the hill again without permission and preparation. They also learned to appreciate the oxygen and the safety they had at home. They still liked to play outside, but they were more careful and respectful of nature.

Tom likes to print pictures on his dad's computer. He likes to print pictures of cars, animals and stars. He uses a big machine that makes the pictures on paper. The machine is called a printer. The printer needs a driver to work. The driver is a small thing that tells the printer what to do.

One day, Tom wants to print a picture of a dinosaur. He finds a picture on the computer and clicks on print. But nothing happens. The printer does not make any noise or paper. Tom tries again and again, but still nothing happens. He gets sad and confused.

He calls his dad for help. His dad comes and looks at the computer and the printer. He sees a message on the screen. The message says: "The printer driver is missing. Please install the printer driver." His dad says: "Oh no, the driver is gone. We need to find it and put it back. Otherwise, the printer will not work."

Tom asks: "Where is the driver? Did it run away? Did someone take it?" His dad says: "No, no, the driver is not a person or an animal. It is a file. A file is a thing that the computer keeps inside. Sometimes, the file can get lost or broken. Then we need to get a new file or fix the old file."

Tom says: "How do we get a new file or fix the old file?" His dad says: "We need to go online and download the file. Download means to get something from another computer. Or we need to use a disk or a stick. A disk or a stick is a thing that has files on it. We can put the disk or the stick in the computer and copy the file."

Tom says: "Can we do that now? I want to print my dinosaur." His dad says: "Yes, we can do that now. But first, we need to turn off the computer and the printer. Then we need to find the disk or the stick or go online. It might take some time. Are you patient?" Tom says: "Yes, I am patient. But I hope the driver is not angry with us. I hope it will come back and make the printer work." His dad says: "Don't worry, the driver is not angry with us. It is just a file. It does not have feelings. It will come back and make the printer work. Then you can print your dinosaur and anything else you want." Tom says: "OK, thank you, dad. You are the best." His dad says: "You are welcome, son. You are the best, too." They hug and smile.

Anna said, "No, Tom, that is not right. You have to learn to share and be kind. If you don't, you will have no friends and you will be lonely. You have to say sorry to mom and give back the steak."

Tom realized that Anna was right. He felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. You are a good sister. I will give back the steak and say sorry to mom. I will also try to talk to other kids and make friends. I don't want to be shy and greedy anymore."

Anna smiled and said, "That's good, Tom. I'm proud of you. I will help you make friends and share with you. I love you, brother."

Tom hugged Anna and said, "I love you, too, sister. Thank you for teaching me a lesson."

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring and being kind is better than being greedy and selfish.

As she went up and down on the ferris wheel, she looked down at all the people and animals walking around the fair. It was so much fun! 

At the end of the day, Lily went back home with her jar of candy. She remembered how she had resisted sharing with her brother earlier, and decided to give him some candy after all. She felt happy knowing that she had been kind and fair.

But the wind came again and spread more leaves and garbage. The people were frustrated. They didn't know what to do. Then, they had an idea. They put a big fence around the building to stop the wind from spreading things. The building was safe and clean again. The end.

Suddenly, the boy's ball rolled towards Lily's boots. She picked it up and introduced herself. They started to play together and Lily realized that making new friends wasn't so scary after all. From that day on, Lily wore her shiny red boots to the park every day and made lots of new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to color with her markers. One day, she was coloring a picture of a flower when she noticed that her yellow marker was dull. 

Lily said, "Mommy, my marker is dull. Can I have a new one?" 

Her mommy replied, "No, sweetie. We don't have any more markers. You'll have to use the dull one." 

Lily was sad because she wanted her picture to look pretty. But then she had an idea. She decided to spread the yellow marker all over the flower so it would look like it was supposed to be that color. 

When Lily showed her mommy the picture, her mommy was surprised. "Wow, Lily! You did a great job spreading the yellow marker. The flower looks beautiful!" 

Lily was happy that her mommy liked her picture. She learned that sometimes when things don't go the way we want them to, we can use our creativity to make things better.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play outside with his friends. One day, he started feeling very sick. His tummy hurt and he couldn't eat his food. His owner took him to the veterinarian, who was a kind lady who helped sick animals.

The veterinarian checked Spot's tummy and said, "Spot, you have eaten something that is making you sick. We need to take an X-ray to see what it is." Spot was scared, but he knew the veterinarian was trying to help him.

After the X-ray, the veterinarian said, "Spot, you have eaten a very heavy bone that is starting to rot in your tummy. We need to take it out right away." Spot felt scared, but he knew he needed the bone out of his tummy. The veterinarian took the bone out and Spot felt much better. From that day on, Spot made sure to only eat his dog food and treats from his owner.

Suddenly, they heard a voice from a distant bench. "Excuse me, can you help me?" an old man asked. Lily's mommy went over to see what he needed. The old man had dropped his wallet and couldn't find it. Lily saw the wallet on the ground and picked it up. "Here you go, mister. You dropped your money," she said. Suddenly, an old man appeared in the garden. He was wearing a warm coat and looked very wise. He said to Tom, "Hello, my boy. I have something to teach you. Tom looked out the window and saw that the fog had disappeared and the garden was clean and bright. He smiled and ran outside to play in the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful elephant. He lived in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy bear. He needed a place to rest.

He heard a reply saying, "You can sleep on the shore". The bear nodded and waddled over to the shore.

He found a cozy spot next to the water. He curled up and soon enough he was asleep.

He snored softly in his sleep until the sun began to set. A duck came by and saw him. "What are you doing here, sleepy bear?" the duck asked.

The bear snorted in his sleep and mumbled, "I was looking for a place to sleep".

The duck quacked in agreement and said, "Well, you found the perfect spot".

The bear smiled in his sleep and snuggled further into the sand. The duck swam away, content knowing the bear had finally found rest.

One day Jack took his dog, Sam, to the forest. They were walking through the trees when they heard a loud noise. It sounded like somebody was calling out. "Help me, help me!" 

Jack and Sam ran towards the noise and to their surprise, they found a little 3 year old girl, alone in the forest. She was scared and asked, "Where is my mommy?" 

Jack reassured her, "Don't worry, little one. This is my forest, you're safe now."

He picked the girl up and with the help of Sam, took her home safely. Jack looked after her for the rest of the day. 

The next morning, the girl's parents came and thanked Jack for taking care of their daughter. Jack explained, "This is my forest, I own it and I had to make sure everybody was safe. You can trust me with your little girl whenever she wants to visit." 

The parents thanked Jack and the little girl hugged him before they all left. Jack was proud that he owned a forest and he was also glad to know that he could help others when needed.

Daisy quickly jumped up and ran away. She didn't stop until she made it back home. 

Daisy was so scared that she decided to never go near the rail again.

After a while, they were both tired and happy. Timmy patted Spot on the head and said, "You're a very smart dog, Spot!" Spot wagged his tail and licked Timmy's face. From that day on, they were the best of friends, always playing and having fun together.

The kids smiled and went back to playing near the tall tree. They were happy they could help the little bird. From that day on, the bird always came to sing for Tim and his friend when they played in the park.

From that day on, Jim learned an important lesson. He realized that he shouldn't always rely on others to supply him with what he needs. Sometimes, he needed to take care of himself and be independent.

As they were leaving the store, they saw a boy who didn't have a guitar. Timmy felt sad for him and decided to give him his old guitar. The boy was so happy and thanked Timmy many times. Timmy felt very happy too, knowing that he made someone else happy with his guitar.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Emily. She had a pet turtle named Timmy. Timmy was very slow because he had a hard shell on his back.

One day, Emily wanted to play with Timmy, but he was sleeping in his shell. She said, "Timmy, wake up! Let's play!" Timmy slowly opened his eyes and said, "Hi Emily, what do you want to do?"

Emily said, "Let's play hide and seek. I'll close my eyes and count to ten while you hide." Timmy said, "Okay, I'll hide behind this rock." Emily counted to ten and then looked for Timmy. She found him behind the rock and said, "You're a good hider, Timmy!" Timmy replied, "Thanks, Emily. Let's play again!"

Tim was so excited! He went to his friends to tell them all about the comet. But his friends just laughed at him and told him it must be fake. They said it couldn't really be a comet. 

Tim was very disappointed and started to panic. His mom came to his rescue, calming him down and explaining that even if his friends thought it was fake, that doesn't mean that it was. Tim realized that it's okay to trust your own judgement, even if it doesn't match up with others. 

He was very happy and excited again and decided to keep exploring the world around him. He learned an important lesson that day, that it's okay to trust yourself even when others don't believe in your ideas and opinions.

The moral of the story is: Don't be envious of what others have. Be happy and grateful for what you have.

They turn away from Spot and cross their arms. They are angry and sad. They don't want to play with Spot anymore.

You make me run faster and have more fun. But you're right. Having fun and being friends is more important. You are my friends. I love you."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that being competitive is not bad, but it should not make us forget what is more important: having fun and being friends. It also teaches that we should respect and love others for who they are, not for what they can or cannot do.
