Lily was fearful. She did not like dark and scary places. She wanted to stay in the park with the swings and the slides.

"No, Ben. I don't want to go. It is too high and too old. There might be monsters or ghosts inside. Let's play here instead."

Ben was not fearful. He was curious and brave. He wanted to see what was in the temple. He did not believe in monsters or ghosts.

"Come on, Lily. Don't be a baby. It will be fun. There is nothing to be afraid of. I will protect you."

He took Lily's hand and pulled her towards the temple. Lily tried to resist, but Ben was stronger. She started to cry.

"Ben, stop! Please, stop! I don't want to go. I want to quit. Let me go!"

A man who was walking his dog heard Lily's cry. He ran to see what was wrong. He saw Ben dragging Lily to the temple.

"Hey, kids. What are you doing? This is not a place to play. It is dangerous and forbidden. You could get hurt or lost. Come back to the park with me."

He took Lily and Ben by their hands and led them back to the park. Lily was relieved and grateful. She hugged the man and thanked him. Ben was ashamed and sorry. He apologized to Lily and the man.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. You are not a baby. You are my friend. I won't make you do things you don't want to do again."

"I'm sorry, sir. I was foolish. I should have respected the temple. It is not a toy. It is a special place. I won't go there again."

The man smiled and forgave them. He gave them some cookies and juice. He told them stories about the temple and its history. He taught them to be careful and respectful. He became their friend.

Lily and Ben learned their lesson. They played happily in the park. They never went to the temple again. They were not fearful. They were wise.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play together. One day, they see a big package on the porch. It is wide and heavy. It has a sticker with their names on it.

"Wow, what is it?" Lily asks.

"Maybe it is a toy or a book," Tom says.

They want to open the package, but it is too high for them. They look around for something to stand on. They see a stool and a chair. They have an idea.

"Let's balance on the stool and the chair," Tom says.

"OK, but be careful," Lily says.

They drag the stool and the chair to the porch. They put them next to each other. Tom climbs on the stool and Lily climbs on the chair. They reach for the package.

"Got it!" Tom says.

He pulls the package towards him. But it is too heavy. He loses his balance. He falls off the stool. The package falls with him. Lily falls off the chair. They both land on the ground.

"Ouch!" they say.

They look at the package. It is open. They see a big teddy bear and a big puzzle inside.

"Wow, it is a toy and a book!" Lily says.

They smile. They hug the teddy bear and the puzzle. They forget about their bumps. They are happy. They say thank you to Mom and Dad for the package. They play with their new things. They have fun.

Lily and Sam were twins who liked to draw pictures. They had a grandma who lived far away and they missed her a lot. One day, their mom said, "It is a new season. The leaves are red and yellow and the air is cold. Do you want to mail some pictures to grandma?"

Lily and Sam nodded and ran to get their crayons and paper. They drew trees and pumpkins and apples and birds. They wrote their names and "I love you" on their pictures. They put them in a big envelope and gave it to their mom.

Their mom took them to the small blue mailbox on the corner. She lifted them up so they could see the slot. "Do you want to mail your pictures?" she asked.

Lily and Sam said, "Yes!" and pushed the envelope through the slot. They heard a thud as it landed inside. They clapped and smiled.

"Good job!" their mom said. "Now grandma will get your pictures and she will be very happy. She will mail you a letter back and tell you how much she loves you too."

Lily and Sam hugged their mom and said, "We love you, mom. And we love grandma. And we love the new season."

One day, they decided to go on an adventure. They followed the map to a big tree. Under the tree, they dug a hole and found a shiny box. They opened the box and saw many coins and jewels. They were very happy and shouted "We found the treasure!"

But then, they heard a loud bark. It was Rex, the dog from next door. Rex liked to chase Sam and Lily and make them run away. He saw the shiny box and wanted to play with it. He ran towards them and growled.

"Quick, we have to escape!" Sam said. He grabbed the box and ran to the ship. Lily followed him. Rex was faster and almost caught them. But Sam and Lily jumped into the ship and closed the lid. Rex scratched and barked at the box, but he could not get in.

Sam and Lily hugged each other and looked at their treasure. They felt safe and comfortable in their ship. They smiled and said "We are the best pirates ever!"

"Let's go and touch it!" Ben said. He ran towards the statue.

Anna was afraid. She did not want to touch the lion. She thought it might bite her.

"See? It is not scary. It is fun!" Ben said. He smiled and climbed on the lion's back.

Anna did not like it. She wanted Ben to come back. She looked around and saw a swing. It looked fun and safe.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were spies on a mission. Lily had a pink hat and a pink toy phone. Max had a black cap and a black toy gun. They ran and hid behind the trees and the slides.

"Max, I see the bad guy!" Lily whispered into her phone. "He is wearing a red shirt and a blue hat. He has a big weapon in his hand. It looks like a knife!"

"OK, Lily, I see him too. We have to stop him before he hurts anyone. Follow me!" Max said into his gun. He crawled towards the bad guy, holding his gun in front of him.

Lily followed Max, but she was scared. She did not like the bad guy's weapon. It looked sharp and shiny. She wished they had a real phone to call for help. She wished they were not spies, but just kids.

Suddenly, the bad guy turned around and saw them. He smiled and waved his knife. "Hello, little spies. Do you want to play with me?" he said in a mean voice.

Max and Lily paused. They did not know what to do. They looked at each other and then at the bad guy. They felt a cold shiver in their backs.

"Run!" Max shouted. He grabbed Lily's hand and pulled her away. They ran as fast as they could, leaving their toys behind. They did not stop until they reached the playground gate, where their mom was waiting for them.

"Mom, mom, there was a bad guy in the park! He had a weapon and he wanted to hurt us!" Lily cried, hugging her mom.

"Max, Lily, what are you talking about? Where are your toys?" mom asked, looking worried.

"We left them behind, mom. We had to run. The bad guy was scary!" Max said, panting.

Mom looked at the park and saw a man in a red shirt and a blue hat. He was holding a knife and a pink hat and a black gun. He was laughing and waving them in the air.

"Oh, no, that's not a bad guy. That's Mr. Jones, the clown. He was doing a show for the kids. He was using fake weapons to make jokes. He was not going to hurt anyone. He was just playing!" mom explained.

Max and Lily looked at the man again. They saw that he was wearing a big red nose and big shoes. They saw that the kids were clapping and laughing. They saw that the knife and the gun were made of plastic.

They felt silly and confused. They did not know that the bad guy was a clown. They did not know that the weapons were fake. They did not know that it was a show.

They looked at each other and then at their mom. They smiled and shrugged.

"Oops!" they said.

Tim and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They had fun with their toys and their friends. But there was a problem. There were many mosquitoes in the park. The mosquitoes liked to bite Tim and Mia. They made them itch and hurt.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tim cried. "The mosquitoes are biting me!"

"Me too!" Mia said. "They are mean and bad!"

They ran to their mom. She had a spray. She sprayed them with the spray. She said it would keep the mosquitoes away.

"Thank you, mom!" Tim and Mia said. "Now we can play again!"

They went back to the park. They saw a big ball. They wanted to kick the ball. They took turns to kick the ball. They kicked it hard and far. They laughed and cheered.

But they did not see the mosquito. The mosquito was hiding on the ball. It was angry and hungry. It waited for a chance to bite them.

Tim kicked the ball. The ball flew in the air. The mosquito flew with the ball. It saw Mia. It flew to Mia. It bit Mia on the nose.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Mia cried. "The mosquito bit me!"

She dropped the ball. She held her nose. She ran to her mom. She was crying and bleeding.

Tim saw Mia. He felt sorry and scared. He ran to her too. He wanted to help her.

But he did not see the ball. The ball rolled on the ground. It rolled to the road. It rolled in front of a car.

The car did not see the ball. The car hit the ball. The ball popped. The ball was gone.

Tim and Mia were sad. They lost their ball. They lost their fun. They learned a lesson.

They learned to be careful. They learned to watch out. They learned to stay safe.

Tom and Lily like to jog in the park with their dog Spot. They jog fast and slow, up and down, and have fun. Spot likes to chase the birds and the squirrels, and bark at them.

One day, they meet a rude boy in the park. He has a big bike and a loud horn. He rides his bike very close to Tom and Lily and Spot, and honks his horn very loud. He makes them jump and scare.

"Hey, stop that!" Tom says to the rude boy. "You are not nice. You make us and Spot sad."

The rude boy laughs and says, "I don't care. You are slow and silly. I am fast and cool. My bike is better than your dog."

He rides his bike away, but not before he kicks some dirt at them.

Tom and Lily and Spot are angry and hurt. They feel a pain in their lungs from the dirt and the horn. They want to tell someone what the rude boy did.

They see a nice lady on a bench. She has a book and a hat. She smiles at them.

"Hello, children. What are you doing in the park?" she asks.

"We are jogging with our dog Spot," Lily says. "But a rude boy on a bike was mean to us. He honked his horn and kicked dirt at us. He hurt our lungs and our feelings."

The nice lady frowns and says, "That is not good. That is very rude. He should not do that. He should say sorry and be kind. Do you want some water and a tissue?"

Tom and Lily and Spot nod. They are thirsty and dirty. The nice lady gives them some water and a tissue. They drink and wipe their faces.

"Thank you, nice lady," Tom says. "You are very kind. You make us and Spot happy."

The nice lady hugs them and says, "You are very welcome, children. You are very brave and sweet. You make me happy too."

They smile and hug her back. They feel better in their lungs and their hearts. They say goodbye to the nice lady and jog away with Spot. They hope they will not see the rude boy again. They hope he will learn to be nice.

It was a cold day. Tom and Lily wanted to play outside, but their mom said no. She said it was too icy and they could slip and hurt themselves. Tom and Lily were sad. They looked out the window and saw the snow and the trees.

"Let's play a game," Tom said. "We can pretend we are spies and look for clues."

"OK," Lily said. "How do we play?"

Tom said, "We can peek around the house and find things that are hidden or strange. Then we can guess what they are for."

Lily liked the idea. She followed Tom as he peeked under the sofa, behind the curtains, and in the closet. They found a lot of things, like a ball, a book, and a hat. They made up stories about them.

Sam does not listen. He is curious and hungry. He reaches for the pepper. Mia tries to stop him. But he is too fast. He plucks the pepper and bites it.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing and run on the grass. They saw many animals, like birds, dogs and squirrels. They were having fun.

"Mom, what is that?" Lily asked.

"That is a fire truck, sweetie. It is a vehicle that helps people when there is a fire. The firefighters drive it and use the ladder and the hose to put out the fire. They are very brave and kind," mom explained.

"Why does it make that noise?" Sam asked.

"It makes that noise to let other vehicles and people know that it is coming. It is a way of saying 'please move out of the way, we have an emergency'. It is very important that we listen and follow the noise, so we do not get in the way of the fire truck," mom said.

"Oh, I see. Thank you, mom. Can we wave to the firefighters?" Lily asked.

"Of course, you can. They will appreciate it. They work very hard to keep us safe," mom said.

Lily and Sam smiled. They were not scared anymore. They understood what the fire truck was and why it made that noise. They waved to the firefighters as they passed by. The firefighters waved back and smiled. They were happy to see the children. Lily and Sam felt proud and happy. They learned something new today. They went back to playing in the park with their mom. They had a great day.

Ben and Lily were twins who loved to play on their farm. They liked to run, jump, climb and explore. But their favorite thing to do was to dive into the big pile of hay in the barn. They would pretend they were birds or planes or superheroes.

One day, they decided to have a contest to see who could dive the farthest. They climbed up the ladder to the loft, where the hay was stacked high. They took turns to run and jump and dive into the hay. Ben went first and landed with a thud. He smiled and said, "I dove so far! I bet you can't beat me, Lily!"

Lily went next and ran faster and jumped higher. She flew through the air and dove into the hay. She landed with a soft sound and said, "I dove farther than you, Ben! I win!"

Ben was not happy. He wanted to win. He said, "No, you didn't! You cheated! You jumped from a higher spot!"

Lily said, "No, I didn't! I jumped from the same spot as you! You're just a sore loser!"

They started to argue and yell. They forgot to be careful and quiet. They did not hear the farmer coming into the barn. He was looking for his tools. He heard the noise and climbed up the ladder. He saw Ben and Lily in the hay, still fighting.

He was not pleased. He said, "What are you two doing up here? You know you're not supposed to play in the hay. You could get hurt or make a mess. And you're making so much noise! You're scaring the animals. This is a peaceful farm, not a circus!"

Ben and Lily felt ashamed. They knew they had broken the rules and upset the farmer. They said, "We're sorry, sir. We were just having fun. We won't do it again."

The farmer said, "You better not. Now come down and help me with the chores. And no more diving in the hay. You can play somewhere else."

Ben and Lily nodded and followed the farmer. They learned their lesson. They realized that diving in the hay was not worth fighting over. They decided to be nice to each other and to respect the farm. They still liked to play, but they also liked to help and to be peaceful.

Lily did not listen to Ben. She did not accept his words. She thought he was silly. She threw the lime again and again. She laughed and smiled.

Lily was sad and sorry. She learned her lesson. She realized that Ben was right. She apologized to him and mom. She promised to never play with limes again. She hoped her eyes would get better soon.

They ran to the rock and tried to climb. But the rock was slippery and wet. Tom slipped and fell into the pond. He was wet and cold and miserable.

"Help!" Tom cried. "I don't like it!"

Sue heard Tom and ran to him. She reached out her hand and pulled him out of the pond. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm here."

They walked back to the bench where their mom was sitting. She saw them and said, "Oh, dear. What happened?"

"We climbed on the rock and Tom fell in the pond," Sue said.

Mom took out a towel and dried Tom. She said, "You're very brave, Sue. And you're very lucky, Tom. Next time, be careful with the rock."

Tom and Sue nodded. They said, "We're sorry, Mom."

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay. I love you both. Let's go home and have some hot chocolate."

Tom and Sue felt better. They said, "We love you, Mom."

They held Mom's hand and walked home. They learned a lesson about the rock.

Lila and Sam were outside with their mom and dad. They were looking at the sky. It was dark and full of stars. Mom and dad said there was something special to see tonight.

"What is it?" Lila asked.

"It is a comet," dad said. "A comet is a big ball of ice and dust that goes very fast around the sun. Sometimes we can see it from the earth, like a bright star with a long tail."

"Wow," Sam said. "When will it come?"

"Soon," mom said. "We have to wait and watch. It will only appear for a few minutes."

They waited and watched. They saw the moon and some planes and a satellite. But no comet. Lila and Sam were getting bored and sleepy.

"Maybe it is hiding," Lila said.

"Maybe it is shy," Sam said.

"Maybe it is late," mom said.

"Maybe it is lost," dad said.

They were about to give up and go inside, when they saw something amazing. A bright and colorful light appeared in the sky. It was the comet. It was beautiful. It had a long tail that sparkled like a rainbow. It looked like a magic wand.

"Look, look!" Lila and Sam shouted. "It is the comet! It is here!"

They clapped and cheered. They were so happy and excited. They hugged mom and dad. They thanked them for taking them outside. They wished on the comet. They hoped it would come back someday.

The end.

Ben and Lily were playing pirates in the backyard. They had a big cardboard box for their ship, and a map that Ben drew with crayons. The map showed where they could find gold and other treasures.

"Arr, matey, we need to supply our ship with food and water before we sail away," Ben said, putting on a pirate hat.

"OK, captain, I'll get some apples and juice from the kitchen," Lily said, running inside.

Ben looked at the map again. He was anxious to find the gold. He hoped no one else had found it first. He wondered what he would do with it. Maybe he could buy a real pirate ship, or a big toy castle, or a lot of candy.

Lily came back with a basket of apples and juice boxes. She put them in the box and climbed in.

"Ready to go, captain?" she asked.

"Aye, aye, first mate. Let's set sail!" Ben said, grabbing a stick for a steering wheel.

They pretended to sail across the ocean, facing storms, sharks, and other pirates. They followed the map until they reached a big X.

"We're here, we're here! This is where the gold is!" Ben shouted.

They jumped out of the box and dug in the dirt with their hands. They found a small wooden chest with a lock.

"Wow, look at this! It must be full of gold!" Lily said.

"Let's open it and see!" Ben said.

They tried to break the lock, but it was too hard. They looked around for something to help them.

"Hey, what are you kids doing?" a voice said.

They turned around and saw Mr. Jones, their neighbor. He was holding a shovel and a key.

"This is my chest. I buried it here for safekeeping. It has some old coins and medals from my grandfather. He was a soldier in the war," he said.

Ben and Lily felt embarrassed and sorry. They had dug up his chest and tried to open it.

"We're sorry, Mr. Jones. We didn't know. We were playing pirates and looking for gold," Ben said.

"We thought this was our treasure map," Lily said, showing him the crayon drawing.

Mr. Jones smiled and shook his head.

"I see. Well, you have a lot of imagination, kids. But you shouldn't dig up other people's things. That's not nice," he said.

He opened the chest and showed them the coins and medals. They were shiny and old, but not gold.

"These are very special to me. They remind me of my grandfather and his stories. He was a brave and kind man. He fought for peace and freedom," he said.

He gave them each a coin and a medal.

"Here, you can have these as a souvenir. But don't dig up any more chests, OK?" he said.

"OK, Mr. Jones. Thank you. And we're sorry again," Ben and Lily said.

One day, Amy told Tom that she had to leave. Her dad got a new job in another town. She had to move to a new house and a new school. She was sad and scared.

"Will you come back?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Amy said. "Maybe in a long time. But we can still talk on the phone and send letters."

Amy smiled and gave Tom her favorite doll. "You are my best friend too," she said. "Thank you for the car. I will keep it with me always."

They said goodbye and Amy got in the car with her mom and dad. Tom waved until he could not see the car anymore. He felt sad and lonely.

Amy did not forget Tom either. She called him every week and wrote him letters with drawings and stickers. She told him about her new house and her new school. She made new friends, but she still missed Tom. She told him she loved him too.

Amy was happy to hear from Tom. She said she was glad he saw her on TV. She said she was having fun, but she still missed him. She said he was amazing and famous too.

They laughed and talked for a long time. They realized they were still best friends, even though they were far apart. They promised to see each other soon. They said goodbye and hung up the phone.

They smiled and hugged their car and their doll. They knew they would always be in each other's hearts.

Lily and Tom were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were pirates and explore the sofa, the table and the rug. They had a big cardboard box that they used as a ship. They also had a flag that they made with a stick and a cloth.

One day, they decided to raise their flag on the highest point of the living room. They looked around and saw a chair near the window. They thought it would be a good place to put their flag. They dragged the box and the flag to the chair and climbed on it.

"Look, we are the best pirates in the world!" Tom said, holding the flag. "We can see everything from here!"

Lily nodded and smiled. She liked to play with Tom. But then, she saw something scary outside the window. It was a big dog with sharp teeth and a loud bark. It was running towards their house.

"Tom, Tom, look!" Lily said, pointing at the window. "There is a scary dog! It is coming here!"

Tom turned his head and saw the dog too. He felt afraid. He dropped the flag and tried to get down from the chair. But he slipped and fell. He hit his head on the floor and started to cry.

Lily also got down from the chair. She ran to Tom and hugged him. She was sorry that he got hurt. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. It was a bad idea to raise the flag on the chair. It was too high and dangerous. We should have asked Mom or Dad first."

Tom nodded and wiped his tears. He said, "You're right, Lily. It was a bad idea. We should have been more careful. And we should have been nicer to the dog. Maybe he just wanted to play with us."

Lily and Tom learned their lesson. They never raised their flag on the chair again. They also made friends with the dog. His name was Spot and he was very friendly. They played with him in the backyard and gave him treats. They were happy pirates and they had a lot of fun.

"What have you done?" Mom yelled. "You know you are not allowed to climb on the fireplace! It is dangerous!"

She picked up Lily and took her to the car. She told Tom to stay with Grandma, who lived next door. She drove Lily to the hospital, where the doctor gave her stitches and a bandage.

Lily and Tom learned their lesson. They never climbed on the fireplace again. They were sorry for making Mom sad and scared. They hugged her and said they loved her. Mom forgave them, but she was still sad. She wished they had listened to her.

"Let's go home, Sara. It's too dark and scary here," Tom said.

They looked around, but they could not find the ball. It was gone. Someone had taken it.

"Who took my ball? That's not fair. I liked my ball," Sara said. She started to cry.

"Wow, that car is so cool!" Lily said. "Can I try it too?"

"Sure, after I finish this round," Ben said. He pushed the button again and the car went faster and faster. It reached the top of the loop and then...

Ben and Lily gasped. They looked around, but they could not see the car anywhere. It was gone!

"Where did it go?" Ben asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it went to another place. Maybe it can fly."

They waited for a while, but the car did not come back. They felt sad and confused. They wondered if they would ever see the car again.

"Maybe we should look for it," Ben said. "Maybe it is hiding somewhere."

"OK, let's look," Lily said. They got up and started to search for the car. They looked under the sofa, behind the curtains, in the closet, but they could not find it.

"Hello, I'm back!" the car said. "Did you miss me?"

"You are a magic car!" Ben said.

"You are a fun car!" Lily said.

"Thank you, you are nice kids," the car said. "Do you want to play with me again?"

"Yes, we do!" Ben and Lily said. They picked up the car and hugged it. They decided to keep it as their special toy. They had a lot of fun with the magic car on the large loop.

"Hello, little ones," the giant said in a deep voice. "What are you doing here?"

Tim and Lily were scared and shy. They did not know what to say. They had never seen a giant before.

"We are sorry, Mr. Giant," Lily said in a small voice. "We were just playing and we wanted to see what was on the other side of the hill. We did not mean to bother you."

The giant smiled and put down his book. He did not look angry or mean. He looked kind and friendly.

"You did not bother me at all," he said. "I like visitors. I get lonely sometimes. Do you want to sit with me and talk? I have some cookies and juice for you. They are not too big for you, I promise."

"What does that mean?" Lily asked.

"It means he can't hear anything. He uses his eyes and his hands to talk," Ben said.

Lily and Ben were very hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They saw a big cooler in the park. It had a sign that said "Do not touch".

"Maybe there is food in the cooler," Lily said. "Let's open it and see."

"No, we can't," Ben said. "The sign says no. It is not ours. We have to ask first."

But Lily was too curious. She was clever and fast. She ran to the cooler and opened it. She saw many sandwiches and fruits and drinks. She smiled and took a sandwich.

"Look, Ben, I found food!" she said. "Come and eat with me. It is so good."

Ben was scared. He did not want to eat the food. He knew it was wrong. He saw a man coming to the cooler. He had a hat and a badge. He was a park ranger.

"Hey, you kids, what are you doing?" the man said. "That is my lunch. You can't eat it. That is stealing."

Lily and Ben were shocked. They dropped the sandwich and the fruit. They felt bad and sorry.

"We are sorry, sir," Ben said. "We were hungry and we saw the cooler. We did not know it was yours."

The man was angry, but he was also kind. He saw that they were just little kids. He did not want to be mean.

"It's okay, kids, but you have to learn to respect other people's things," he said. "You can't just take what you want. You have to ask first. And you have to read the signs. They are there for a reason."

He gave them each a small piece of his sandwich and a drink. He told them to go and find their parents. He told them to be good and not to do it again.

Lily and Ben thanked him and ran away. They learned their lesson. They decided to be more careful and polite. They never ate from a stranger's cooler again.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to explore the forest near their home. One evening, they found a big cave with many shiny stones and old bones. They wanted to see more, so they went inside with their flashlight.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said, pointing at a huge skull with long teeth and horns. "It must be a dinosaur!"
